**3.2 `infra/lib/alarms.ts` (new):**
```ts
import { Duration } from 'aws-cdk-lib';
import * as cloudwatch from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-cloudwatch';
import * as actions from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-cloudwatch-actions';
import * as elbv2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-elasticloadbalancingv2';
import * as logs from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-logs';
import * as sns from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-sns';
import * as subs from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-sns-subscriptions';
import type { Construct } from 'constructs';
import type { SanchayEnvName } from './config.js';

/**
 * The worker's `ops.gauges.emit` job (F1, apps/api/src/modules/platform/ops-gauges.job.ts) logs one
 * JSON line a minute: `{"service":"worker",…,"gauges":{...},"msg":"ops.gauges"}`. These names mirror its
 * OPS_GAUGE_KEYS; a rename on either side must change both (each side has a test pinning the list).
 */
export const OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE = 'ops.gauges';
export const OPS_GAUGE_KEYS = [
  'workerHeartbeatAgeSeconds',
  'jobQueueOldestAgeSeconds',
  'reconcilingOverSla',
  'criticalBreaksOpen',
  'webhookSignatureFailures5m',
  'smsSentToday',
  'navBusinessDaysBehind',
] as const;
export type OpsGaugeKey = (typeof OPS_GAUGE_KEYS)[number];

/** OtpService (F1 log lines): one `otp.sent` per delivered code, one `otp.send_failed` per provider failure. */
export const OTP_SENT_MESSAGE = 'otp.sent';
export const OTP_SEND_FAILED_MESSAGE = 'otp.send_failed';

/**
 * R-34: every api-image container writes to the one group, and every pino line carries `service`, the
 * SANCHAY_APP_ROLE of its task definition (Plan 01 B4's logging.ts). Each filter reads one container's
 * lines: the gauges come only from the worker, the OTP counts only from the api.
 */
export const GAUGES_SERVICE = 'worker';
export const OTP_SERVICE = 'api';

/** The lines one metric counts: one container's pino lines with one `msg`. */
export interface AppLines {
  service: string;
  message: string;
}

/** `{ ($.service = "…") && ($.msg = "…") }`: JSON lines only, so the web's plain text never matches. */
export function appLinesPattern(lines: AppLines): logs.IFilterPattern {
  return logs.FilterPattern.all(
    logs.FilterPattern.stringValue('$.service', '=', lines.service),
    logs.FilterPattern.stringValue('$.msg', '=', lines.message),
  );
}

/** Each metric's lines, by metric name: what the filter proof (log-proof.ts) expects each filter to match. */
export const METRIC_LINES: Readonly<Record<string, AppLines>> = {
  ...Object.fromEntries(
    OPS_GAUGE_KEYS.map((key) => [key, { service: GAUGES_SERVICE, message: OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE }]),
  ),
  [OTP_SENT_MESSAGE]: { service: OTP_SERVICE, message: OTP_SENT_MESSAGE },
  [OTP_SEND_FAILED_MESSAGE]: { service: OTP_SERVICE, message: OTP_SEND_FAILED_MESSAGE },
};

/** OTP_POLICY.smsPerIstDay (Plan 01) is 2,000; page at 90 % so there is time to act before logins stop. */
export const SMS_CAP_ALARM_THRESHOLD = 1_800;

/**
 * F1 owns these names (spec §2.4, G-E5). Every alarm is `sanchay-{env}-<suffix>` (R-31: prod is the only
 * stack, so `sanchay-prod-<suffix>`); runbooks and the alarm drill use exactly these.
 */
export const ALARM_SUFFIXES = [
  'alb-5xx',
  'target-unhealthy',
  'worker-heartbeat-stale',
  'job-queue-age',
  'reconciling-sla',
  'money-invariant-breach',
  'webhook-signature-failures',
  'otp-send-failure-rate',
  'sms-cap-reached',
  'nav-age',
] as const;
export type AlarmSuffix = (typeof ALARM_SUFFIXES)[number];

export function alarmName(envName: SanchayEnvName, suffix: AlarmSuffix): string {
  return `sanchay-${envName}-${suffix}`;
}

export interface OpsMetrics {
  gauges: Record<OpsGaugeKey, logs.MetricFilter>;
  otpSent: logs.MetricFilter;
  otpSendFailed: logs.MetricFilter;
  namespace: string;
}

export interface OpsMetricsProps {
  envName: SanchayEnvName;
  logGroup: logs.ILogGroup;
}

/**
 * F1: CloudWatch Logs metric filters on the app log group (E25 `/sanchay/{env}/app`), in namespace
 * `Sanchay/{env}` (`Sanchay/prod`).
 */
export function buildOpsMetrics(scope: Construct, props: OpsMetricsProps): OpsMetrics {
  const namespace = `Sanchay/${props.envName}`;
  const gaugesPattern = appLinesPattern({ service: GAUGES_SERVICE, message: OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE });
  const gauges = Object.fromEntries(
    OPS_GAUGE_KEYS.map((key) => [
      key,
      new logs.MetricFilter(scope, `OpsGauge-${key}`, {
        logGroup: props.logGroup,
        filterPattern: gaugesPattern,
        metricNamespace: namespace,
        metricName: key,
        metricValue: `$.gauges.${key}`,
      }),
    ]),
  ) as Record<OpsGaugeKey, logs.MetricFilter>;
  const counter = (id: string, message: string) =>
    new logs.MetricFilter(scope, id, {
      logGroup: props.logGroup,
      filterPattern: appLinesPattern({ service: OTP_SERVICE, message }),
      metricNamespace: namespace,
      metricName: message,
      metricValue: '1',
      defaultValue: 0,
    });
  return {
    gauges,
    otpSent: counter('OtpSentCount', OTP_SENT_MESSAGE),
    otpSendFailed: counter('OtpSendFailedCount', OTP_SEND_FAILED_MESSAGE),
    namespace,
  };
}

/**
 * R-34: the worker logs every gauge each minute, so a gauge alarm counts a period without a gauge line as
 * breaching. A stopped worker, or a filter that no longer matches (a renamed `service` or `msg`), then
 * pages instead of reading as OK. The count alarms (5xx, unhealthy targets, OTP failures) treat no data
 * as not breaching: no line, no error.
 */
const NO_GAUGES =
  'A period without a gauge line counts as breaching: with worker-heartbeat-stale in ALARM too, the worker stopped logging the gauges.';

/**
 * R-12: NAV missing for a business day after 11:00 IST (construct id `NavAgeAlarm`); buildAlarms
 * wires it to the topic with the other nine.
 */
export function buildNavAgeAlarm(
  scope: Construct,
  envName: SanchayEnvName,
  metrics: OpsMetrics,
): cloudwatch.Alarm {
  return new cloudwatch.Alarm(scope, 'NavAgeAlarm', {
    alarmName: alarmName(envName, 'nav-age'),
    metric: metrics.gauges.navBusinessDaysBehind.metric({
      statistic: 'Maximum',
      period: Duration.hours(1),
    }),
    threshold: 1,
    evaluationPeriods: 1,
    comparisonOperator: cloudwatch.ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO_THRESHOLD,
    treatMissingData: cloudwatch.TreatMissingData.BREACHING,
    alarmDescription: `NAV missing for a business day after 11:00 IST (R-12): the per-scheme STALE grade blocks new purchases and AMOUNT redemptions in the affected schemes only. Verify the AMFI file, then ops:nav-release. ${NO_GAUGES}`,
  });
}

export interface AlarmsProps {
  envName: SanchayEnvName;
  alarmEmails: readonly string[];
  alarmSmsNumbers: readonly string[];
  metrics: OpsMetrics;
  alb: elbv2.ApplicationLoadBalancer;
  apiTargetGroup: elbv2.ApplicationTargetGroup;
  /** buildNavAgeAlarm's alarm; prod wires it to the same topic as the other nine. */
  navAgeAlarm: cloudwatch.Alarm;
}

export interface Alarms {
  topic: sns.Topic;
  alarms: cloudwatch.Alarm[];
}

interface GaugeAlarmSpec {
  id: string;
  suffix: AlarmSuffix;
  key: OpsGaugeKey;
  period: Duration;
  comparison: cloudwatch.ComparisonOperator;
  threshold: number;
  evaluationPeriods: number;
  description: string;
}

const GT = cloudwatch.ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN_THRESHOLD;
const GTE = cloudwatch.ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO_THRESHOLD;

/** Every one treats missing data as breaching (NO_GAUGES above). */
const GAUGE_ALARMS: readonly GaugeAlarmSpec[] = [
  {
    id: 'WorkerHeartbeatStaleAlarm',
    suffix: 'worker-heartbeat-stale',
    key: 'workerHeartbeatAgeSeconds',
    period: Duration.minutes(1),
    comparison: GT,
    threshold: 120,
    evaluationPeriods: 3,
    description:
      'Newest worker heartbeat older than 2 min for 3 min, or the worker stopped emitting gauges.',
  },
  {
    id: 'JobQueueAgeAlarm',
    suffix: 'job-queue-age',
    key: 'jobQueueOldestAgeSeconds',
    period: Duration.minutes(1),
    comparison: GT,
    threshold: 120,
    evaluationPeriods: 2,
    description: `A due pg-boss job has waited more than 2 min, two minutes running. ${NO_GAUGES}`,
  },
  {
    id: 'ReconcilingSlaAlarm',
    suffix: 'reconciling-sla',
    key: 'reconcilingOverSla',
    period: Duration.minutes(5),
    comparison: GT,
    threshold: 0,
    evaluationPeriods: 1,
    description: `An order, plan or mandate has been RECONCILING for more than 2 h. ${NO_GAUGES}`,
  },
  {
    id: 'MoneyInvariantBreachAlarm',
    suffix: 'money-invariant-breach',
    key: 'criticalBreaksOpen',
    period: Duration.minutes(5),
    comparison: GT,
    threshold: 0,
    evaluationPeriods: 1,
    description: `An OPEN CRITICAL recon break: the M1/M3/M4 integrity invariants, SHORTFALL-BREAK, an ambiguous create, an invalid allotment. Runbook: kill switch first. Stays in ALARM until every CRITICAL break is resolved. ${NO_GAUGES}`,
  },
  {
    id: 'WebhookSignatureFailuresAlarm',
    suffix: 'webhook-signature-failures',
    key: 'webhookSignatureFailures5m',
    period: Duration.minutes(5),
    comparison: GT,
    threshold: 3,
    evaluationPeriods: 1,
    description: `More than 3 FP webhooks with an invalid signature in 5 min. ${NO_GAUGES}`,
  },
  {
    id: 'SmsCapReachedAlarm',
    suffix: 'sms-cap-reached',
    key: 'smsSentToday',
    period: Duration.minutes(5),
    comparison: GTE,
    threshold: SMS_CAP_ALARM_THRESHOLD,
    evaluationPeriods: 1,
    description: `SMS OTPs sent since IST midnight reached 1,800, 90 % of the 2,000/day cap; logins stop at the cap. ${NO_GAUGES}`,
  },
];

/**
 * F1 (spec §2.4, G-E5): the prod alarm set, routed to SNS email and SMS for both developers on ALARM
 * and on OK. Nine alarms are built here; the tenth is the NAV-age alarm, wired to the same topic.
 */
export function buildAlarms(scope: Construct, props: AlarmsProps): Alarms {
  const topic = new sns.Topic(scope, 'OpsAlertsTopic', {
    topicName: `sanchay-ops-alerts-${props.envName}`,
    displayName: 'Sanchay ops alerts',
  });
  for (const email of props.alarmEmails) topic.addSubscription(new subs.EmailSubscription(email));
  for (const number of props.alarmSmsNumbers) {
    topic.addSubscription(new subs.SmsSubscription(number));
  }
  const action = new actions.SnsAction(topic);
  const name = (suffix: AlarmSuffix) => alarmName(props.envName, suffix);

  const alarms: cloudwatch.Alarm[] = [
    new cloudwatch.Alarm(scope, 'Alb5xxAlarm', {
      alarmName: name('alb-5xx'),
      alarmDescription: 'More than 10 target 5xx responses in 5 min.',
      metric: props.alb.metrics.httpCodeTarget(elbv2.HttpCodeTarget.TARGET_5XX_COUNT, {
        period: Duration.minutes(5),
        statistic: 'Sum',
      }),
      threshold: 10,
      comparisonOperator: GT,
      evaluationPeriods: 1,
      treatMissingData: cloudwatch.TreatMissingData.NOT_BREACHING,
    }),
    new cloudwatch.Alarm(scope, 'TargetUnhealthyAlarm', {
      alarmName: name('target-unhealthy'),
      alarmDescription: 'An api target failed /api/v1/health for 3 min.',
      metric: props.apiTargetGroup.metrics.unhealthyHostCount({
        period: Duration.minutes(1),
        statistic: 'Maximum',
      }),
      threshold: 0,
      comparisonOperator: GT,
      evaluationPeriods: 3,
      treatMissingData: cloudwatch.TreatMissingData.NOT_BREACHING,
    }),
    ...GAUGE_ALARMS.map(
      (spec) =>
        new cloudwatch.Alarm(scope, spec.id, {
          alarmName: name(spec.suffix),
          alarmDescription: spec.description,
          metric: props.metrics.gauges[spec.key].metric({
            period: spec.period,
            statistic: 'Maximum',
          }),
          threshold: spec.threshold,
          comparisonOperator: spec.comparison,
          evaluationPeriods: spec.evaluationPeriods,
          treatMissingData: cloudwatch.TreatMissingData.BREACHING,
        }),
    ),
    new cloudwatch.Alarm(scope, 'OtpSendFailureRateAlarm', {
      alarmName: name('otp-send-failure-rate'),
      alarmDescription: 'More than 5 % of OTP sends failed in 15 min (with at least 20 attempts).',
      metric: new cloudwatch.MathExpression({
        expression: 'IF((sent + failed) >= 20, 100 * failed / (sent + failed), 0)',
        usingMetrics: {
          sent: props.metrics.otpSent.metric({ statistic: 'Sum' }),
          failed: props.metrics.otpSendFailed.metric({ statistic: 'Sum' }),
        },
        period: Duration.minutes(15),
        label: 'OTP send failure %',
      }),
      threshold: 5,
      comparisonOperator: GT,
      evaluationPeriods: 1,
      treatMissingData: cloudwatch.TreatMissingData.NOT_BREACHING,
    }),
    props.navAgeAlarm,
  ];

  for (const alarm of alarms) {
    alarm.addAlarmAction(action);
    alarm.addOkAction(action);
  }
  return { topic, alarms };
}
```

**3.2a `infra/lib/log-masking.ts` (new, R-34):**
```ts
import * as logs from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-logs';

/**
 * R-34 (F1): CloudWatch Logs data protection on the log groups. A PAN or an Indian mobile number that
 * slips past Plan 01's key-based scrubber (an error message, a provider's response text) is masked
 * wherever the line leaves CloudWatch: the console, `get-log-events`, Logs Insights, metric and
 * subscription filters; only `logs:Unmask` shows it. The shapes follow F21's PII scan.
 *
 * CloudWatch takes at most 10 custom identifiers, names of up to 128 `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` characters, and
 * regexes of up to 200 characters without `(` or `)`, so there is no lookaround. Each pattern therefore
 * consumes one bounding character on either side (or meets the start or end of the line). That keeps it
 * off the 13-digit pino `time`, UUIDs and longer numbers, which matters: metric filters read the masked
 * line, and a masked digit would end the JSON of every gauge line.
 */
function bounded(body: string, before: string, after: string): string {
  const shapes = [`${before}${body}${after}`, `^${body}${after}`, `${before}${body}$`, `^${body}$`];
  return shapes.join('|');
}

export interface PiiIdentifier {
  name: string;
  regex: string;
}

export const PII_IDENTIFIERS: readonly PiiIdentifier[] = [
  // PAN: five letters, four digits, a letter. Any fourth letter (F21's scan wants a holder type).
  { name: 'PanIndia', regex: bounded('[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z]', '[^0-9A-Za-z_]', '[^0-9A-Za-z_]') },
  // A 10-digit mobile starting 6-9, not inside a longer number, a word or a hyphenated id.
  { name: 'MobileIndia', regex: bounded('[6-9][0-9]{9}', '[^0-9A-Za-z_+-]', '[^0-9A-Za-z_-]') },
  // The same with the country code, as MSG91 and FP write it: 91, +91, +91 or +91-.
  {
    name: 'MobileIndiaWithCountryCode',
    regex: bounded('\\+?91[ -]?[6-9][0-9]{9}', '[^0-9A-Za-z_+-]', '[^0-9A-Za-z_-]'),
  },
];

/** The data-protection policy one log group carries: audit and mask PAN and Indian mobile numbers. */
export function piiMaskingPolicy(name: string): logs.DataProtectionPolicy {
  return new logs.DataProtectionPolicy({
    name: `${name}-pii`,
    description: 'R-34: audit and mask PAN and Indian mobile numbers',
    identifiers: PII_IDENTIFIERS.map((id) => new logs.CustomDataIdentifier(id.name, id.regex)),
  });
}
```

**3.2b `infra/lib/log-proof.ts` (new, R-34).** The offline half of the filter proof and the alarm drill; `log-proof.test.ts` covers it without AWS.
```ts
import {
  GAUGES_SERVICE,
  METRIC_LINES,
  OPS_GAUGE_KEYS,
  OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE,
  type OpsGaugeKey,
} from './alarms.js';

/**
 * R-34 (F1): the captured app log lines (written by the api image's real loggers; Vitest pins them in
 * apps/api/src/modules/platform/log-lines.test.ts), relative to the repository root.
 */
export const LOG_FIXTURE = 'apps/api/test/fixtures/app-log-lines.jsonl';
/** The plain text the web container (Next.js 16 standalone) writes; no JSON filter may match it. */
export const WEB_LINES = ['▲ Next.js 16.3.6', '✓ Ready in 162ms'] as const;

export function parseLogLines(text: string): string[] {
  return text.split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => line.trim() !== '');
}

/** A pino line as an object; undefined for a line that is not a JSON object (the web's plain text). */
export function jsonOf(line: string): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
  try {
    const value: unknown = JSON.parse(line);
    return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
      ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)
      : undefined;
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

/** The value a metric filter's `$.a.b` selector reads from a line. */
export function valueAt(line: string, selector: string): unknown {
  let value: unknown = jsonOf(line);
  for (const key of selector.replace(/^\$\./, '').split('.')) {
    value =
      typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
        ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)[key]
        : undefined;
  }
  return value;
}

interface CfnResource {
  Type: string;
  Properties?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

/** One metric filter of the synthesised stack, the lines the proof sends it and the ones it must match. */
export interface FilterCase {
  metricName: string;
  pattern: string;
  metricValue: string;
  /** The fixture lines and WEB_LINES: test-metric-filter takes at most 50 per call. */
  lines: string[];
  /** The lines of the container and `msg` that METRIC_LINES names for this metric. */
  expected: string[];
}

export function filterCases(
  resources: Record<string, CfnResource>,
  fixture: string[],
): FilterCase[] {
  const lines = [...fixture, ...WEB_LINES];
  return Object.values(resources)
    .filter((r) => r.Type === 'AWS::Logs::MetricFilter')
    .map((r) => {
      const [transform] = (r.Properties?.MetricTransformations ?? []) as Array<{
        MetricName: string;
        MetricValue: string;
      }>;
      if (transform === undefined) throw new Error('a metric filter without a transformation');
      const want = METRIC_LINES[transform.MetricName];
      if (want === undefined) throw new Error(`no METRIC_LINES entry for ${transform.MetricName}`);
      return {
        metricName: transform.MetricName,
        pattern: String(r.Properties?.FilterPattern),
        metricValue: transform.MetricValue,
        lines,
        expected: lines.filter((line) => {
          const json = jsonOf(line);
          return json?.service === want.service && json.msg === want.message;
        }),
      };
    });
}

/** What CloudWatch matched that it should not have, and what it missed; empty when the filter is right. */
export function checkMatches(c: FilterCase, matched: readonly string[]): string[] {
  const problems = c.expected
    .filter((line) => !matched.includes(line))
    .map((line) => `missed: ${line}`);
  for (const line of matched) {
    if (!c.expected.includes(line)) problems.push(`matched a line it must refuse: ${line}`);
  }
  if (c.metricValue !== '1') {
    for (const line of c.expected) {
      if (typeof valueAt(line, c.metricValue) !== 'number') {
        problems.push(`${c.metricValue} is not a number in: ${line}`);
      }
    }
  }
  return problems;
}

/** A healthy worker's gauges; each drill raises one past its alarm. */
const HEALTHY: Record<OpsGaugeKey, number> = Object.fromEntries(
  OPS_GAUGE_KEYS.map((key) => [key, key === 'workerHeartbeatAgeSeconds' ? 10 : 0]),
) as Record<OpsGaugeKey, number>;

/**
 * The alarm drill's synthetic gauge lines (R-34, F1): the worker's `ops.gauges` line with one gauge past
 * its alarm, one line a minute for `minutes` minutes up to now. They test the path from the log group to
 * SNS without writing prod data; the SQL behind each gauge is ops-gauges.int.test.ts's.
 */
export const DRILL_GAUGES = {
  'job-queue-age': { key: 'jobQueueOldestAgeSeconds', value: 600, minutes: 3 },
  'reconciling-sla': { key: 'reconcilingOverSla', value: 1, minutes: 1 },
  'money-invariant-breach': { key: 'criticalBreaksOpen', value: 1, minutes: 1 },
  'sms-cap-reached': { key: 'smsSentToday', value: 1800, minutes: 1 },
  'nav-age': { key: 'navBusinessDaysBehind', value: 1, minutes: 1 },
} as const satisfies Record<string, { key: OpsGaugeKey; value: number; minutes: number }>;
export type DrillName = keyof typeof DRILL_GAUGES;

export function isDrillName(name: string): name is DrillName {
  return Object.hasOwn(DRILL_GAUGES, name);
}

export interface LogEvent {
  timestamp: number;
  message: string;
}

const drillLine = (timestamp: number, fields: Record<string, unknown>): string =>
  JSON.stringify({
    level: 30,
    time: timestamp,
    service: GAUGES_SERVICE,
    context: 'AlarmDrill',
    drill: true,
    ...fields,
  });

export function drillEvents(name: DrillName, now: number): LogEvent[] {
  const { key, value, minutes } = DRILL_GAUGES[name];
  return Array.from({ length: minutes }, (_, i) => {
    const timestamp = now - (minutes - 1 - i) * 60_000;
    const gauges = { ...HEALTHY, [key]: value };
    return { timestamp, message: drillLine(timestamp, { gauges, msg: OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE }) };
  });
}

/** The masking drill: Plan 01's test PAN and mobile, which the data-protection policy must hide. */
export const MASK_DRILL_VALUES = ['ABCDE1234F', '9876543210', '+919876543210'] as const;

export function maskDrillEvent(now: number): LogEvent {
  const [pan, mobile, withCode] = MASK_DRILL_VALUES;
  return {
    timestamp: now,
    message: drillLine(now, { msg: `masking drill: pan ${pan}, mobile ${mobile}, ${withCode}` }),
  };
}
```

**3.2c `infra/bin/log-checks.ts` (new, R-34).** The half that needs AWS credentials and the AWS CLI v2: `deploy.yml` runs `prove-filters` before every deploy (3.5), and people run both commands by hand (credential-rotation runbook, "Alarm drill"). Each request reaches the CLI as a JSON file, so no shell quotes a log line.
```ts
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { setTimeout as sleep } from 'node:timers/promises';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { App } from 'aws-cdk-lib';
import { Template } from 'aws-cdk-lib/assertions';
import { loadStackConfig } from '../lib/config.js';
import {
  checkMatches,
  drillEvents,
  filterCases,
  isDrillName,
  LOG_FIXTURE,
  type LogEvent,
  MASK_DRILL_VALUES,
  maskDrillEvent,
  parseLogLines,
} from '../lib/log-proof.js';
import { SanchayMvpStack } from '../lib/sanchay-mvp-stack.js';

/**
 * R-34 (F1), with AWS credentials for the prod account and the AWS CLI v2 (never in PR CI):
 *   prove-filters   replay the captured app log lines through every metric filter of this commit's
 *                   stack with `aws logs test-metric-filter` (deploy.yml runs it before each deploy)
 *   drill <name>    write the alarm drill's synthetic gauge lines (job-queue-age, reconciling-sla,
 *                   money-invariant-breach, sms-cap-reached, nav-age) to /sanchay/prod/app
 *   drill mask      write a fake PAN and mobile there and fail unless they read back masked
 */
const REGION = 'ap-south-1';
const LOG_GROUP = '/sanchay/prod/app';
const repoRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../../..');

/** One AWS CLI call; the request goes through a JSON file, so no shell quotes a log line. */
function aws(command: string[], request: object): unknown {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'sanchay-logs-'));
  const file = path.join(dir, 'request.json');
  try {
    writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(request));
    const args = [...command, '--cli-input-json', `file://${file}`, '--region', REGION];
    const out = execFileSync('aws', [...args, '--output', 'json'], {
      encoding: 'utf8',
      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
    });
    return out.trim() === '' ? {} : JSON.parse(out);
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

/** The metric filters do not depend on the deploy inputs, so the tests' placeholders synthesise them. */
function synthResources() {
  const config = loadStackConfig('prod', {
    SANCHAY_PLATFORM_ARN: 'ARN-000000',
    SANCHAY_SMS_RETRIEVER_HASH: 'FA+9qCX9VSu',
  });
  const stack = new SanchayMvpStack(new App(), 'SanchayMvpStack-prod', {
    env: { account: '111111111111', region: REGION },
    config,
  });
  return Template.fromStack(stack).toJSON().Resources;
}

function proveFilters(): number {
  const fixture = parseLogLines(readFileSync(path.join(repoRoot, LOG_FIXTURE), 'utf8'));
  let failed = 0;
  for (const c of filterCases(synthResources(), fixture)) {
    const result = aws(['logs', 'test-metric-filter'], {
      filterPattern: c.pattern,
      logEventMessages: c.lines,
    }) as { matches?: Array<{ eventMessage?: string }> };
    const matched = (result.matches ?? []).map((m) => m.eventMessage ?? '');
    const problems = checkMatches(c, matched);
    console.log(
      `${problems.length === 0 ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'} ${c.metricName}: ${matched.length} of ${c.lines.length} lines matched ${c.pattern}`,
    );
    for (const problem of problems) console.log(`     ${problem}`);
    if (problems.length > 0) failed += 1;
  }
  console.log(
    failed === 0 ? 'every metric filter matches exactly its lines' : `${failed} filter(s) wrong`,
  );
  return failed === 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

function putDrillEvents(events: LogEvent[]): string {
  const logStreamName = `drill/${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}`;
  try {
    aws(['logs', 'create-log-stream'], { logGroupName: LOG_GROUP, logStreamName });
  } catch (error) {
    const stderr = String((error as { stderr?: unknown }).stderr);
    if (!stderr.includes('ResourceAlreadyExistsException')) throw error;
  }
  aws(['logs', 'put-log-events'], { logGroupName: LOG_GROUP, logStreamName, logEvents: events });
  return logStreamName;
}

async function drill(name: string | undefined): Promise<number> {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (name === 'mask') {
    const event = maskDrillEvent(now);
    const logStreamName = putDrillEvents([event]);
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 10; attempt++) {
      await sleep(3_000);
      const read = aws(['logs', 'get-log-events'], {
        logGroupName: LOG_GROUP,
        logStreamName,
        startTime: now,
        startFromHead: true,
      }) as { events?: Array<{ message?: string }> };
      const line = (read.events ?? [])
        .map((e) => e.message ?? '')
        .find((m) => m.includes('masking drill'));
      if (line === undefined) continue;
      const visible = MASK_DRILL_VALUES.filter((value) => line.includes(value));
      console.log(`read back from ${LOG_GROUP} ${logStreamName}: ${line}`);
      console.log(
        visible.length === 0
          ? 'masked: PAN and mobile numbers are hidden'
          : `NOT MASKED: ${visible.join(', ')}`,
      );
      return visible.length === 0 ? 0 : 1;
    }
    console.log('the masking drill line did not come back within 30 s');
    return 1;
  }
  if (name === undefined || !isDrillName(name)) {
    console.error(
      'usage: drill <job-queue-age|reconciling-sla|money-invariant-breach|sms-cap-reached|nav-age|mask>',
    );
    return 2;
  }
  const events = drillEvents(name, now);
  const logStreamName = putDrillEvents(events);
  console.log(
    `${events.length} drill line(s) for sanchay-prod-${name} in ${LOG_GROUP} ${logStreamName}`,
  );
  return 0;
}

const [command, arg] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (command === 'prove-filters') process.exitCode = proveFilters();
else if (command === 'drill') process.exitCode = await drill(arg);
else {
  console.error('usage: log-checks.js prove-filters | drill <name>');
  process.exitCode = 2;
}
```

**3.7 `apps/api/src/db/db-logins.ts` (new):**
```ts
import { createHash, createHmac, pbkdf2Sync, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { pgErrorCodeOf } from '../modules/platform/pg-errors.js';
import type { Database, DbExecutor } from './client.js';

/**
 * D6 (F1): the two LOGIN roles the deployed containers and people use. Neither owns an object: the RDS
 * master (sanchay_master) runs the migrations, owns schema app and every table, and is used only by the
 * migrate task, which calls ensureDbLogins after runMigrations. The NOLOGIN roles they join come from
 * 0000_bootstrap: sanchay_app holds the DML grants (0003 and later), sanchay_readonly the ops views (F7).
 */
export const DB_LOGINS = {
  app: { login: 'sanchay_app_login', memberOf: 'sanchay_app' },
  readonly: { login: 'sanchay_readonly_login', memberOf: 'sanchay_readonly' },
} as const;
export type DbLoginKey = keyof typeof DB_LOGINS;
export type DbLoginPasswords = Readonly<Record<DbLoginKey, string>>;

/**
 * The CDK stack generates 40 letters and digits (sanchay/{env}/db-app, db-readonly); docker-entrypoint.sh
 * puts the app password into DATABASE_URL unescaped, so nothing else is accepted.
 */
const PASSWORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9]{32,128}$/;
const SCRAM_ITERATIONS = 4096;

export class DbLoginError extends Error {
  override name = 'DbLoginError';
}

/**
 * PostgreSQL's SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier (RFC 5802/7677, the form pg_authid stores). ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD
 * keeps a value in this form as it is, so the plaintext never reaches the server, its logs or an error
 * message. The password is ASCII letters and digits, which SASLprep leaves unchanged.
 */
export function scramSha256Verifier(password: string, salt: Buffer = randomBytes(16)): string {
  const salted = pbkdf2Sync(password, salt, SCRAM_ITERATIONS, 32, 'sha256');
  const clientKey = createHmac('sha256', salted).update('Client Key').digest();
  const storedKey = createHash('sha256').update(clientKey).digest();
  const serverKey = createHmac('sha256', salted).update('Server Key').digest();
  return `SCRAM-SHA-256$${SCRAM_ITERATIONS}:${salt.toString('base64')}$${storedKey.toString('base64')}:${serverKey.toString('base64')}`;
}

/** Runs one role statement; a failure is rethrown without the statement text (it holds the verifier). */
async function roleStatement(
  exec: DbExecutor,
  login: string,
  what: string,
  text: string,
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await exec.execute(sql.raw(text));
  } catch (error) {
    throw new DbLoginError(
      `${login}: ${what} failed (SQLSTATE ${pgErrorCodeOf(error) ?? 'unknown'})`,
    );
  }
}

interface LoginShape extends Record<string, unknown> {
  can_login: boolean;
  superuser: boolean;
  create_role: boolean;
  create_db: boolean;
  replication: boolean;
  bypass_rls: boolean;
  inherit: boolean;
  member_of: string[];
  member_ok: boolean | null;
}

/** Fail closed: a login that could run DDL, bypass RLS or reach another role's grants is refused. */
async function assertLoginShape(exec: DbExecutor, login: string, memberOf: string): Promise<void> {
  const { rows } = await exec.execute<LoginShape>(sql`
    SELECT r.rolcanlogin AS can_login, r.rolsuper AS superuser, r.rolcreaterole AS create_role,
           r.rolcreatedb AS create_db, r.rolreplication AS replication, r.rolbypassrls AS bypass_rls,
           r.rolinherit AS inherit,
           coalesce(array_agg(DISTINCT g.rolname::text) FILTER (WHERE g.rolname IS NOT NULL), '{}'::text[])
             AS member_of,
           bool_or(g.rolname = ${memberOf} AND m.inherit_option AND m.set_option) AS member_ok
      FROM pg_roles r
      LEFT JOIN pg_auth_members m ON m.member = r.oid
      LEFT JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid
     WHERE r.rolname = ${login}
     GROUP BY r.oid, r.rolcanlogin, r.rolsuper, r.rolcreaterole, r.rolcreatedb, r.rolreplication,
              r.rolbypassrls, r.rolinherit`);
  const row = rows[0];
  const problems: string[] = [];
  if (row === undefined) problems.push('does not exist');
  else {
    if (!row.can_login) problems.push('cannot log in');
    if (row.superuser || row.create_role || row.create_db || row.replication || row.bypass_rls) {
      problems.push('has SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, REPLICATION or BYPASSRLS');
    }
    if (!row.inherit) problems.push('does not inherit');
    if (row.member_ok !== true) problems.push(`is not a member of ${memberOf} WITH INHERIT, SET`);
    const others = row.member_of.filter((r) => r !== memberOf);
    if (others.length > 0) problems.push(`is also a member of ${others.join(', ')}`);
  }
  if (problems.length > 0) throw new DbLoginError(`${login} ${problems.join('; ')}`);
}

/**
 * D6 (F1): creates or updates the two LOGIN roles in one transaction, as the role that created
 * sanchay_app and sanchay_readonly (the RDS master; PostgreSQL 16+ gave it ADMIN OPTION on both).
 * Idempotent: every run sets the passwords from the current secrets, so a rotation is "new secret
 * version, run the migrate task, restart the tasks" (docs/runbooks/credential-rotation.md).
 */
export async function ensureDbLogins(db: Database, passwords: DbLoginPasswords): Promise<string[]> {
  for (const key of Object.keys(DB_LOGINS) as DbLoginKey[]) {
    if (!PASSWORD.test(passwords[key])) {
      throw new DbLoginError(
        `${DB_LOGINS[key].login}: the password must be 32-128 letters and digits`,
      );
    }
  }
  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    for (const key of Object.keys(DB_LOGINS) as DbLoginKey[]) {
      const { login, memberOf } = DB_LOGINS[key];
      const { rows } = await tx.execute(sql`SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = ${login}`);
      if (rows.length === 0)
        await roleStatement(tx, login, 'CREATE ROLE', `CREATE ROLE ${login} LOGIN`);
      await roleStatement(
        tx,
        login,
        'ALTER ROLE',
        `ALTER ROLE ${login} WITH LOGIN INHERIT NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE PASSWORD '${scramSha256Verifier(passwords[key])}'`,
      );
      await roleStatement(
        tx,
        login,
        'GRANT',
        `GRANT ${memberOf} TO ${login} WITH INHERIT TRUE, SET TRUE`,
      );
      if (key === 'readonly') {
        // People query prod through this login (SSM, spec §2.4): never a write, never a runaway query.
        await roleStatement(
          tx,
          login,
          'ALTER ROLE SET',
          `ALTER ROLE ${login} SET default_transaction_read_only = on`,
        );
        await roleStatement(
          tx,
          login,
          'ALTER ROLE SET',
          `ALTER ROLE ${login} SET statement_timeout = '60s'`,
        );
      }
      await assertLoginShape(tx, login, memberOf);
    }
  });
  return Object.values(DB_LOGINS).map((l) => l.login);
}
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-legal-seed.ts` (E3's file; replace the whole file). E3's front matter, sha256 and upsert are kept. The function is exported, the CLI runs behind a main guard, `docs/legal/documents` resolves four directories up from `cli/` (E3's five reached `/docs/legal/documents`, outside the repo), and the text of a version that is no longer DRAFT is frozen:
```ts
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readdir, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { isOneOf, LEGAL_DOCUMENT_KEYS, type LegalDocumentKey } from '@sanchay/domain';
import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { loadDotEnvFile } from '../config/dotenv.js';
import { parseEnv } from '../config/env.js';
import { createDb, type Database } from '../db/client.js';
import {
  LEGAL_DOCUMENT_STATUSES,
  type LegalDocumentStatus,
  legalDocuments,
} from '../modules/legal-consent/legal-consent.schema.js';
import { newId } from '../modules/platform/ids.js';

/** docs/legal/documents: apps/api/{src,dist}/cli -> the repo root (/repo in the api image). */
export const LEGAL_DOCUMENTS_DIR = fileURLToPath(
  new URL('../../../../docs/legal/documents', import.meta.url),
);

export class LegalSeedError extends Error {
  override name = 'LegalSeedError';
}

interface LegalDocumentFile {
  file: string;
  key: LegalDocumentKey;
  version: string;
  status: LegalDocumentStatus;
  effectiveFrom: Date | null;
  markdown: string;
  sha256: Buffer;
}

/** E3's front matter: `key: TNC`, `version: '1'`, `status: DRAFT|PUBLISHED`, `effective_from`. */
function parseLegalDocument(file: string, raw: string): LegalDocumentFile {
  const match = /^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n([\s\S]*)$/.exec(raw);
  if (match === null) throw new LegalSeedError(`${file}: missing front matter`);
  const [, head = '', body = ''] = match;
  const meta: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const line of head.split('\n')) {
    const [name, ...rest] = line.split(':');
    if (name === undefined || rest.length === 0) continue;
    meta[name.trim()] = rest
      .join(':')
      .trim()
      .replace(/^'(.*)'$/, '$1');
  }
  const { key, version, status = 'DRAFT', effective_from: effectiveFrom } = meta;
  if (!isOneOf(LEGAL_DOCUMENT_KEYS, key) || !isOneOf(LEGAL_DOCUMENT_STATUSES, status) || !version) {
    throw new LegalSeedError(
      `${file}: front matter needs a known key, a version and a known status`,
    );
  }
  const markdown = body.trim();
  return {
    file,
    key,
    version,
    status,
    effectiveFrom: effectiveFrom === undefined ? null : new Date(effectiveFrom),
    markdown,
    sha256: createHash('sha256').update(markdown, 'utf8').digest(),
  };
}

/**
 * E3's upsert, exported for the migrate task (F1, FR-3), which runs it on every deploy. Every file
 * is parsed before the one transaction starts. A DRAFT row takes the file's text and status (G-C1
 * publishes by flipping `status`). A version that is no longer DRAFT keeps its text, because
 * consents cite its sha256 (sanchay.consent.v2): a changed file for it is refused, nothing is
 * written, and the change must be published as a new version.
 */
export async function seedLegalDocumentFiles(
  db: Database,
  dir: string = LEGAL_DOCUMENTS_DIR,
): Promise<number> {
  const names = (await readdir(dir)).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.md')).sort();
  const docs: LegalDocumentFile[] = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    docs.push(parseLegalDocument(name, await readFile(path.join(dir, name), 'utf8')));
  }
  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    for (const doc of docs) {
      const [existing] = await tx
        .select({ status: legalDocuments.status, sha256: legalDocuments.sha256 })
        .from(legalDocuments)
        .where(and(eq(legalDocuments.key, doc.key), eq(legalDocuments.version, doc.version)));
      if (
        existing !== undefined &&
        existing.status !== 'DRAFT' &&
        !existing.sha256.equals(doc.sha256)
      ) {
        throw new LegalSeedError(
          `${doc.file}: ${doc.key} version ${doc.version} is ${existing.status} and consents cite its sha256; publish the changed text as a new version`,
        );
      }
      await tx
        .insert(legalDocuments)
        .values({
          id: newId('legal_documents'),
          createdBy: 'ops:legal:seed',
          updatedBy: 'ops:legal:seed',
          key: doc.key,
          version: doc.version,
          bodyMarkdown: doc.markdown,
          sha256: doc.sha256,
          status: doc.status,
          effectiveFrom: doc.effectiveFrom,
        })
        .onConflictDoUpdate({
          target: [legalDocuments.key, legalDocuments.version],
          set: {
            bodyMarkdown: doc.markdown,
            sha256: doc.sha256,
            status: doc.status,
            effectiveFrom: doc.effectiveFrom, // Plan 03 RV-03-29
          },
        });
    }
  });
  return docs.length;
}

// `pnpm ops:legal:seed` (RV-02-24's main guard: file URLs compare equal on Windows too).
const entry = process.argv[1];
if (entry !== undefined && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(entry).href) {
  loadDotEnvFile();
  const env = parseEnv(process.env);
  const dbh = createDb(env.DATABASE_URL, 1);
  try {
    const upserted = await seedLegalDocumentFiles(dbh.db);
    console.log(`ops:legal:seed: upserted ${upserted} legal_documents rows`);
  } finally {
    await dbh.close();
  }
}
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-ref-seed.ts` (E6's file with E7's IFSC pass; replace the whole file). The two upserts are kept; `ref_pincodes` and `ref_ifsc` have `stdColumns()` only, so the rows carry no `createdBy`/`updatedBy`:
```ts
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { loadDotEnvFile } from '../config/dotenv.js';
import { parseEnv } from '../config/env.js';
import { createDb, type Database } from '../db/client.js';
import { refIfsc, refPincodes } from '../modules/onboarding/ref.schema.js';
import { newId } from '../modules/platform/ids.js';

/** data/: apps/api/{src,dist}/cli -> the repo root (/repo in the image), as DEFAULT_DATA_DIR (D8). */
export const REF_DATA_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../data', import.meta.url));

function parseCsv(raw: string): string[][] {
  return raw
    .trim()
    .split('\n')
    .slice(1)
    .map((line) => line.split(',').map((cell) => cell.trim()));
}

/**
 * E6's ref_pincodes pass and E7's ref_ifsc pass, exported for the migrate task (F1, FR-3), which
 * runs them on every deploy. Idempotent upserts keyed on the pincode and the IFSC.
 */
export async function seedRefTables(
  db: Database,
  dataDir: string = REF_DATA_DIR,
): Promise<{ pincodes: number; ifsc: number }> {
  let pincodes = 0;
  const pincodeRows = parseCsv(await readFile(path.join(dataDir, 'ref-pincodes.csv'), 'utf8'));
  for (const [pincode, city, state] of pincodeRows) {
    if (!pincode || !city || !state) continue;
    await db
      .insert(refPincodes)
      .values({ id: newId('ref_pincodes'), pincode, city, state })
      .onConflictDoUpdate({ target: refPincodes.pincode, set: { city, state } });
    pincodes += 1;
  }
  let ifsc = 0;
  const ifscRows = parseCsv(await readFile(path.join(dataDir, 'ref-ifsc.csv'), 'utf8'));
  for (const [code, bankName, branchName] of ifscRows) {
    if (!code || !bankName || !branchName) continue;
    await db
      .insert(refIfsc)
      .values({ id: newId('ref_ifsc'), ifsc: code, bankName, branchName })
      .onConflictDoUpdate({ target: refIfsc.ifsc, set: { bankName, branchName } });
    ifsc += 1;
  }
  return { pincodes, ifsc };
}

// `pnpm ops:ref:seed` (RV-02-24's main guard: file URLs compare equal on Windows too).
const entry = process.argv[1];
if (entry !== undefined && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(entry).href) {
  loadDotEnvFile();
  const env = parseEnv(process.env);
  const dbh = createDb(env.DATABASE_URL, 1);
  try {
    const { pincodes, ifsc } = await seedRefTables(dbh.db);
    console.log(`ops:ref:seed: upserted ${pincodes} ref_pincodes rows`);
    console.log(`ops:ref:seed: upserted ${ifsc} ref_ifsc rows`);
  } finally {
    await dbh.close();
  }
}
```

```ts
import type { Database } from '../db/client.js';
import { DEFAULT_DATA_DIR, seedCatalogueReference } from './ops-catalogue-seed.js';
import { LEGAL_DOCUMENTS_DIR, seedLegalDocumentFiles } from './ops-legal-seed.js';
import { seedRefTables } from './ops-ref-seed.js';
import { seedRiskQuestionnaire } from '../modules/onboarding/risk-profile.service.js';

/** Where the files are: the repo checkout locally, /repo in the api image (apps/api/Dockerfile). */
export interface ReferenceDataDirs {
  legalDocuments: string;
  data: string;
}

export const REFERENCE_DATA_DIRS: ReferenceDataDirs = {
  legalDocuments: LEGAL_DOCUMENTS_DIR,
  data: DEFAULT_DATA_DIR,
};

/**
 * F1 (FR-3): the reference data every deployed database needs, loaded by the migrate task after the
 * D6 logins on every deploy. Each step is an idempotent upsert:
 * - E3's legal documents (docs/legal/documents; a version that is no longer DRAFT keeps its text);
 * - E6/E7's ref_pincodes and ref_ifsc (data/ref-pincodes.csv, data/ref-ifsc.csv);
 * - D8's catalogue reference tables: AMCs, SEBI categories and their aliases, market holidays;
 * - E9's risk questionnaire, DRAFT until its file names the compliance sign-off (R-36).
 * Never the curated scheme list, its fund facts or its commission lines: F19's ops command
 * `ops:catalogue:seed --pilot-list` loads those, with the G-B10 checks.
 */
export async function seedReferenceData(
  db: Database,
  dirs: ReferenceDataDirs = REFERENCE_DATA_DIRS,
): Promise<string> {
  const legal = await seedLegalDocumentFiles(db, dirs.legalDocuments);
  const ref = await seedRefTables(db, dirs.data);
  await seedCatalogueReference(db, dirs.data);
  await seedRiskQuestionnaire(db);
  const counts = `${legal} legal documents, ${ref.pincodes} pincodes, ${ref.ifsc} IFSC codes`;
  return `${counts}, catalogue reference tables`;
}
```

`apps/api/package.json` (key-level; append under `scripts`, D8's pattern):
```json
"ops:legal:seed": "nest build -b swc && node dist/cli/ops-legal-seed.js",
"ops:ref:seed": "nest build -b swc && node dist/cli/ops-ref-seed.js"
```
Root `package.json` (key-level; E3's and E6's two script values become):
```json
"ops:legal:seed": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:legal:seed",
"ops:ref:seed": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:ref:seed"
```

**3.9 `apps/api/src/cli/migrate.ts` (Plan 01 B23; replace the whole file):**
```ts
import { pino } from 'pino';
import { loadDotEnvFile } from '../config/dotenv.js';
import { parseEnv } from '../config/env.js';
import { createDb } from '../db/client.js';
import { ensureDbLogins } from '../db/db-logins.js';
import { runMigrations } from '../db/migrate.js';
import { buildPinoOptions } from '../modules/platform/logging.js';
import { seedReferenceData } from './reference-data.js';

loadDotEnvFile();
const env = parseEnv(process.env);
// R-34: pino JSON lines with the app's options, so in the deployed task each one carries
// service "migrate" (its SANCHAY_APP_ROLE) like every other line in /sanchay/{env}/app.
const log = pino(buildPinoOptions(env));
await runMigrations(env.DATABASE_URL);
log.info('migrations applied');

// F1: the deployed one-off migrate task (SANCHAY_APP_ROLE=migrate, logged in as the RDS master)
// also syncs the D6 logins (boot invariant 14 guarantees both passwords outside local/test) and
// loads the reference data baked into the image (FR-3), on every deploy. A developer's
// `pnpm db:migrate` (role api, the compose superuser) only migrates; locally the
// `pnpm ops:legal:seed`, `ops:ref:seed` and `ops:catalogue:seed` scripts load that data.
if (env.SANCHAY_APP_ROLE === 'migrate') {
  const handle = createDb(env.DATABASE_URL, 1);
  try {
    const app = env.SANCHAY_DB_APP_PASSWORD;
    const readonly = env.SANCHAY_DB_READONLY_PASSWORD;
    if (app !== undefined && readonly !== undefined) {
      const logins = await ensureDbLogins(handle.db, { app, readonly });
      log.info(`db logins synced: ${logins.join(', ')}`);
    }
    log.info(`reference data seeded: ${await seedReferenceData(handle.db)}`);
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}
```

**3.11 `apps/api/src/modules/platform/ops-gauges.job.ts` (new):**
```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { Logger } from 'nestjs-pino';
import { DB, type DbExecutor, type DbHandle } from '../../db/client.js';
import { CLOCK, type Clock } from './clock.js';
import { type Job, JobHandler } from './jobs/job-registry.js';

/** The log line F1's CloudWatch metric filters match (`infra/lib/alarms.ts` OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE). */
export const OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE = 'ops.gauges';

/** Mirrors `infra/lib/alarms.ts` OPS_GAUGE_KEYS; both sides pin this list in a test. */
export const OPS_GAUGE_KEYS = [
  'workerHeartbeatAgeSeconds',
  'jobQueueOldestAgeSeconds',
  'reconcilingOverSla',
  'criticalBreaksOpen',
  'webhookSignatureFailures5m',
  'smsSentToday',
  'navBusinessDaysBehind',
] as const;
export type OpsGaugeKey = (typeof OPS_GAUGE_KEYS)[number];
/** `null` only for the heartbeat age when no worker has ever beaten (the metric filter then emits nothing). */
export type OpsGauges = Record<OpsGaugeKey, number | null>;

/** Reported when no non-quarantined NAV exists at all, so the NAV-age alarm fires rather than stays silent. */
export const NAV_NEVER_SYNCED = 99;

/**
 * One read of every alarm signal (spec §2.4, G-E5). `now` is the job's clock; all windows are relative to it.
 * - heartbeat: seconds since the freshest `worker_heartbeats` row (D2);
 * - queue: seconds the oldest due pg-boss job (`created`/`retry`, not `blocked`, `start_after <= now`) has waited (D2);
 * - RECONCILING SLA: orders, plans and mandates whose latest real transition (from != to, so the
 *   `fp.reconcile.nonfinal.miss` self-events of E20 do not reset the clock) entered RECONCILING over 2 h ago;
 * - CRITICAL breaks still OPEN (D1; M1/M3/M4 from F7, SHORTFALL-BREAK from F4, ambiguous creates from F2);
 * - FP webhooks with an invalid signature in the last 5 min (E1 `inbound_webhook_events`);
 * - SMS OTP rows since IST midnight, the same count OtpService's 2,000/day cap uses (Plan 01);
 * - NAV: business days (Mon-Fri minus `market_holidays`, D8) strictly between the newest non-quarantined
 *   `scheme_navs.nav_date` and (IST now - 11 h); the 07:00 and 10:30 IST syncs (D9) have run by 11:00.
 */
export async function readOpsGauges(exec: DbExecutor, now: Date): Promise<OpsGauges> {
  const result = await exec.execute<OpsGauges>(sql`
    WITH clock AS (
      SELECT ${now}::timestamptz AS now,
             ((${now}::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '11 hours')::date AS nav_as_of,
             date_trunc('day', ${now}::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'
               AS ist_midnight
    ),
    latest_moves AS (
      (SELECT DISTINCT ON (e.order_id) e.to_status, e.occurred_at FROM app.order_events e
        WHERE e.order_id IS NOT NULL AND e.from_status IS DISTINCT FROM e.to_status
        ORDER BY e.order_id, e.occurred_at DESC, e.id DESC)
      UNION ALL
      (SELECT DISTINCT ON (e.plan_id) e.to_status, e.occurred_at FROM app.order_events e
        WHERE e.order_id IS NULL AND e.plan_id IS NOT NULL AND e.from_status IS DISTINCT FROM e.to_status
        ORDER BY e.plan_id, e.occurred_at DESC, e.id DESC)
      UNION ALL
      (SELECT DISTINCT ON (e.mandate_id) e.to_status, e.occurred_at FROM app.order_events e
        WHERE e.order_id IS NULL AND e.plan_id IS NULL AND e.mandate_id IS NOT NULL
          AND e.from_status IS DISTINCT FROM e.to_status
        ORDER BY e.mandate_id, e.occurred_at DESC, e.id DESC)
    ),
    newest_nav AS (SELECT max(n.nav_date) AS d FROM app.scheme_navs n WHERE NOT n.quarantined)
    SELECT
      (SELECT floor(extract(epoch FROM c.now - max(h.last_beat_at)))::int FROM app.worker_heartbeats h)
        AS "workerHeartbeatAgeSeconds",
      (SELECT coalesce(floor(extract(epoch FROM c.now - min(j.start_after)))::int, 0) FROM pgboss.job j
        WHERE j.state IN ('created', 'retry') AND NOT j.blocked AND j.start_after <= c.now)
        AS "jobQueueOldestAgeSeconds",
      (SELECT count(*)::int FROM latest_moves m
        WHERE m.to_status = 'RECONCILING' AND m.occurred_at < c.now - interval '2 hours') AS "reconcilingOverSla",
      (SELECT count(*)::int FROM app.recon_breaks b WHERE b.status = 'OPEN' AND b.severity = 'CRITICAL')
        AS "criticalBreaksOpen",
      (SELECT count(*)::int FROM app.inbound_webhook_events w
        WHERE NOT w.signature_valid AND w.received_at > c.now - interval '5 minutes')
        AS "webhookSignatureFailures5m",
      (SELECT count(*)::int FROM app.otp_codes o WHERE o.channel = 'SMS' AND o.created_at >= c.ist_midnight)
        AS "smsSentToday",
      (SELECT CASE WHEN nn.d IS NULL THEN ${NAV_NEVER_SYNCED} ELSE (
          SELECT count(*)::int FROM generate_series(nn.d + 1, c.nav_as_of - 1, interval '1 day') AS s(day)
          WHERE extract(isodow FROM s.day) < 6
            AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM app.market_holidays mh WHERE mh.holiday_date = s.day::date)
        ) END FROM newest_nav nn) AS "navBusinessDaysBehind"
    FROM clock c
  `);
  const row = result.rows[0];
  if (row === undefined) throw new Error('ops gauges query returned no row');
  return Object.fromEntries(OPS_GAUGE_KEYS.map((key) => [key, row[key] ?? null])) as OpsGauges;
}

/**
 * F1: worker only (pg-boss runs handlers only in the worker role), every minute. Logs one JSON line that
 * CloudWatch Logs metric filters turn into the `Sanchay/{env}` metrics behind the prod alarms. It writes
 * nothing; a failed read throws, pg-boss retries, and the missing datapoint trips the heartbeat alarm.
 */
@Injectable()
@JobHandler('ops.gauges.emit')
export class OpsGaugesJob {
  constructor(
    @Inject(DB) private readonly dbh: DbHandle,
    @Inject(CLOCK) private readonly clock: Clock,
    @Inject(Logger) private readonly logger: Logger,
  ) {}

  async handle(_job: Job<'ops.gauges.emit'>): Promise<void> {
    const gauges = await readOpsGauges(this.dbh.db, this.clock.now());
    // nestjs-pino: the last argument is the context, the one before it the message (`msg`).
    this.logger.log({ gauges }, OPS_GAUGES_MESSAGE, OpsGaugesJob.name);
  }
}
```

Directly above `export function buildPinoOptions(`:
