```ts
describe('ops:payout-ref (two founders; payout.watch credits on the evidence)', () => {
  /** A settled redemption whose payout F5 scheduled (EXPECTED, with its dates). */
  async function payoutExpected(): Promise<string> {
    const own = await seedScheme(t);
    const { folioId } = await settledPurchase(t, investor, own, {
      allottedUnits: '10.000',
      purchasedAmount: '4999.75',
      purchasedPrice: '499.9750',
      allottedNavDate: '2026-10-12',
      folioNumber: `F-PAY-${own.id.slice(-6)}`,
    });
    const exit = await seedRedemption(t, investor, own.id, folioId);
    await t.db.db
      .update(orders)
      .set({
        status: 'SETTLED',
        payoutStatus: 'EXPECTED',
        payoutExpectedOn: '2026-10-14',
        payoutDueBy: '2026-10-15',
      })
      .where(eq(orders.id, exit.id));
    return exit.id;
  }
  const argv = (orderId: string, a1: string, a2: string) => [
    '--order',
    orderId,
    '--ref',
    'SBIN426281234567',
    '--approver1',
    a1,
    '--approver2',
    a2,
  ];

  it('records the reference with two founders and writes no status; payout.watch then credits it', async () => {
    const orderId = await payoutExpected();
    await opsPayoutRef(ctx, argv(orderId, 'f.one', 'f.two'));
    const [after] = await t.db.db.select().from(orders).where(eq(orders.id, orderId));
    expect(after).toMatchObject({
      payoutStatus: 'EXPECTED',
      payoutRef: 'SBIN426281234567',
      payoutUpdatedAt: t.clock.now(),
    });
    expect(await auditFor(orderId, 'OPS_PAYOUT_REF_RECORDED')).toEqual([
      expect.objectContaining({
        actorId: 'f.one',
        data: { approver2: 'f.two', payoutRef: 'SBIN426281234567', status: 'EXPECTED' },
      }),
    ]);
    await t.app.get(PayoutWatchJob).handle(jobOf('payout.watch', {}));
    const [credited] = await t.db.db.select().from(orders).where(eq(orders.id, orderId));
    expect(credited?.payoutStatus).toBe('CREDITED');
  });

  it('refuses one founder twice, an order not awaiting a payout, and a second reference', async () => {
    const orderId = await payoutExpected();
    await expect(opsPayoutRef(ctx, argv(orderId, 'f.one', 'f.one'))).rejects.toThrow(
      /two different founders/,
    );
    const { orderId: purchase } = await seedProcessingPurchase(t, investor, scheme);
    await expect(opsPayoutRef(ctx, argv(purchase, 'f.one', 'f.two'))).rejects.toThrow(
      /not a settled redemption awaiting its payout/,
    );
    await opsPayoutRef(ctx, argv(orderId, 'f.one', 'f.two'));
    await expect(opsPayoutRef(ctx, argv(orderId, 'f.one', 'f.two'))).rejects.toThrow(
      /already has a reference/,
    );
    expect(await auditFor(orderId, 'OPS_PAYOUT_REF_RECORDED')).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});

describe('ops:invite (D7 through the ops runner; a mobile never on the command line, FR-21)', () => {
  const BOM = String.fromCharCode(0xfeff);
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'ops-invite-'));
  const listFile = (name: string, text: string): string => {
    const path = join(dir, name);
    writeFileSync(path, text, 'utf8');
    return path;
  };
  const bidxOf = (mobile: string) => t.app.get(Crypto).blindIndex('mobile', mobile);
  const inviteAudits = () =>
    t.db.db.select().from(auditEvents).where(eq(auditEvents.action, 'PILOT_INVITE_ADDED'));
  /** The deployed source: opsInputsFor's real SigV4 client against fakes of the ECS credential endpoint and SSM. */
  const withSsm = (values: Record<string, string>): OpsContext => ({
    ...ctx,
    inputs: opsInputsFor({
      appEnv: 'test',
      processEnv: {
        AWS_REGION: 'ap-south-1',
        AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI: '/v2/credentials/ops',
      },
      fetch: (async (input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit) => {
        if (String(input).startsWith('http://169.254.170.2/')) {
          return Response.json({
            AccessKeyId: 'ASIATESTONLY',
            SecretAccessKey: 'sanchay_test_only',
            Token: 'sanchay_test_only',
          });
        }
        const { Name } = JSON.parse(String(init?.body)) as { Name: string };
        const value = values[Name];
        return value === undefined
          ? Response.json({ __type: 'ParameterNotFound' }, { status: 400 })
          : Response.json({ Parameter: { Name, Type: 'SecureString', Value: value, Version: 1 } });
      }) as typeof fetch,
      now: () => new Date(),
    }),
  });

  it('invites every mobile of an SSM SecureString in one transaction, prints only last-4 digits and audits each invite', async () => {
    const out = await opsInvite(
      withSsm({ '/sanchay/test/invites/pilot-1': `${BOM}+91 98765 00101\r\n9876500102\r\n\r\n` }),
      [
        '--mobiles-param',
        '/sanchay/test/invites/pilot-1',
        '--by',
        'f.one',
        '--note',
        'pilot-2026-11',
      ],
    );
    const expiresAt = new Date(t.clock.now().getTime() + 30 * DAY);
    expect(out).toBe(
      `ops:invite: invited ******0101, ******0102 (expires ${expiresAt.toISOString()})`,
    );
    for (const mobile of ['9876500101', '9876500102']) {
      const [invite] = await t.db.db
        .select()
        .from(pilotInvites)
        .where(eq(pilotInvites.mobileBidx, bidxOf(mobile)));
      expect(invite).toMatchObject({
        invitedBy: 'f.one',
        note: 'pilot-2026-11',
        usedAt: null,
        expiresAt,
      });
      expect(await auditFor(invite?.id ?? '', 'PILOT_INVITE_ADDED')).toEqual([
        expect.objectContaining({
          actorType: 'ADMIN',
          actorId: 'f.one',
          entityType: 'pilot_invite',
        }),
      ]);
    }
  });

  it('reads --mobiles-file here (SANCHAY_APP_ENV=test); refuses an invited mobile in the list, a malformed line, a mobile on the command line and a missing parameter, writing nothing', async () => {

    const both = await opsInvite(ctx, [

    ]).catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect((both as Error).message).toBe(

        '--by',

      ]),

    await expect(opsInvite(ctx, ['--mobile', '9876500104', '--by', 'f.two'])).rejects.toThrow(

    expect(await t.db.db.select().from(pilotInvites)).toHaveLength(2);

  it('a concurrent invite that commits mid-run (23505) is reported masked, and the run writes nothing', async () => {
    const raced = '9876500107';
    const racing: OpsContext = {
      ...ctx,
      invites: {
        add: async (exec, input) => {
          if (input.mobileBidx.equals(bidxOf(raced))) {
            // Another session commits an invite for this mobile after the run's pre-check.
            await t.db.db.insert(pilotInvites).values({
              mobileBidx: input.mobileBidx,
              invitedBy: 'f.other',
              note: null,
              expiresAt: new Date(t.clock.now().getTime() + DAY),

          }

      '--mobiles-file',

        .select()
        .from(pilotInvites)
        .where(eq(pilotInvites.mobileBidx, bidxOf('9876500106'))),
    ).toEqual([]);
    expect(await inviteAudits()).toHaveLength(audits);
  });

describe('ops:resolve-break (two founders; invariant breaks resolve themselves)', () => {
  async function openBreak(kind: string, entityType: string, entityId: string): Promise<string> {
    await ReconBreaks.open(t.db.db, { kind, entityType, entityId, severity: 'CRITICAL' });
    const [row] = await t.db.db
      .select()
      .from(reconBreaks)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(reconBreaks.kind, kind),
          eq(reconBreaks.entityId, entityId),
          eq(reconBreaks.status, 'OPEN'),
        ),
      );
    if (row === undefined) throw new Error(`no ${kind} break on ${entityId}`);
    return row.id;
  }
  const argv = (id: string, a2 = 'f.two') => [
    '--id',
    id,
    '--note',
    'Cybrilla confirmed a sandbox test object',
    '--approver1',
    'f.one',
    '--approver2',
    a2,
  ];

  it('resolves a handled CRITICAL break with two founders, the note as the audit reason', async () => {
    const id = await openBreak('RECON_FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN', 'mf_purchase', 'mfp_unknown_1');
    await expect(opsResolveBreak(ctx, argv(id, 'f.one'))).rejects.toThrow(/two different founders/);
    expect(await opsResolveBreak(ctx, argv(id))).toBe(
      'ops:resolve-break: RECON_FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN on mf_purchase mfp_unknown_1 is RESOLVED (approved by f.one and f.two)',
    );
    const [row] = await t.db.db.select().from(reconBreaks).where(eq(reconBreaks.id, id));
    expect(row).toMatchObject({ status: 'RESOLVED', resolvedAt: t.clock.now() });
    expect(await auditFor(id, 'OPS_BREAK_RESOLVED')).toEqual([
      expect.objectContaining({
        actorType: 'ADMIN',
        actorId: 'f.one',
        entityType: 'recon_breaks',
        reason: 'Cybrilla confirmed a sandbox test object',
        data: { approver2: 'f.two', outcome: 'RECON_FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN', status: 'CRITICAL' },
      }),
    ]);
    await expect(opsResolveBreak(ctx, argv(id))).rejects.toThrow(/already RESOLVED/);
  });

  it('refuses an invariant break, a mandate break while the mandate is still RECONCILING, and an unknown id', async () => {
    const invariant = await openBreak(
      'INVARIANT_M1_PROVIDER_ID_WITHOUT_CONSENT',
      'orders',
      newId('orders'),
    );
    await expect(opsResolveBreak(ctx, argv(invariant))).rejects.toThrow(/resolves itself/);
    const { mandateId } = await seedPlanRows(t, investor, scheme.id, {
      planStatus: 'MANDATE_SETUP',
      mandateStatus: 'RECONCILING',
    });
    const ambiguous = await openBreak('MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS', 'mandates', mandateId);
    await expect(opsResolveBreak(ctx, argv(ambiguous))).rejects.toThrow(/still RECONCILING/);
    await expect(opsResolveBreak(ctx, argv(newId('orders')))).rejects.toThrow(/no recon break/);
    const open = await t.db.db
      .select({ id: reconBreaks.id })
      .from(reconBreaks)
      .where(eq(reconBreaks.status, 'OPEN'));
    expect(open.map((b) => b.id)).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([invariant, ambiguous]));
  });
});

describe('the ops role (R-16)', () => {
  it('connects as sanchay_app and cannot run DDL', async () => {
    const dbh = createDb(opsDatabaseUrl(t.db.url), 1);
    try {
      await expect(assertOpsPrivileges(dbh.db)).resolves.toEqual({ role: 'sanchay_app' });
      const ddl = await dbh.db
        .execute(sql`CREATE TABLE app.ops_ddl_probe (id int)`)
        .catch((e: unknown) => e);
      expect(pgErrorCodeOf(ddl)).toBe('42501');
      // The role is a startup parameter of the session, so RESET ROLE lands back on sanchay_app.
      await dbh.db.execute(sql`RESET ROLE`);
      const { rows } = await dbh.db.execute<{ role: string }>(sql`SELECT current_user AS role`);
      expect(rows).toEqual([{ role: 'sanchay_app' }]);
    } finally {
      await dbh.close();
    }
  });

  it('refuses a connection that can run DDL', async () => {
    await expect(assertOpsPrivileges(t.db.db)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(OpsPrivilegeError);
  });
});

// Last in the file: runOpsCli boots (and closes) its own application context in this process.
describe('runOpsCli (the main.ts ops branch): exit codes and its own application context', () => {
  const freeze = ['ops:kill-switch', '--off', '--by', 'ops.runner', '--reason', 'runner smoke'];
  const runnerAudits = async () =>
    (await auditFor('orders.enabled', 'OPS_KILL_SWITCH')).filter((r) => r.actorId === 'ops.runner');

  it('exits 2 with the usage for a missing or unknown command, before touching the database', async () => {
    expect(await runOpsCli(t.env, [])).toBe(2);
    expect(await runOpsCli(t.env, ['ops:nope'])).toBe(2);
  });

  it('exits 1 before Nest boots when the pinned role could run DDL', async () => {
    await t.db.db.execute(sql`GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA app TO sanchay_app`);
    try {
      expect(await runOpsCli(t.env, freeze)).toBe(1);
    } finally {
      await t.db.db.execute(sql`REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA app FROM sanchay_app`);
    }
    expect(await runnerAudits()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('runs a command as sanchay_app in an application context built with NEST_APP_OPTIONS (exit 0); a refusal exits 1', async () => {
    expect(await runOpsCli(t.env, freeze.slice(0, -2))).toBe(1); // --reason missing
    expect(await runOpsCli(t.env, freeze)).toBe(0);
    expect(await RuntimeConfig.get(t.db.db, 'orders.enabled')).toBe(false);
    expect(await runnerAudits()).toEqual([
      expect.objectContaining({ actorType: 'ADMIN', reason: 'runner smoke' }),
    ]);
    await t.db.db.delete(appConfig).where(eq(appConfig.key, 'orders.enabled'));
  });
});
```

```ts
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createTestDatabase, type TestDatabase } from './db.js';

let t: TestDatabase;

beforeAll(async () => {
  t = await createTestDatabase();
});
afterAll(async () => {
  await t.drop();
});

const OPS_VIEWS = [
  'v_ops_audit',
  'v_payouts_due',
  'v_pilot_invites_count',
  'v_recon_breaks_open',
  'v_reconciling_orders',
  'v_units_pending',
];

/** Runs one statement as sanchay_readonly inside a rolled-back transaction: its rows, or its SQLSTATE. */
async function asReadonly(
  sqlText: string,
): Promise<{ code?: string | undefined; rows?: unknown[] }> {
  const client = await t.pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    await client.query('SET LOCAL ROLE sanchay_readonly');
    const { rows } = await client.query(sqlText);
    return { rows };
  } catch (e) {
    return { code: (e as { code?: string }).code };
  } finally {
    await client.query('ROLLBACK');
    client.release();
  }
}

      [
        randomUUID(),
        randomBytes(32),
        randomUUID(),
        randomBytes(32),
        randomUUID(),
        randomBytes(32),
        randomUUID(),
        randomBytes(32),
      ],
    );
    expect(
      (await asReadonly('SELECT status, invites FROM app.v_pilot_invites_count ORDER BY status'))
        .rows,
    ).toEqual([
      { status: 'EXPIRED', invites: 1 },

    await t.pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO app.audit_events (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, reason, ip, data) VALUES
         ('ADMIN', 'f.one', 'OPS_KILL_SWITCH', 'app_config', 'orders.enabled', 'drill', '203.0.113.9', '{"outcome":"FROZEN"}'),
```

```ts
import type { Database } from '../db/client.js';
import type { PilotInvites } from '../modules/identity/pilot-invites.service.js';
import type { AuditService } from '../modules/platform/audit.service.js';
import type { Clock } from '../modules/platform/clock.js';
import type { Crypto } from '../modules/platform/crypto.js';
import { UUID_RE } from '../modules/platform/ids.js';
import type { Jobs } from '../modules/platform/jobs/jobs.service.js';
import type { OpsInputs } from './ops-inputs.js';

/**
 * What an ops command may touch (R-16): the database as sanchay_app, the job queue, the audit log, the
 * blind index (never decryption), D7's invite writer and the inputs an operator must never type on a
 * command line. Never FP. `opsContextOf(app)` (ops-runner.ts) builds it from a booted application
 * context, in `runOpsCli` and in tests.
 */
export interface OpsContext {
  db: Database;
  jobs: Pick<Jobs, 'enqueue'>;
  audit: Pick<AuditService, 'record'>;
  clock: Clock;
  crypto: Pick<Crypto, 'blindIndex'>;
  invites: Pick<PilotInvites, 'add'>;
  /** ops:invite's mobiles: an SSM SecureString in a deployed task, a file locally, never argv (FR-21). */
  inputs: OpsInputs;
}

/** Runs one ops command and returns the line printed on success. Refusals throw OpsCliError before any write. */
export type OpsCommand = (ctx: OpsContext, argv: readonly string[]) => Promise<string>;

/** audit_events.action values the ops CLIs write (R-20). ops:invite writes D7's PILOT_INVITE_ADDED. */
export const OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS = {
  OPS_SYNC_REQUESTED: 'OPS_SYNC_REQUESTED',
  OPS_KILL_SWITCH: 'OPS_KILL_SWITCH',
  OPS_SIP_SWITCH: 'OPS_SIP_SWITCH',
  OPS_REFUND_UTR_RECORDED: 'OPS_REFUND_UTR_RECORDED',
  OPS_PAYOUT_REF_RECORDED: 'OPS_PAYOUT_REF_RECORDED',
  OPS_BREAK_RESOLVED: 'OPS_BREAK_RESOLVED',
  /** D9's action name, kept for ops:nav-release. */
  NAV_RELEASE: 'NAV_RELEASE',
} as const;

/** A refused ops command: printed as one line, exit code 1, nothing written. */
export class OpsCliError extends Error {
  override name = 'OpsCliError';
}

export type OpsFlags = ReadonlyMap<string, string | true>;

/** `--name value` and bare `--switch` flags only; anything unknown, repeated or valueless is refused. */
export function parseFlags(
  argv: readonly string[],
  spec: { values?: readonly string[]; switches?: readonly string[] },
): OpsFlags {
  const values = new Set(spec.values ?? []);
  const switches = new Set(spec.switches ?? []);
  const out = new Map<string, string | true>();
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    const raw = argv[i] ?? '';
    if (!raw.startsWith('--')) throw new OpsCliError(`unexpected argument '${raw}'`);
    const name = raw.slice(2);
    if (out.has(name)) throw new OpsCliError(`--${name} is given twice`);
    if (switches.has(name)) {
      out.set(name, true);
      continue;
    }
    if (!values.has(name)) throw new OpsCliError(`unknown flag --${name}`);
    const value = argv[i + 1];
    if (value === undefined || value.startsWith('--') || value.trim() === '') {
      throw new OpsCliError(`--${name} needs a value`);
    }
    out.set(name, value.trim());
    i += 1;
  }
  return out;
}

export function flagValue(flags: OpsFlags, name: string): string {
  const value = flags.get(name);
  if (typeof value !== 'string') throw new OpsCliError(`--${name} is required`);
  return value;
}

export function requireUuid(flags: OpsFlags, name: string): string {
  const value = flagValue(flags, name);
  if (!UUID_RE.test(value)) throw new OpsCliError(`--${name} must be a uuid`);
  return value.toLowerCase();
}

/** Operator handles, never names or emails: they land in audit_events.actor_id, which is not PII-scrubbed. */
const HANDLE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{1,31}$/;

export function requireHandle(flags: OpsFlags, name: string): string {
  const value = flagValue(flags, name);
  if (!HANDLE.test(value)) {
    throw new OpsCliError(
      `--${name} must be an operator handle (a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-'; 2-32 chars)`,
    );
  }
  return value;
}

/** Spec §5: two-founder approval on every money-adjacent CLI. */
export function requireTwoApprovers(flags: OpsFlags): { approver1: string; approver2: string } {
  const approver1 = requireHandle(flags, 'approver1');
  const approver2 = requireHandle(flags, 'approver2');
  if (approver1 === approver2) {
    throw new OpsCliError('--approver1 and --approver2 must be two different founders');
  }
  return { approver1, approver2 };
}
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-db.ts`:
```ts
import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import type { DbExecutor } from '../db/client.js';

/** R-16: every ops CLI runs as this role, which holds DML grants (0003_grants) and no DDL. */
export const OPS_DB_ROLE = 'sanchay_app';

export class OpsPrivilegeError extends Error {
  override name = 'OpsPrivilegeError';
}

/**
 * Pins the session role with the libpq `options` startup parameter (`-c role=sanchay_app`), so every
 * pooled connection (Drizzle, pg-boss, the OTP bookkeeping pool) starts as sanchay_app and even
 * `RESET ROLE` returns to it. Any `options` already in the URL is replaced.
 */
export function opsDatabaseUrl(databaseUrl: string): string {
  const url = new URL(databaseUrl);
  url.searchParams.set('options', `-c role=${OPS_DB_ROLE}`);
  return url.toString();
}

interface PrivilegeRow extends Record<string, unknown> {
  role: string;
  superuser: boolean | null;
  rds_superuser: boolean;
  app_create: boolean;
  public_create: boolean;
  db_create: boolean;
}

/**
 * Fail closed before an ops command runs: the effective role must be sanchay_app and must not be able to
 * run DDL (no superuser, no rds_superuser, no CREATE on the database or on schemas app/public).
 */
export async function assertOpsPrivileges(exec: DbExecutor): Promise<{ role: string }> {
  const { rows } = await exec.execute<PrivilegeRow>(sql`
    SELECT current_user AS role,
           (SELECT rolsuper FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) AS superuser,
           EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM pg_auth_members m
               JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = m.roleid
              WHERE r.rolname = 'rds_superuser'
                AND m.member = (SELECT oid FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user)
           ) AS rds_superuser,
           has_schema_privilege('app', 'CREATE') AS app_create,
           has_schema_privilege('public', 'CREATE') AS public_create,
           has_database_privilege(current_database(), 'CREATE') AS db_create
  `);
  const row = rows[0];
  if (row === undefined) throw new OpsPrivilegeError('R-16: could not read the session role');
  const problems: string[] = [];
  if (row.role !== OPS_DB_ROLE)
    problems.push(`the session role is ${row.role}, not ${OPS_DB_ROLE}`);
  if (row.superuser !== false) problems.push('the role is a superuser');
  if (row.rds_superuser) problems.push('the role is a member of rds_superuser');
  if (row.app_create) problems.push('the role can CREATE in schema app');
  if (row.public_create) problems.push('the role can CREATE in schema public');
  if (row.db_create) problems.push('the role can CREATE in this database');
  if (problems.length > 0) {
    throw new OpsPrivilegeError(`R-16: refusing to run an ops command: ${problems.join('; ')}`);
  }
  return { role: row.role };
}
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-sync.ts`:
```ts
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { inboundWebhookEvents } from '../modules/fp-webhooks/inbound-webhook.schema.js';
import { orders } from '../modules/orders/orders.schema.js';
import { newId } from '../modules/platform/ids.js';
import {
  OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  parseFlags,
  requireHandle,
  requireUuid,
} from './ops-common.js';

/** inbound_webhook_events.event_type of a re-fetch ops requested (not a webhook FP sent). */
export const OPS_SYNC_EVENT_TYPE = 'ops.sync';

/**
 * `pnpm ops:sync --order <id> --by <handle>` (spec §4.6: read and re-fetch only).
 *
 * It never calls FP and never writes a status. For an order FP knows, it records a re-fetch request in
 * `inbound_webhook_events` and enqueues `fp.event.process` for it in the same transaction: the worker
 * then re-fetches the object and applies it through the same idempotent handler a webhook uses (F4's
 * `PurchaseSettlement` for purchases; F5's handler for redemptions). A RECONCILING order has no FP id
 * yet, so it enqueues `fp.reconcile.nonfinal` (LOOKUP-ADOPT) instead.
 */
export const opsSync: OpsCommand = async (ctx, argv) => {
  const flags = parseFlags(argv, { values: ['order', 'by'] });
  const orderId = requireUuid(flags, 'order');
  const by = requireHandle(flags, 'by');
  const [order] = await ctx.db
    .select({
      id: orders.id,
      type: orders.type,
      status: orders.status,
      fpOrderId: orders.fpOrderId,
    })
    .from(orders)
    .where(eq(orders.id, orderId));
  if (order === undefined) throw new OpsCliError(`no order ${orderId}`);

  if (order.status === 'RECONCILING') {
    await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      // Keyless, like the */5 schedule: the queue is stately, so a sweep already queued absorbs this one
      // (enqueue returns null) and two sweeps never run side by side (R-32, RV-04-F7-2).
      await ctx.jobs.enqueue(tx, 'fp.reconcile.nonfinal', {});
      await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
        action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.OPS_SYNC_REQUESTED,
        actorType: 'ADMIN',
        actorId: by,
        entityType: 'orders',
        entityId: order.id,
        data: { outcome: 'fp.reconcile.nonfinal', status: order.status },
      });
    });
    return `ops:sync: order ${order.id} is RECONCILING; enqueued fp.reconcile.nonfinal (LOOKUP-ADOPT). No status was written.`;
  }

  const fpOrderId = order.fpOrderId;
  if (fpOrderId === null) {
    throw new OpsCliError(`order ${order.id} (${order.status}) has no FP object to re-fetch`);
  }
  const objectType = order.type === 'PURCHASE' ? 'mf_purchase' : 'mf_redemption';
  const eventRowId = newId('inbound_webhook_events');
  const requestedAt = ctx.clock.now();
  await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.insert(inboundWebhookEvents).values({
      id: eventRowId,
      provider: 'FP',
      eventId: `ops-sync:${eventRowId}`,
      eventType: OPS_SYNC_EVENT_TYPE,
      objectType,
      objectId: fpOrderId,
      signatureMode: 'NONE',
      signatureValid: true,
      payloadEnc: null,
      payloadSha256: createHash('sha256')
        .update(JSON.stringify({ orderId: order.id, by, requestedAt: requestedAt.toISOString() }))
        .digest(),
      receivedAt: requestedAt,
    });
    await ctx.jobs.enqueue(tx, 'fp.event.process', { eventRowId }, { singletonKey: eventRowId });
    await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
      action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.OPS_SYNC_REQUESTED,
      actorType: 'ADMIN',
      actorId: by,
      entityType: 'orders',
      entityId: order.id,
      data: { outcome: 'fp.event.process', status: order.status },
    });
  });
  return `ops:sync: enqueued fp.event.process for order ${order.id} (${objectType} ${fpOrderId}). No status was written.`;
};
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-kill-switch.ts`:
```ts
import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { appConfig } from '../modules/platform/kernel.schema.js';
import {
  flagValue,
  OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  type OpsContext,
  parseFlags,
  requireHandle,
  requireTwoApprovers,
} from './ops-common.js';

/** One boolean `app_config` switch an ops command flips (D1 RuntimeConfig keys; the row is the value). */
export interface AppConfigSwitch {
  command: string;
  key: 'orders.enabled' | 'plans.sip.enabled';
  action: string;
  offOutcome: string;
  onOutcome: string;
}

/**
 * `<command> --off --by <handle> --reason <text>` turns the flag off with one actor (spec §4.6: the page
 * response is never blocked on a second person). `<command> --on --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b> --reason
 * <text>` turns it back on; resuming money flow is money-adjacent, so it needs two founders (spec §5).
 * Writes app_config and one audit row; nothing else.
 */
export function appConfigSwitch(spec: AppConfigSwitch): OpsCommand {
  return async (ctx, argv) => {
    const flags = parseFlags(argv, {
      values: ['by', 'reason', 'approver1', 'approver2'],
      switches: ['off', 'on'],
    });
    const off = flags.has('off');
    if (off === flags.has('on')) throw new OpsCliError('give exactly one of --off or --on');
    const reason = flagValue(flags, 'reason');
    if (off) {
      if (flags.has('approver1') || flags.has('approver2')) {
        throw new OpsCliError('--off is a single-actor switch: give --by, not approvers');
      }
      const by = requireHandle(flags, 'by');
      await setSwitch(ctx, spec, false, { actorId: by, approver2: null, reason });
      return `${spec.command}: ${spec.key}=false (${spec.offOutcome} by ${by})`;
    }
    if (flags.has('by')) {
      throw new OpsCliError('--on needs --approver1 and --approver2 (two founders), not --by');
    }
    const { approver1, approver2 } = requireTwoApprovers(flags);
    await setSwitch(ctx, spec, true, { actorId: approver1, approver2, reason });
    return `${spec.command}: ${spec.key}=true (${spec.onOutcome} by ${approver1} and ${approver2})`;
  };
}

async function setSwitch(
  ctx: OpsContext,
  spec: AppConfigSwitch,
  enabled: boolean,
  who: { actorId: string; approver2: string | null; reason: string },
): Promise<void> {
  const now = ctx.clock.now();
  await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const [before] = await tx
      .select({ value: appConfig.value })
      .from(appConfig)
      .where(eq(appConfig.key, spec.key))
      .for('update');
    await tx
      .insert(appConfig)
      .values({ key: spec.key, value: enabled, updatedAt: now })
      .onConflictDoUpdate({ target: appConfig.key, set: { value: enabled, updatedAt: now } });
    await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
      action: spec.action,
      actorType: 'ADMIN',
      actorId: who.actorId,
      entityType: 'app_config',
      entityId: spec.key,
      reason: who.reason,
      data: {
        outcome: enabled ? spec.onOutcome : spec.offOutcome,
        status: before === undefined ? 'DEFAULT' : String(before.value),
        ...(who.approver2 === null ? {} : { approver2: who.approver2 }),
      },
    });
  });
}

/**
 * `pnpm ops:kill-switch --off --by <handle> --reason <text>` freezes new orders, purchases and redemptions
 * alike (spec §4.6: the M1/M3/M4 page response). `--on --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b> --reason <text>`
 * resumes them.
 */
export const opsKillSwitch: OpsCommand = appConfigSwitch({
  command: 'ops:kill-switch',
  key: 'orders.enabled',
  action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.OPS_KILL_SWITCH,
  offOutcome: 'FROZEN',
  onOutcome: 'RESUMED',
});
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-refund-utr.ts`:
```ts
import { and, eq, inArray } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { paymentAttempts } from '../modules/payments/payments.schema.js';
import {
  flagValue,
  OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  parseFlags,
  requireTwoApprovers,
  requireUuid,
} from './ops-common.js';

/** NEFT/RTGS/IMPS references are 12 to 22 alphanumerics; a little slack either side, nothing else. */
const UTR = /^[A-Za-z0-9]{6,35}$/;
/** E21 writes IN_PROGRESS on a late failure after SUCCESS; D-MONEY-040 names the same state REFUND_PENDING. */
const REFUND_IN_PROGRESS = ['IN_PROGRESS', 'REFUND_PENDING'];

/**
 * `pnpm ops:refund-utr --order <id> --utr <ref> --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b>` (spec §4.6, D-MONEY-040):
 * records the bank UTR of a refund the AMC confirmed, with two founders. The refund evidence on the
 * payment attempt is the only write; the order's own status is never touched.
 */
export const opsRefundUtr: OpsCommand = async (ctx, argv) => {
  const flags = parseFlags(argv, { values: ['order', 'utr', 'approver1', 'approver2'] });
  const orderId = requireUuid(flags, 'order');
  const utr = flagValue(flags, 'utr');
  if (!UTR.test(utr))
    throw new OpsCliError('--utr must be the bank reference (6-35 letters or digits)');
  const { approver1, approver2 } = requireTwoApprovers(flags);
  const now = ctx.clock.now();
  const attemptId = await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const pending = await tx
      .select({ id: paymentAttempts.id, refundStatus: paymentAttempts.refundStatus })
      .from(paymentAttempts)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(paymentAttempts.orderId, orderId),
          inArray(paymentAttempts.refundStatus, REFUND_IN_PROGRESS),
        ),
      )
      .for('update');
    const [attempt, ...more] = pending;
    if (attempt === undefined) throw new OpsCliError(`order ${orderId} has no refund in progress`);
    if (more.length > 0) {
      throw new OpsCliError(
        `order ${orderId} has ${pending.length} refunds in progress; record them by hand`,
      );
    }
    await tx
      .update(paymentAttempts)
      .set({ refundStatus: 'REFUNDED', refundRef: utr, refundRecordedAt: now })
      .where(eq(paymentAttempts.id, attempt.id));
    await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
      action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.OPS_REFUND_UTR_RECORDED,
      actorType: 'ADMIN',
      actorId: approver1,
      entityType: 'payment_attempts',
      entityId: attempt.id,
      data: { approver2, refundRef: utr, status: 'REFUNDED', outcome: attempt.refundStatus ?? '' },
    });
    return attempt.id;
  });
  return `ops:refund-utr: payment attempt ${attemptId} of order ${orderId} is REFUNDED with UTR ${utr} (approved by ${approver1} and ${approver2})`;
};
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-payout-ref.ts`:
```ts
import { and, eq, inArray, isNull } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { orders } from '../modules/orders/orders.schema.js';
import {
  flagValue,
  OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  parseFlags,
  requireTwoApprovers,
  requireUuid,
} from './ops-common.js';

/** A bank credit reference (UTR) is 12 to 22 alphanumerics; a little slack either side, nothing else. */
const BANK_REF = /^[A-Za-z0-9]{6,35}$/;

/**
 * `pnpm ops:payout-ref --order <id> --ref <bank credit ref> --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b>` (spec §4.4
 * payout row, D-MONEY-053): records the investor's bank credit reference for a redemption payout, with
 * two founders. It writes the evidence only; F5's `payout.watch` sees `payout_ref` on its next run and
 * moves the payout to CREDITED, so this command never writes a status.
 */
export const opsPayoutRef: OpsCommand = async (ctx, argv) => {
  const flags = parseFlags(argv, { values: ['order', 'ref', 'approver1', 'approver2'] });
  const orderId = requireUuid(flags, 'order');
  const ref = flagValue(flags, 'ref');
  if (!BANK_REF.test(ref))
    throw new OpsCliError('--ref must be the bank credit reference (6-35 letters or digits)');
  const { approver1, approver2 } = requireTwoApprovers(flags);
  const now = ctx.clock.now();
  await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const updated = await tx
      .update(orders)
      .set({ payoutRef: ref, payoutUpdatedAt: now })
      .where(
        and(
          eq(orders.id, orderId),
          eq(orders.type, 'REDEMPTION'),
          eq(orders.status, 'SETTLED'),
          inArray(orders.payoutStatus, ['EXPECTED', 'DELAYED']),
          isNull(orders.payoutRef),
        ),
      )
      .returning({ id: orders.id, payoutStatus: orders.payoutStatus });
    const [order] = updated;
    if (order === undefined) {
      throw new OpsCliError(
        `order ${orderId} is not a settled redemption awaiting its payout (or it already has a reference)`,
      );
    }
    await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
      action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.OPS_PAYOUT_REF_RECORDED,
      actorType: 'ADMIN',
      actorId: approver1,
      entityType: 'orders',
      entityId: order.id,
      data: { approver2, payoutRef: ref, status: order.payoutStatus },
    });
  });
  return `ops:payout-ref: order ${orderId} payout reference ${ref} recorded (approved by ${approver1} and ${approver2}); payout.watch marks it CREDITED`;
};
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-inputs.ts` (FR-21: the two places an operator's invite list may come from. A RunTask's `containerOverrides.command` stays in CloudTrail and on the stopped task, so a mobile never goes on a command line):
```ts
import { createHash, createHmac } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import type { Env } from '../config/env.js';
import { OpsCliError } from './ops-common.js';

/**
 * Values an operator must never put on a command line (FR-21). A deployed run's RunTask
 * `containerOverrides.command` is kept by CloudTrail and shown on stopped tasks, so ops:invite reads its
 * mobiles from an SSM SecureString (deployed) or from a file (local and test), never from argv.
 */
export interface OpsInputs {
  /**
   * The decrypted value of the SecureString `name`, which must be `/sanchay/{SANCHAY_APP_ENV}/invites/<name>`.
   * Read with the ops task role, which F1 allows `ssm:GetParameter` on that prefix and nothing else.
   */
  ssmSecureString(name: string): Promise<string>;
  /** A local file's UTF-8 text; refused unless SANCHAY_APP_ENV is local or test. */
  localFile(path: string): Promise<string>;
}

export interface OpsInputsDeps {
  appEnv: Env['SANCHAY_APP_ENV'];
  /** `process.env` in a run: ECS sets AWS_REGION and AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI in a Fargate task. */
  processEnv: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
  fetch: typeof fetch;
  /** The wall clock for X-Amz-Date (AWS refuses a skewed signature), never the app's FakeClock. */
  now: () => Date;
}

/** The only SSM names ops reads; F1's IAM grant is the same prefix. */
export const invitesParamPrefix = (appEnv: string): string => `/sanchay/${appEnv}/invites/`;
const INVITES_PARAM_LEAF = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$/;
/** ECS's task-role credential endpoint (Fargate platform 1.4+). */
const ECS_CREDENTIALS_HOST = 'http://169.254.170.2';
const CREDENTIALS_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;
const SSM_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

export interface AwsCredentials {
  accessKeyId: string;
  secretAccessKey: string;
  /** Always present for task-role credentials. */
  sessionToken: string | null;
}

export interface SigV4Request {
  method: string;
  host: string;
  /** The canonical (already URI-encoded) path; `/` for the AWS JSON protocol. No query string. */
  path: string;
  /** Lower-case names; `host` is added from `host`. Every header given here is signed. */
  headers: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  body: string;
  region: string;
  service: string;
  /** `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`. */
  amzDate: string;
}

const sha256Hex = (text: string): string => createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex');
const hmac = (key: string | Buffer, text: string): Buffer =>
  createHmac('sha256', key).update(text, 'utf8').digest();

export const toAmzDate = (at: Date): string =>
  at
    .toISOString()
    .replace(/[-:]/g, '')
    .replace(/\.\d{3}/, '');

/** SigV4's signing key: HMAC-SHA256 over the date, region, service and `aws4_request`. */
export function sigV4SigningKey(
  secretAccessKey: string,
  dateStamp: string,
  region: string,
  service: string,
): Buffer {
  const date = hmac(`AWS4${secretAccessKey}`, dateStamp);
  return hmac(hmac(hmac(date, region), service), 'aws4_request');
}

/**
 * AWS Signature Version 4 for a request without a query string; returns the Authorization header value.
 * ops-inputs.test.ts pins it to AWS's published vectors. The repo has no AWS SDK for SSM and the catalog
 * is closed (A1 rule), so this is the documented algorithm over node:crypto.
 */
export function sigV4Authorization(
  req: SigV4Request,
  credentials: Pick<AwsCredentials, 'accessKeyId' | 'secretAccessKey'>,
): string {
  const headers = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries({ ...req.headers, host: req.host })) {
    headers.set(name.toLowerCase(), value.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' '));
  }
  const names = [...headers.keys()].sort();
  const signedHeaders = names.join(';');
  const canonicalRequest = [
    req.method,
    req.path,
    '',
    ...names.map((name) => `${name}:${headers.get(name) ?? ''}`),
    '',
    signedHeaders,
    sha256Hex(req.body),
  ].join('\n');
  const dateStamp = req.amzDate.slice(0, 8);
  const scope = `${dateStamp}/${req.region}/${req.service}/aws4_request`;
  const stringToSign = ['AWS4-HMAC-SHA256', req.amzDate, scope, sha256Hex(canonicalRequest)].join(
    '\n',
  );
  const key = sigV4SigningKey(credentials.secretAccessKey, dateStamp, req.region, req.service);
  const signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(stringToSign, 'utf8').digest('hex');
  return `AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=${credentials.accessKeyId}/${scope}, SignedHeaders=${signedHeaders}, Signature=${signature}`;
}

/** fetch with a deadline; a network failure or timeout is a refusal (exit 1), never a stack trace. */
async function fetchOrRefuse(
  deps: OpsInputsDeps,
  what: string,
  url: string,
  init: RequestInit,
  timeoutMs: number,
): Promise<Response> {
  try {
    return await deps.fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });
  } catch (err) {
    throw new OpsCliError(`could not reach ${what} (${err instanceof Error ? err.name : 'error'})`);
  }
}

async function taskRoleCredentials(deps: OpsInputsDeps): Promise<AwsCredentials> {
  const relative = deps.processEnv.AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI;
  if (relative === undefined || relative === '') {
    throw new OpsCliError(
      '--mobiles-param needs the ops task role (AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI is not set): run it as the deployed ops task (docs/runbooks/ops-cli.md), or use --mobiles-file locally',
    );
  }
  const res = await fetchOrRefuse(
    deps,
    'the ECS credential endpoint',
    `${ECS_CREDENTIALS_HOST}${relative}`,
    {},
    CREDENTIALS_TIMEOUT_MS,
  );
  if (!res.ok) throw new OpsCliError(`the ECS credential endpoint answered HTTP ${res.status}`);
  const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as Record<string, unknown> | null;
  const id = body?.AccessKeyId;
  const signing = body?.SecretAccessKey;
  const session = body?.Token;
  if (typeof id !== 'string' || typeof signing !== 'string') {
    throw new OpsCliError('the ECS credential endpoint returned no task-role credentials');
  }
  return {
    accessKeyId: id,
    secretAccessKey: signing,
    sessionToken: typeof session === 'string' ? session : null,
  };
}

/** `ssm:GetParameter` with decryption (AWS JSON 1.1 protocol). The value is returned, never printed. */
async function getSecureString(deps: OpsInputsDeps, name: string): Promise<string> {
  const prefix = invitesParamPrefix(deps.appEnv);
  if (!name.startsWith(prefix) || !INVITES_PARAM_LEAF.test(name.slice(prefix.length))) {
    throw new OpsCliError(
      `--mobiles-param must be ${prefix}<name> (a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-'; at most 63 characters)`,
    );
  }
  const region = deps.processEnv.AWS_REGION ?? deps.processEnv.AWS_DEFAULT_REGION;
  if (region === undefined || region === '') {
    throw new OpsCliError('--mobiles-param needs AWS_REGION, which ECS sets in a Fargate task');
  }
  const credentials = await taskRoleCredentials(deps);
  const host = `ssm.${region}.amazonaws.com`;
  const amzDate = toAmzDate(deps.now());
  const body = JSON.stringify({ Name: name, WithDecryption: true });
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    'content-type': 'application/x-amz-json-1.1',
    'x-amz-date': amzDate,
    'x-amz-target': 'AmazonSSM.GetParameter',
  };
  if (credentials.sessionToken !== null) headers['x-amz-security-token'] = credentials.sessionToken;
  const authorization = sigV4Authorization(
    { method: 'POST', host, path: '/', headers, body, region, service: 'ssm', amzDate },
    credentials,
  );
  const res = await fetchOrRefuse(
    deps,
    'SSM',
    `https://${host}/`,
    { method: 'POST', headers: { ...headers, authorization }, body },
    SSM_TIMEOUT_MS,
  );
  // A 200 carries the decrypted value: parsed here, never logged or put in a message.
  const json = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as {
    __type?: unknown;
    Parameter?: { Type?: unknown; Value?: unknown };
  } | null;
  if (!res.ok) {
    const type = String(json?.__type ?? `HTTP ${res.status}`)
      .split('#')
      .pop();
    if (type === 'ParameterNotFound') {
      throw new OpsCliError(`no SSM parameter ${name}: put it first (docs/runbooks/ops-cli.md)`);
    }
    throw new OpsCliError(`SSM refused to read ${name} (${type})`);
  }
  const parameter = json?.Parameter;
  if (parameter?.Type !== 'SecureString') {
    throw new OpsCliError(
      `${name} must be a SecureString because it holds mobile numbers: delete it and put it again with --type SecureString`,
    );
  }
  if (typeof parameter.Value !== 'string') throw new OpsCliError(`${name} has no value`);
  return parameter.Value;
}

/** The inputs of a run: `opsContextOf(app)` passes process.env, the global fetch and the wall clock. */
export function opsInputsFor(deps: OpsInputsDeps): OpsInputs {
  return {
    ssmSecureString: (name) => getSecureString(deps, name),
    localFile: async (path) => {
      if (deps.appEnv !== 'local' && deps.appEnv !== 'test') {
        throw new OpsCliError(
          '--mobiles-file is for SANCHAY_APP_ENV local and test; a deployed run reads --mobiles-param',
        );
      }
      try {
        return await readFile(path, 'utf8');
      } catch {
        throw new OpsCliError(`could not read --mobiles-file ${path}`);
      }
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { inArray } from 'drizzle-orm';
import type { DbExecutor } from '../db/client.js';
import { pilotInvites } from '../modules/identity/pilot-invites.schema.js';
import { pgErrorCodeOf } from '../modules/platform/pg-errors.js';
import {
  flagValue,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  type OpsFlags,
  parseFlags,
  requireHandle,
} from './ops-common.js';
import type { OpsInputs } from './ops-inputs.js';

/** D7's invite lifetime. */
export const INVITE_TTL_DAYS = 30;
/** Mobiles per run: an SSM standard parameter holds 4 KB, about 350 lines. */
export const INVITE_BATCH_MAX = 300;
/** `MOBILE_REGEX` of @sanchay/validation: the 10-digit national number the login OTP blind-indexes. */
const MOBILE_RE = /^[6-9][0-9]{9}$/;
const NOTE_MAX = 200;
/** The byte-order mark some Windows editors put at the start of a UTF-8 file. */
const BOM = 0xfeff;

/** `+91 98765 43210`, `919876543210` and `98765-43210` mean 9876543210; anything else is refused (null). */
export function inviteMobile(raw: string): string | null {
  const compact = raw.replace(/[\s-]/g, '').replace(/^\+?91(?=\d{10}$)/, '');
  return MOBILE_RE.test(compact) ? compact : null;
}

/** Stdout is CloudWatch in a deployed environment: a mobile is only ever printed as its last 4 digits. */
export const maskMobile = (mobile: string): string => `******${mobile.slice(-4)}`;

const lineList = (lines: readonly number[]): string =>
  `${lines.length === 1 ? 'line' : 'lines'} ${lines.join(', ')}`;

/**
 * The invite list: one mobile per line (LF or CRLF; a leading BOM, blank lines and spaces are ignored).
 * Every refusal names line numbers only, never a value.
 */
export function parseInviteList(text: string): string[] {
  const mobiles: string[] = [];
  const malformed: number[] = [];
  const repeated: number[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const body = text.charCodeAt(0) === BOM ? text.slice(1) : text;
  body.split(/\r?\n/).forEach((raw, index) => {
    if (raw.trim() === '') return;
    const mobile = inviteMobile(raw);
    if (mobile === null) malformed.push(index + 1);
    else if (seen.has(mobile)) repeated.push(index + 1);
    else {
      seen.add(mobile);
      mobiles.push(mobile);
    }
  });
  if (malformed.length > 0) {
    throw new OpsCliError(
      `${lineList(malformed)} of the invite list ${malformed.length === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'} not a 10-digit Indian mobile number (one per line; a +91 prefix is dropped)`,
    );
  }
  if (repeated.length > 0) {
    throw new OpsCliError(
      `${lineList(repeated)} of the invite list ${repeated.length === 1 ? 'repeats' : 'repeat'} an earlier mobile`,
    );
  }
  if (mobiles.length === 0) throw new OpsCliError('the invite list has no mobile number');
  if (mobiles.length > INVITE_BATCH_MAX) {
    throw new OpsCliError(`the invite list has more than ${INVITE_BATCH_MAX} mobiles; split it`);
  }
  return mobiles;
}

/** Exactly one source; a mobile never goes on the command line (FR-21). */
function inviteListText(inputs: OpsInputs, flags: OpsFlags): Promise<string> {
  const param = flags.get('mobiles-param');
  const file = flags.get('mobiles-file');
  if (typeof param === 'string' && file === undefined) return inputs.ssmSecureString(param);
  if (typeof file === 'string' && param === undefined) return inputs.localFile(file);
  throw new OpsCliError(
    'give exactly one of --mobiles-param /sanchay/<env>/invites/<name> (deployed) or --mobiles-file <path> (local and test)',
  );
}

function alreadyInvited(mobiles: readonly string[]): OpsCliError {
  const masked = mobiles.map(maskMobile).join(', ');
  return new OpsCliError(
    mobiles.length === 1
      ? `the mobile ${masked} already has an invite (used or not); nothing was written`
      : `the mobiles ${masked} already have an invite (used or not); nothing was written`,
  );
}

/**
 * `ops:invite --mobiles-param /sanchay/{env}/invites/<name> --by <handle> [--note <text>]` (deployed: an
 * SSM SecureString read with the ops task role, deleted by the operator after the run) or
 * `ops:invite --mobiles-file <path> --by <handle> [--note <text>]` (local and test). One pilot invite per
 * listed mobile for INVITE_TTL_DAYS, each written by D7's `PilotInvites.add` with its PILOT_INVITE_ADDED
 * audit row, all in one transaction: if any listed mobile already has an invite, nothing is written. A
 * mobile is stored only as its blind index (the one `AuthService.verifyLoginOtp` computes) and is printed
 * only as its last 4 digits.
 */
export const opsInvite: OpsCommand = async (ctx, argv) => {
  const flags = parseFlags(argv, { values: ['mobiles-param', 'mobiles-file', 'by', 'note'] });
  const by = requireHandle(flags, 'by');
  const note = flags.has('note') ? flagValue(flags, 'note') : null;
  if (note !== null && note.length > NOTE_MAX) {
    throw new OpsCliError(`--note is at most ${NOTE_MAX} characters`);
  }
  const mobiles = parseInviteList(await inviteListText(ctx.inputs, flags));
  const bidxOf = new Map(mobiles.map((m) => [m, ctx.crypto.blindIndex('mobile', m)] as const));
  const bidxs = [...bidxOf.values()];
  const invitedAmong = async (exec: DbExecutor): Promise<string[]> => {
    const rows = await exec
      .select({ bidx: pilotInvites.mobileBidx })
      .from(pilotInvites)
      .where(inArray(pilotInvites.mobileBidx, bidxs));
    const taken = new Set(rows.map((r) => r.bidx.toString('hex')));
    return mobiles.filter((m) => taken.has(bidxOf.get(m)?.toString('hex') ?? ''));
  };
  let expiresAt: Date;
  try {
    expiresAt = await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      const taken = await invitedAmong(tx);
      if (taken.length > 0) throw alreadyInvited(taken);
      for (const mobileBidx of bidxs) {
        await ctx.invites.add(tx, { mobileBidx, invitedBy: by, note, ttlDays: INVITE_TTL_DAYS });
      }
      const rows = await tx
        .select({ expiresAt: pilotInvites.expiresAt })
        .from(pilotInvites)
        .where(inArray(pilotInvites.mobileBidx, bidxs));
      if (rows.length !== bidxs.length) {
        throw new Error('ops:invite: an invite row is missing after add');
      }
      return new Date(Math.min(...rows.map((r) => r.expiresAt.getTime())));
    });
  } catch (err) {
    if (pgErrorCodeOf(err) !== '23505') throw err;
    // A concurrent invite won the race for one of these mobiles; this transaction wrote nothing.
    const taken = await invitedAmong(ctx.db);
    throw taken.length > 0
      ? alreadyInvited(taken)
      : new OpsCliError('a concurrent run invited one of these mobiles; nothing was written');
  }
  return `ops:invite: invited ${mobiles.map(maskMobile).join(', ')} (expires ${expiresAt.toISOString()})`;
};
```

```ts
import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { schemeNavs } from '../modules/catalogue/catalogue.schema.js';
import {
  flagValue,
  OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  parseFlags,
  requireTwoApprovers,
} from './ops-common.js';

/** D8's `scheme_navs_isin_ck`. */
const ISIN_RE = /^INF[A-Z0-9]{9}$/;

/**
 * `pnpm ops:nav-release --isin <isin> --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b>` (D9, through the ops runner): lifts
 * a NAV quarantine once two founders have checked the NAV on the AMC site (NAV-09). `scheme_navs.quarantined`
 * and one `NAV_RELEASE` audit row are the only writes; a NAV that is not quarantined is refused. R-35: the
 * next `nav.sync.daily` finds that row (D9's `pendingNavReleases`) and takes the ISIN's feed value once,
 * without the 25% check.
 */
export const opsNavRelease: OpsCommand = async (ctx, argv) => {
  const flags = parseFlags(argv, { values: ['isin', 'approver1', 'approver2'] });
  const isin = flagValue(flags, 'isin').toUpperCase();
  if (!ISIN_RE.test(isin)) {
    throw new OpsCliError('--isin must be a mutual fund ISIN (INF and 9 letters or digits)');
  }
  const { approver1, approver2 } = requireTwoApprovers(flags);
  const now = ctx.clock.now();
  await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const [row] = await tx
      .select({ quarantined: schemeNavs.quarantined })
      .from(schemeNavs)
      .where(eq(schemeNavs.isin, isin))
      .for('update');
    if (row === undefined) throw new OpsCliError(`no NAV row for ${isin}`);
    if (!row.quarantined) {
      throw new OpsCliError(`the NAV of ${isin} is not quarantined; nothing to release`);
    }
    await tx
      .update(schemeNavs)
      .set({ quarantined: false, updatedAt: now })
      .where(and(eq(schemeNavs.isin, isin), eq(schemeNavs.quarantined, true)));
    await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
      action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.NAV_RELEASE,
      actorType: 'ADMIN',
      actorId: approver1,
      entityType: 'scheme_navs',
      entityId: isin,
      data: { approver2, status: 'RELEASED' },
    });
  });
  return `ops:nav-release: the NAV of ${isin} is released (approved by ${approver1} and ${approver2})`;
};
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-resolve-break.ts`:
```ts
import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { mandates } from '../modules/plans/plans.schema.js';
import { reconBreaks } from '../modules/platform/kernel.schema.js';
import {
  flagValue,
  OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS,
  OpsCliError,
  type OpsCommand,
  parseFlags,
  requireTwoApprovers,
  requireUuid,
} from './ops-common.js';

/** integrity.invariants resolves its own breaks once the data is right; a person never does. */
const SELF_RESOLVING_PREFIX = 'INVARIANT_';
const NOTE_MAX = 500;

/**
 * `pnpm ops:resolve-break --id <break id> --note <what was done> --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b>`: marks one
 * OPEN recon break RESOLVED once ops has dealt with it, so F1's `sanchay-prod-money-invariant-breach` alarm
 * can return to OK and page again on the next one. The break row and one audit row (the note is its reason)
 * are the only writes. Refused: an INVARIANT_* break (it resolves itself), and a MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS
 * break while its mandate is still RECONCILING (fp.reconcile.nonfinal would re-open it within 5 minutes).
 */
export const opsResolveBreak: OpsCommand = async (ctx, argv) => {
  const flags = parseFlags(argv, { values: ['id', 'note', 'approver1', 'approver2'] });
  const id = requireUuid(flags, 'id');
  const note = flagValue(flags, 'note');
  if (note.length > NOTE_MAX) throw new OpsCliError(`--note is at most ${NOTE_MAX} characters`);
  const { approver1, approver2 } = requireTwoApprovers(flags);
  const now = ctx.clock.now();
  const resolved = await ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const [brk] = await tx
      .select({
        kind: reconBreaks.kind,
        severity: reconBreaks.severity,
        status: reconBreaks.status,
        entityType: reconBreaks.entityType,
        entityId: reconBreaks.entityId,
      })
      .from(reconBreaks)
      .where(eq(reconBreaks.id, id))
      .for('update');
    if (brk === undefined) throw new OpsCliError(`no recon break ${id}`);
    if (brk.status !== 'OPEN') throw new OpsCliError(`recon break ${id} is already ${brk.status}`);
    if (brk.kind.startsWith(SELF_RESOLVING_PREFIX)) {
      throw new OpsCliError(
        `${brk.kind} resolves itself on the next hourly integrity.invariants run once the data is right`,
      );
    }
    if (brk.kind === 'MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS') {
      const [stuck] = await tx
        .select({ id: mandates.id })
        .from(mandates)
        .where(and(eq(mandates.id, brk.entityId), eq(mandates.status, 'RECONCILING')));
      if (stuck !== undefined) {
        throw new OpsCliError(
          `mandate ${brk.entityId} is still RECONCILING; fp.reconcile.nonfinal keeps this break open until it is not`,
        );
      }
    }
    await tx
      .update(reconBreaks)
      .set({ status: 'RESOLVED', resolvedAt: now, updatedAt: now })
      .where(eq(reconBreaks.id, id));
    await ctx.audit.record(tx, {
      action: OPS_AUDIT_ACTIONS.OPS_BREAK_RESOLVED,
      actorType: 'ADMIN',
      actorId: approver1,
      entityType: 'recon_breaks',
      entityId: id,
      reason: note,
      data: { approver2, outcome: brk.kind, status: brk.severity },
    });
    return brk;
  });
  return `ops:resolve-break: ${resolved.kind} on ${resolved.entityType} ${resolved.entityId} is RESOLVED (approved by ${approver1} and ${approver2})`;
};
```

`apps/api/src/cli/ops-runner.ts`:
```ts
import type { INestApplicationContext } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppConfig } from '../config/app-config.js';
import type { Env } from '../config/env.js';
import { createDb, DB, type DbHandle } from '../db/client.js';
import { PilotInvites } from '../modules/identity/pilot-invites.service.js';
import { AuditService } from '../modules/platform/audit.service.js';
import { CLOCK, type Clock } from '../modules/platform/clock.js';
import { Crypto } from '../modules/platform/crypto.js';
import { Jobs } from '../modules/platform/jobs/jobs.service.js';
import { OpsCliError, type OpsCommand, type OpsContext } from './ops-common.js';
import { assertOpsPrivileges, OpsPrivilegeError, opsDatabaseUrl } from './ops-db.js';
import { opsInputsFor } from './ops-inputs.js';
import { opsInvite } from './ops-invite.js';
import { opsKillSwitch } from './ops-kill-switch.js';
import { opsNavRelease } from './ops-nav-release.js';
import { opsPayoutRef } from './ops-payout-ref.js';
import { opsRefundUtr } from './ops-refund-utr.js';
import { opsResolveBreak } from './ops-resolve-break.js';
import { opsSipSwitch } from './ops-sip-switch.js';
import { opsSync } from './ops-sync.js';

/**
 * Every ops command (R-16). A later task registers one by key-level edits only: create
 * `apps/api/src/cli/ops-<name>.ts` exporting `ops<Name>: OpsCommand`, import it here, append one entry
 * below and one USAGE line, and append its file to the boundary list in `ops-common.test.ts`.
 */
export const OPS_COMMANDS: Readonly<Record<string, OpsCommand>> = {
  'ops:sync': opsSync,
  'ops:kill-switch': opsKillSwitch,
  'ops:sip-switch': opsSipSwitch,
  'ops:refund-utr': opsRefundUtr,
  'ops:payout-ref': opsPayoutRef,
  'ops:invite': opsInvite,
  'ops:nav-release': opsNavRelease,
  'ops:resolve-break': opsResolveBreak,
};

const USAGE = [
  'usage (SANCHAY_APP_ROLE=ops; see docs/runbooks/ops-cli.md):',
  '  ops:sync --order <id> --by <handle>',
  '  ops:kill-switch --off --by <handle> --reason <text>',
  '  ops:kill-switch --on --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle> --reason <text>',
  '  ops:sip-switch --off --by <handle> --reason <text>',
  '  ops:sip-switch --on --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle> --reason <text>',
  '  ops:refund-utr --order <id> --utr <ref> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>',
  '  ops:payout-ref --order <id> --ref <bank ref> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>',
  '  ops:invite --mobiles-param /sanchay/<env>/invites/<name> --by <handle> [--note <text>]',
  '  ops:invite --mobiles-file <path> --by <handle> [--note <text>]   (local and test only)',
  '  ops:nav-release --isin <isin> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>',
  '  ops:resolve-break --id <break id> --note <text> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>',
].join('\n');

/**
 * The pieces an ops command may use, from a booted application context: the one builder of an OpsContext
 * (runOpsCli, and every test that runs a command with its app). `inputs` reads SSM with this process's
 * ECS task-role credentials and the wall clock, and allows a local file only in SANCHAY_APP_ENV local/test.
 */
export function opsContextOf(app: INestApplicationContext): OpsContext {
  return {
    db: app.get<DbHandle>(DB).db,
    jobs: app.get(Jobs),
    audit: app.get(AuditService),
    clock: app.get<Clock>(CLOCK),
    crypto: app.get(Crypto),
    invites: app.get(PilotInvites),
    inputs: opsInputsFor({
      appEnv: app.get(AppConfig).env.SANCHAY_APP_ENV,
      processEnv: process.env,
      fetch: globalThis.fetch,
      now: () => new Date(),
    }),
  };
}

/**
 * The `ops` role (R-16): runs one command and returns the exit code (0 done, 1 refused, 2 usage); no HTTP
 * listener, no job worker. The session role is pinned to sanchay_app and checked for DDL rights before
 * Nest boots, then the command runs against an application context built with RV-04-F4-2's
 * NEST_APP_OPTIONS (FpModule is worker-only, so no FP client exists in this process).
 */
export async function runOpsCli(env: Env, argv: readonly string[]): Promise<number> {
  const [name, ...rest] = argv;
  const command = name === undefined ? undefined : OPS_COMMANDS[name];
  if (name === undefined || command === undefined) {
    console.error(USAGE);
    return 2;
  }
  const opsEnv: Env = {
    ...env,
    SANCHAY_APP_ROLE: 'ops',
    DATABASE_URL: opsDatabaseUrl(env.DATABASE_URL),
  };
  const probe = createDb(opsEnv.DATABASE_URL, 1);
  try {
    await assertOpsPrivileges(probe.db);
  } catch (err) {
    if (!(err instanceof OpsPrivilegeError)) throw err;
    console.error(`${name}: ${err.message}`);
    return 1;
  } finally {
    await probe.close();
  }

  const { NestFactory } = await import('@nestjs/core');
  const { Logger } = await import('nestjs-pino');
  const { NEST_APP_OPTIONS } = await import('../bootstrap.js');
  const { AppModule } = await import('../app.module.js');
  const app = await NestFactory.createApplicationContext(AppModule.forRoot(opsEnv), {
    ...NEST_APP_OPTIONS,
    bufferLogs: true,
  });
  app.useLogger(app.get(Logger));
  try {
    console.log(await command(opsContextOf(app), rest));
    return 0;
  } catch (err) {
    if (!(err instanceof OpsCliError)) throw err;
    console.error(`${name}: ${err.message}`);
    return 1;
  } finally {
    await app.close();
  }
}
```

`apps/api/src/modules/platform/recon/recon-rules.ts`:
```ts
import type { OrderStatus, PlanStatus } from '@sanchay/domain';
import { MINUTE } from '../clock.js';

const text = (value: unknown): string | null =>
  value === null || value === undefined || value === '' ? null : String(value);

/** The fields reconciliation needs from any FP order-like object (mf_purchase, mf_purchase_plan, mf_redemption). */
export interface FpObjectRef {
  id: string;
  oldId: number | null;
  state: string;
  /** Our row id, when we created the object; FP-raised SIP instalments carry none. */
  sourceRefId: string | null;
  /** The mf_purchase_plan an instalment belongs to (mf_purchase only). */
  plan: string | null;
}

export function fpObjectRef(raw: Record<string, unknown>): FpObjectRef {
  const oldId = Number(raw.old_id);
  return {
    id: String(raw.id),
    oldId:
      raw.old_id === null || raw.old_id === undefined || !Number.isSafeInteger(oldId)
        ? null
        : oldId,
    state: String(raw.state ?? '').toLowerCase(),
    sourceRefId: text(raw.source_ref_id),
    plan: text(raw.plan),
  };
}

/** One FP MF folio (`GET /v2/mf_folios`): FakeFp and research fp-api §7 call it `number`; `folio_number` is accepted too. */
export function folioNumberOf(raw: Record<string, unknown>): string | null {
  return text(raw.number ?? raw.folio_number);
}

export type DriftSeverity = 'NONE' | 'WARNING' | 'CRITICAL';

const LOCAL_SUCCESS: ReadonlySet<OrderStatus> = new Set<OrderStatus>(['SETTLED', 'UNITS_PENDING']);
const LOCAL_FAILURE: ReadonlySet<OrderStatus> = new Set<OrderStatus>([
  'FAILED',
  'EXPIRED',
  'REJECTED',
  'CANCELLED',
  'CONSENT_EXPIRED',
  'SKIPPED',
]);

/**
 * recon.fp.daily's verdict on one purchase we hold. Lag the sweeps close on their own (FP ahead of us:
 * webhooks, `orders.units.reconcile`, `fp.reconcile.nonfinal`) is NONE. CRITICAL is an outcome
 * disagreement the investor would see wrongly (money in vs money out); WARNING is anything else odd.
 */
export function purchaseDrift(fpState: string, local: OrderStatus): DriftSeverity {
  switch (fpState) {
    case 'successful':
      return LOCAL_FAILURE.has(local) || local === 'REVERSED' ? 'CRITICAL' : 'NONE';
    case 'failed':
    case 'expired':
    case 'cancelled':
      if (LOCAL_SUCCESS.has(local)) return 'CRITICAL';
      return local === 'REVERSED' ? 'WARNING' : 'NONE';
    case 'reversed':
      // Nothing sweeps SETTLED orders: a reversal whose webhook was lost is found only here.
      if (local === 'SETTLED') return 'CRITICAL';
      return local === 'REVERSED' ? 'NONE' : 'WARNING';
    case 'under_review':
    case 'pending':
    case 'submitted':
      return LOCAL_SUCCESS.has(local) || local === 'REVERSED' ? 'WARNING' : 'NONE';
    default:
      return 'WARNING';
  }
}

const FP_PLAN_ENDED: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['failed', 'cancelled', 'completed']);
const LOCAL_PLAN_ENDED: ReadonlySet<PlanStatus> = new Set<PlanStatus>([
  'FAILED',
  'CANCELLED',
  'COMPLETED',
  'REJECTED',
  'CONSENT_EXPIRED',
  'MANDATE_REVOKED',
]);

/** A plan we show as running that FP has ended, or one we ended that FP still debits. */
export function planDrift(fpState: string, local: PlanStatus): boolean {
  if (local === 'ACTIVE') return FP_PLAN_ENDED.has(fpState);
  return LOCAL_PLAN_ENDED.has(local) && fpState === 'active';
}

/**
 * Where LOOKUP-ADOPT moves a RECONCILING redemption once FP shows the object (D5's RECONCILING exits).
 * In review it rejoins F5's advance job; submitted or successful it waits for F5's settlement sweep
 * (`orders.units.reconcile`); a terminal FP state ends it. Null: a state D5 does not map (left alone).
 */
export function redemptionAdoptTarget(fpState: string): OrderStatus | null {
  switch (fpState) {
    case 'under_review':
      return 'UNDER_REVIEW';
    case 'pending':
      return 'CONFIRMING';
    case 'submitted':
    case 'successful':
      return 'PROCESSING';
    case 'failed':
      return 'FAILED';
    case 'expired':
      return 'EXPIRED';
    case 'cancelled':
      return 'CANCELLED';
    default:
      return null;
  }
}

/**
 * How long after approve, or after the consent deadline, an approved redemption is left to F5's own submit
 * attempt (pg-boss retries it at once, up to 3 times) before fp.reconcile.nonfinal acts on it.
 */
export const SUBMIT_GRACE_MS = 2 * MINUTE;

export type RedemptionResumeAction = 'RESUBMIT' | 'WAIT' | 'EXPIRE';

export interface RedemptionResumeInput {
  /** consent_challenges.status: CONSUMED or CONSUMED_UNUSED (the sweep or markUnused). */
  challengeStatus: string;
  /** consent_records: approve's time, the two deadlines, and the first useConsumed call. */
  consumedAt: Date | null;
  executeBefore: Date | null;
  sagaExpiresAt: Date | null;
  firstAttemptAt: Date | null;
  now: Date;
}

/**
 * fp.reconcile.nonfinal's verdict on an approved redemption that F5's submit job has not moved on
 * (CONSENT_PENDING or CONSENTED with a consumed challenge, so no FP write has happened). The deadline is
 * the one `ConsentEngine.useConsumed` applies: `execute_before` until the first attempt is stamped,
 * `saga_expires_at` after it. Inside it: RESUBMIT (once approve is SUBMIT_GRACE_MS old). Within
 * SUBMIT_GRACE_MS after it: WAIT, because an attempt that passed the check may still be on its way to
 * SUBMITTING. Later, or for a CONSUMED_UNUSED challenge: EXPIRE (F5's own CONSENT_EXPIRED path).
 */
export function redemptionResumeAction(input: RedemptionResumeInput): RedemptionResumeAction {
  if (input.challengeStatus !== 'CONSUMED') return 'EXPIRE';
  const deadline = input.firstAttemptAt === null ? input.executeBefore : input.sagaExpiresAt;
  if (deadline === null) return 'EXPIRE';
  const now = input.now.getTime();
  if (now > deadline.getTime() + SUBMIT_GRACE_MS) return 'EXPIRE';
  if (now > deadline.getTime()) return 'WAIT';
  if (input.consumedAt !== null && now - input.consumedAt.getTime() < SUBMIT_GRACE_MS) {
    return 'WAIT';
  }
  return 'RESUBMIT';
}
```

`apps/api/src/modules/platform/recon/invariant-checks.ts`:
```ts
import { type SQL, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';

/** recon_breaks.kind per invariant; every one is CRITICAL (F1's `sanchay-prod-money-invariant-breach` pages on it). */
export const INVARIANT_KINDS = {
  /** D-MONEY-071 M1: a provider id without a matching CONSUMED challenge (investor + subject + consumed_at). */
  M1: 'INVARIANT_M1_PROVIDER_ID_WITHOUT_CONSENT',
  /** D-MONEY-071 M2: lot conservation (the outline's "ledger units = Σ lots"). */
  M2: 'INVARIANT_M2_LOT_CONSERVATION',
  /** D-MONEY-071 M3: at most one SUCCESS payment per order. */
  M3: 'INVARIANT_M3_DUPLICATE_PAYMENT_SUCCESS',
  /** D-MONEY-071 M4: exactly one live lot per SETTLED purchase, holding the allotted units; none before SETTLED. */
  M4: 'INVARIANT_M4_SETTLED_PURCHASE_LOT',
  /** The outline's "M4": ACTIVE reservations never exceed the units the folio holds in that scheme. */
  RESERVATIONS: 'INVARIANT_RESERVATIONS_OVER_HELD',
} as const;

export interface InvariantCheck {
  kind: string;
  /** Read-only; returns one row per violating entity. */
  query: SQL;
}

export interface InvariantViolation extends Record<string, unknown> {
  entity_type: string;
  entity_id: string;
  detail: Record<string, unknown> | null;
}

export const INVARIANT_CHECKS: readonly InvariantCheck[] = [
  {
    kind: INVARIANT_KINDS.M1,
    // SIP instalments are raised by FP under the plan's consent, so the plan is checked, not the instalment.
    query: sql`
      WITH subjects AS (
        SELECT 'orders'::text AS subject_table, o.id, o.investor_id FROM app.orders o
         WHERE o.fp_order_id IS NOT NULL AND o.origin = 'ONE_TIME'
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'plans'::text, p.id, p.investor_id FROM app.plans p WHERE p.fp_plan_id IS NOT NULL
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'mandates'::text, m.id, m.investor_id FROM app.mandates m WHERE m.fp_mandate_id IS NOT NULL
      )
      SELECT s.subject_table AS entity_type, s.id::text AS entity_id,
             jsonb_build_object('investorId', s.investor_id::text) AS detail
        FROM subjects s
       WHERE NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM app.consent_subjects cs
           JOIN app.consent_challenges cc ON cc.id = cs.challenge_id
           JOIN app.consent_records cr ON cr.challenge_id = cc.id
          WHERE cs.subject_table = s.subject_table
            AND cs.subject_id = s.id
            AND cs.status = 'CONSENTED'
            AND cc.status = 'CONSUMED'
            AND cc.investor_id = s.investor_id
            AND cc.consumed_at IS NOT NULL
            AND cr.first_attempt_at IS NOT NULL
            AND cr.first_attempt_at >= cc.consumed_at)
    `,
  },
  {
    kind: INVARIANT_KINDS.M2,
    query: sql`
      SELECT 'lots'::text AS entity_type, l.id::text AS entity_id,
             jsonb_build_object('status', l.status, 'units', l.units::text,
                                'unitsRemaining', l.units_remaining::text,
                                'consumed', COALESCE(c.consumed, 0)::text) AS detail
        FROM app.lots l
        LEFT JOIN (SELECT lot_id, sum(units) AS consumed FROM app.lot_consumptions GROUP BY lot_id) c
          ON c.lot_id = l.id
       WHERE (l.status = 'REVERSED' AND COALESCE(c.consumed, 0) <> 0)
          OR (l.status <> 'REVERSED' AND l.units - l.units_remaining <> COALESCE(c.consumed, 0))
    `,
  },
  {
    kind: INVARIANT_KINDS.M3,
    query: sql`
      SELECT 'orders'::text AS entity_type, pa.order_id::text AS entity_id,
             jsonb_build_object('successAttempts', count(*)) AS detail
        FROM app.payment_attempts pa
       WHERE pa.status = 'SUCCESS'
       GROUP BY pa.order_id
      HAVING count(*) > 1
    `,
  },
  {
    kind: INVARIANT_KINDS.M4,
    query: sql`
      SELECT 'orders'::text AS entity_type, o.id::text AS entity_id,
             jsonb_build_object('status', o.status, 'allottedUnits', o.allotted_units::text,
                                'liveLots', count(l.id) FILTER (WHERE l.status <> 'REVERSED')) AS detail
        FROM app.orders o
        LEFT JOIN app.lots l ON l.source_order_id = o.id
       WHERE o.type = 'PURCHASE' AND o.status = 'SETTLED'
       GROUP BY o.id, o.status, o.allotted_units
      HAVING count(l.id) FILTER (WHERE l.status <> 'REVERSED') <> 1
          OR bool_or(l.status <> 'REVERSED' AND l.units <> o.allotted_units)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT 'orders'::text, o.id::text, jsonb_build_object('status', o.status, 'lotId', l.id::text)
        FROM app.lots l
        JOIN app.orders o ON o.id = l.source_order_id
       WHERE o.status NOT IN ('SETTLED', 'REVERSED')
    `,
  },
  {
    kind: INVARIANT_KINDS.RESERVATIONS,
    // Every OPEN lot counts, locked or not: lock-in is F5's draft-time rule and only ever unlocks over time.
    query: sql`
      SELECT 'folios'::text AS entity_type, r.folio_id::text || ':' || r.scheme_id::text AS entity_id,
             jsonb_build_object('reserved', sum(r.units_reserved)::text,
                                'held', COALESCE(h.held, 0)::text) AS detail
        FROM app.redemption_reservations r
        LEFT JOIN (SELECT folio_id, scheme_id, sum(units_remaining) AS held
                     FROM app.lots WHERE status = 'OPEN' GROUP BY folio_id, scheme_id) h
          ON h.folio_id = r.folio_id AND h.scheme_id = r.scheme_id
       WHERE r.status = 'ACTIVE'
       GROUP BY r.folio_id, r.scheme_id, h.held
      HAVING sum(r.units_reserved) > COALESCE(h.held, 0)
    `,
  },
];
```

`apps/api/src/modules/platform/recon/integrity-invariants.job.ts`:
```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { and, eq, notInArray } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { DB, type DbHandle } from '../../../db/client.js';
import { CLOCK, type Clock } from '../clock.js';
import { type Job, JobHandler } from '../jobs/job-registry.js';
import { reconBreaks } from '../kernel.schema.js';
import { ReconBreaks } from '../runtime-config.js';
import { INVARIANT_CHECKS, type InvariantViolation } from './invariant-checks.js';

/**
 * Worker only, hourly (spec §1 "integrity.invariants (hourly: M1, M3, M4)"). Read-only SQL; each violating
 * entity opens one CRITICAL break, and an invariant break whose violation has cleared is resolved, so F1's
 * `criticalBreaksOpen` gauge (ops.gauges.emit) counts what is wrong now. Nothing here writes an order.
 */
@Injectable()
@JobHandler('integrity.invariants')
export class IntegrityInvariantsJob {
  constructor(
    @Inject(DB) private readonly dbh: DbHandle,
    @Inject(CLOCK) private readonly clock: Clock,
  ) {}

  async handle(_job: Job<'integrity.invariants'>): Promise<void> {
    await this.runChecks();
  }

  /** Returns the number of violations per kind. */
  async runChecks(): Promise<Record<string, number>> {
    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
    for (const check of INVARIANT_CHECKS) {
      const { rows } = await db.execute<InvariantViolation>(check.query);
      for (const row of rows) {
        await ReconBreaks.open(db, {
          kind: check.kind,
          entityType: row.entity_type,
          entityId: row.entity_id,
          severity: 'CRITICAL',
          detail: row.detail ?? {},
        });
      }
      const stillViolating = rows.map((row) => row.entity_id);
      await db
        .update(reconBreaks)
        .set({ status: 'RESOLVED', resolvedAt: this.clock.now() })
        .where(
          and(
            eq(reconBreaks.kind, check.kind),
            eq(reconBreaks.status, 'OPEN'),
            stillViolating.length === 0
              ? undefined
              : notInArray(reconBreaks.entityId, stillViolating),
          ),
        );
      counts[check.kind] = rows.length;
    }
    return counts;
  }
}
```
