```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { eq, isNotNull } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { DB, type DbHandle } from '../../../db/client.js';
import { FpRead } from '../../../integrations/fp/fp-read.js';
import { investors } from '../../identity/identity.schema.js';
import { orders } from '../../orders/orders.schema.js';
import { plans } from '../../plans/plans.schema.js';
import { folios } from '../../portfolio/folios.schema.js';
import { type Job, JobHandler } from '../jobs/job-registry.js';
import { ReconBreaks } from '../runtime-config.js';
import {
  type FpObjectRef,
  folioNumberOf,
  fpObjectRef,
  planDrift,
  purchaseDrift,
} from './recon-rules.js';

/** recon_breaks.kind values recon.fp.daily opens (F4's FP_ORDER_STATE_UNEXPECTED is reused, not redeclared). */
export const RECON_FP_KINDS = {
  /** An FP purchase, plan or redemption on the investor's account that we never placed (CRITICAL). */
  FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN: 'RECON_FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN',
  /** FP and we disagree on the outcome: money in at FP, failed with us, or the reverse (CRITICAL). */
  ORDER_OUTCOME_DIFFERS: 'RECON_ORDER_OUTCOME_DIFFERS',
  /** F4's kind: FP's state is odd for the local one, but not an outcome disagreement (WARNING). */
  ORDER_STATE_UNEXPECTED: 'FP_ORDER_STATE_UNEXPECTED',
  /** A plan running on one side and ended on the other (WARNING). */
  PLAN_STATE_UNEXPECTED: 'FP_PLAN_STATE_UNEXPECTED',
  /** A folio FP holds for the investor that we have no row for (WARNING; folio.sync covers known folios). */
  FOLIO_UNKNOWN: 'RECON_FOLIO_UNKNOWN',
  /** An FP read failed for this investor; the sweep moved on (WARNING). */
  DAILY_FAILED: 'RECON_FP_DAILY_FAILED',
} as const;

/**
 * Worker only, 02:00 IST (spec §1 "recon.fp.daily: orders, plans and holdings per investor"). Read-only:
 * per investor with an FP account, FP's purchases, plans, redemptions and folios are listed first,
 * outside any transaction, then compared with our rows; each finding opens an idempotent break. It does
 * not compare units: F4's `folio.sync` (05:00) owns the per-folio holdings comparison, and F4's
 * `orders.units.reconcile` and `fp.reconcile.nonfinal` close ordinary lag, which is therefore quiet here.
 */
@Injectable()
@JobHandler('recon.fp.daily')
export class ReconFpDailyJob {
  constructor(
    @Inject(DB) private readonly dbh: DbHandle,
    @Inject(FpRead) private readonly fpRead: FpRead,
  ) {}

  async handle(_job: Job<'recon.fp.daily'>): Promise<void> {
    const accounts = await this.dbh.db
      .select({ id: investors.id, mfia: investors.fpMfInvestmentAccountId })
      .from(investors)
      .where(isNotNull(investors.fpMfInvestmentAccountId));
    for (const { id, mfia } of accounts) {
      if (mfia === null) continue;
      try {
        await this.reconcileInvestor(id, mfia);
      } catch (err) {
        await ReconBreaks.open(this.dbh.db, {
          kind: RECON_FP_KINDS.DAILY_FAILED,
          entityType: 'investors',
          entityId: id,
          severity: 'WARNING',
          detail: { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) },
        });
      }
    }
  }

  async reconcileInvestor(investorId: string, mfia: string): Promise<void> {
    const fpPurchases = (await this.fpRead.purchases({ mfInvestmentAccount: mfia })).items.map(
      fpObjectRef,
    );
    const fpPlans = (await this.fpRead.purchasePlans({ mfInvestmentAccount: mfia })).items.map(
      fpObjectRef,
    );
    const fpRedemptions = (await this.fpRead.redemptions({ mfInvestmentAccount: mfia })).items.map(
      fpObjectRef,
    );
    const fpFolios = (await this.fpRead.folios({ mfInvestmentAccount: mfia })).items
      .map(folioNumberOf)
      .filter((n): n is string => n !== null);

    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const localOrders = await db
      .select({ id: orders.id, status: orders.status, fpOrderId: orders.fpOrderId })
      .from(orders)
      .where(eq(orders.investorId, investorId));
    const localPlans = await db
      .select({ id: plans.id, status: plans.status, fpPlanId: plans.fpPlanId })
      .from(plans)
      .where(eq(plans.investorId, investorId));
    const localFolios = await db
      .select({ folioNumber: folios.folioNumber })
      .from(folios)
      .where(eq(folios.investorId, investorId));

    const orderIds = new Set(localOrders.map((o) => o.id));
    const ordersByFpId = new Map(
      localOrders.flatMap((o) => (o.fpOrderId === null ? [] : [[o.fpOrderId, o] as const])),
    );
    const planIds = new Set(localPlans.map((p) => p.id));
    const plansByFpId = new Map(
      localPlans.flatMap((p) => (p.fpPlanId === null ? [] : [[p.fpPlanId, p] as const])),
    );
    // A RECONCILING row has no FP id yet; FP's source_ref_id is our row id, so it is ours (LOOKUP-ADOPT pending).
    const ours = (ref: FpObjectRef, ids: ReadonlySet<string>) =>
      ref.sourceRefId !== null && ids.has(ref.sourceRefId);

    for (const fp of fpPurchases) {
      const local = ordersByFpId.get(fp.id);
      if (local === undefined) {
        // An instalment FP raised on one of our plans is ours; plans.instalments.sync mirrors it.
        const instalment = fp.plan !== null && plansByFpId.has(fp.plan);
        if (!instalment && !ours(fp, orderIds)) await this.unknown('mf_purchase', fp, investorId);
        continue;
      }
      const severity = purchaseDrift(fp.state, local.status);
      if (severity === 'NONE') continue;
      await ReconBreaks.open(db, {
        kind:
          severity === 'CRITICAL'
            ? RECON_FP_KINDS.ORDER_OUTCOME_DIFFERS
            : RECON_FP_KINDS.ORDER_STATE_UNEXPECTED,
        entityType: 'orders',
        entityId: local.id,
        severity,
        detail: { status: local.status, fpState: fp.state, source: 'recon.fp.daily' },
      });
    }

    for (const fp of fpPlans) {
      const local = plansByFpId.get(fp.id);
      if (local === undefined) {
        if (!ours(fp, planIds)) await this.unknown('mf_purchase_plan', fp, investorId);
        continue;
      }
      if (planDrift(fp.state, local.status)) {
        await ReconBreaks.open(db, {
          kind: RECON_FP_KINDS.PLAN_STATE_UNEXPECTED,
          entityType: 'plans',
          entityId: local.id,
          severity: 'WARNING',
          detail: { status: local.status, fpState: fp.state, source: 'recon.fp.daily' },
        });
      }
    }

    for (const fp of fpRedemptions) {
      if (!ordersByFpId.has(fp.id) && !ours(fp, orderIds)) {
        await this.unknown('mf_redemption', fp, investorId);
      }
    }

    const held = new Set(
      localFolios.flatMap((f) => (f.folioNumber === null ? [] : [f.folioNumber])),
    );
    for (const folioNumber of fpFolios) {
      if (held.has(folioNumber)) continue;
      await ReconBreaks.open(db, {
        kind: RECON_FP_KINDS.FOLIO_UNKNOWN,
        entityType: 'folios',
        entityId: `${investorId}:${folioNumber}`,
        severity: 'WARNING',
        detail: { investorId, folioNumber },
      });
    }
  }

  private async unknown(objectType: string, fp: FpObjectRef, investorId: string): Promise<void> {
    await ReconBreaks.open(this.dbh.db, {
      kind: RECON_FP_KINDS.FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN,
      entityType: objectType,
      entityId: fp.id,
      severity: 'CRITICAL',
      detail: { investorId, state: fp.state, sourceRefId: fp.sourceRefId },
    });
  }
}
```

```ts
import { type DynamicModule, Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { Env } from '../../../config/env.js';
import { IntegrityInvariantsJob } from './integrity-invariants.job.js';
import { ReconFpDailyJob } from './recon-fp-daily.job.js';

/** Both jobs run in the worker only: recon.fp.daily injects FpRead, which exists only there (FpModule). */
@Module({})
export class ReconModule {
  static forRoot(env: Env): DynamicModule {
    const workerOnly =
      env.SANCHAY_APP_ROLE === 'worker' ? [IntegrityInvariantsJob, ReconFpDailyJob] : [];
    return { module: ReconModule, providers: workerOnly };
  }
}
```

`apps/api/src/modules/orders/reconcile-nonfinal.job.ts` (E20's file as F5 left it; full content: F5's purchases-only filter becomes the per-type dispatch, and the redemption saga backstop, the redemption LOOKUP-ADOPT, and the plan and mandate branches are added):
```ts
import { Inject, Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import type { ConsentSubjectType, OrderStatus } from '@sanchay/domain';
import { and, desc, eq, inArray, isNotNull } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { DB, type DbHandle } from '../../db/client.js';
import { FpRead } from '../../integrations/fp/fp-read.js';
import { investors } from '../identity/identity.schema.js';
import type { ConsentApprovedJobData } from '../legal-consent/consent-engine.js';
import { consentChallenges, consentRecords } from '../legal-consent/legal-consent.schema.js';
import { mandates, plans } from '../plans/plans.schema.js';
import { AuditService } from '../platform/audit.service.js';
import { CLOCK, type Clock, MINUTE } from '../platform/clock.js';
import { type Job, JobHandler } from '../platform/jobs/job-registry.js';
import { Jobs } from '../platform/jobs/jobs.service.js';
import {
  fpObjectRef,
  redemptionAdoptTarget,
  redemptionResumeAction,
} from '../platform/recon/recon-rules.js';
import { ReconBreaks } from '../platform/runtime-config.js';
import { releaseReservation } from '../portfolio/reservations.js';
import { toFpPurchaseView } from './fp-purchase.js';
import { moveOrder } from './order-transitions.js';
import { orderEvents, orders } from './orders.schema.js';

const MISS_TRIGGER = 'fp.reconcile.nonfinal.miss';
const ABSENT_AFTER_MS = 10 * MINUTE;
/** F2's plans.sip.advance drives these; a lost job chain is re-enqueued here (its singletonKey dedupes). */
const ADVANCED_PLAN_STATUSES = ['UNDER_REVIEW', 'CONFIRMING', 'RECONCILING'] as const;
/** F5's orders.redemption.advance drives these (singletonKey = order id). */
const REDEMPTION_IN_REVIEW = ['UNDER_REVIEW', 'CONFIRMING'] as const;
/** Approved but not yet submitted: F5's orders.redemption.submit owns these (singletonKey = challenge id). */
const REDEMPTION_APPROVED = ['CONSENT_PENDING', 'CONSENTED'] as const;

type OrderRow = typeof orders.$inferSelect;

/**
 * Worker only, every 5 minutes: the backstop for every non-final aggregate (spec §4.1).
 * - Redemption sagas (F7): F5's jobs re-enqueue themselves, but a job whose pg-boss retries ran out leaves
 *   the order, and its ACTIVE reservation, where it stopped (the consent sweep only marks the challenge).
 *   UNDER_REVIEW/CONFIRMING get orders.redemption.advance again; an approved redemption gets
 *   orders.redemption.submit again while its consent is usable, or ends CONSENT_EXPIRED with its
 *   reservation released when it is not (`redemptionResumeAction`).
 * - RECONCILING purchases (E20, unchanged) and redemptions (F7): LOOKUP-ADOPT by source_ref_id (= order
 *   id); absent at two checks at least 10 minutes apart -> FAILED(PROVIDER_OBJECT_ABSENT). A redemption
 *   proven absent also releases its reservation in the same transaction (spec §4.4).
 * - Plans in review, confirmation or RECONCILING (F7): re-enqueue F2's plans.sip.advance, which adopts.
 * - RECONCILING mandates (F7): D3 has no FP list-by-bank read, so the CRITICAL MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS
 *   break F2 opened is kept open (re-opened if someone resolved it while the mandate is still stuck).
 * It emits no metric: F1's ops.gauges.emit reads recon_breaks and order_events directly.
 */
@Injectable()
@JobHandler('fp.reconcile.nonfinal')
export class ReconcileNonfinalJob {
  private readonly log = new Logger(ReconcileNonfinalJob.name);

  constructor(
    @Inject(DB) private readonly dbh: DbHandle,
    @Inject(FpRead) private readonly fpRead: FpRead,
    @Inject(CLOCK) private readonly clock: Clock,
    @Inject(Jobs) private readonly jobs: Jobs,
    @Inject(AuditService) private readonly audit: AuditService,
  ) {}

  async handle(_job: Job<'fp.reconcile.nonfinal'>): Promise<void> {
    await this.resumeRedemptions();
    await this.resumePurchases();
    const stuck = await this.dbh.db.select().from(orders).where(eq(orders.status, 'RECONCILING'));
    for (const order of stuck) {
      try {
        if (order.type === 'PURCHASE') await this.adoptPurchase(order);
        else await this.adoptRedemption(order);
      } catch (err) {
        // FP unreachable for this one: it stays RECONCILING and the next run retries.
        this.log.warn(
          `fp.reconcile.nonfinal: order ${order.id} (${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)})`,
        );
      }
    }
    await this.nudgePlans();
    await this.keepMandateBreaksOpen();
  }

  /**
   * RV-04-F7-6: hands a purchase whose `orders.purchase.advance` chain died back to E20's job. D2 retries
   * a failed job three times without a delay, so a short FP outage ended the chain and left the order in
   * UNDER_REVIEW or CONFIRMING for good. The queue is `stately`, keyed by the order id (R-32): a null
   * return means a chain is still queued, which is fine.
   */
  private async resumePurchases(): Promise<void> {
    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const stalled = await db
      .select({ id: orders.id, challengeId: orders.consentChallengeId })
      .from(orders)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(orders.type, 'PURCHASE'),
          inArray(orders.status, ['UNDER_REVIEW', 'CONFIRMING']),
          isNotNull(orders.consentChallengeId),
        ),
      );
    for (const order of stalled) {
      if (order.challengeId === null) continue;
      await this.jobs.enqueue(
        db,
        'orders.purchase.advance',
        { orderId: order.id, challengeId: order.challengeId },
        { singletonKey: order.id },
      );
    }
  }

  /** Hands every redemption F5's saga left mid-way back to F5's own jobs, or ends it (see the class note). */
  private async resumeRedemptions(): Promise<void> {
    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const inReview = await db
      .select({ id: orders.id, challengeId: orders.consentChallengeId })
      .from(orders)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(orders.type, 'REDEMPTION'),
          inArray(orders.status, [...REDEMPTION_IN_REVIEW]),
          isNotNull(orders.consentChallengeId),
        ),
      );
    for (const order of inReview) {
      if (order.challengeId === null) continue;
      await this.jobs.enqueue(
        db,
        'orders.redemption.advance',
        { orderId: order.id, challengeId: order.challengeId },
        { singletonKey: order.id },
      );
    }

    const approved = await db
      .select({
        orderId: orders.id,
        investorId: orders.investorId,
        challengeId: consentChallenges.id,
        challengeStatus: consentChallenges.status,
        recordId: consentRecords.id,
        subjectType: consentRecords.subjectType,
        subjectIds: consentRecords.subjectIds,
        consumedAt: consentRecords.consumedAt,
        executeBefore: consentRecords.executeBefore,
        sagaExpiresAt: consentRecords.sagaExpiresAt,
        firstAttemptAt: consentRecords.firstAttemptAt,
      })
      .from(orders)
      .innerJoin(consentChallenges, eq(consentChallenges.id, orders.consentChallengeId))
      .innerJoin(
        consentRecords,
        and(
          eq(consentRecords.challengeId, consentChallenges.id),
          eq(consentRecords.kind, 'CHALLENGE'),
        ),
      )
      .where(
        and(
          eq(orders.type, 'REDEMPTION'),
          inArray(orders.status, [...REDEMPTION_APPROVED]),
          inArray(consentChallenges.status, ['CONSUMED', 'CONSUMED_UNUSED']),
        ),
      );
    const now = this.clock.now();
    for (const row of approved) {
      const action = redemptionResumeAction({ ...row, now });
      if (action === 'WAIT') continue;
      if (action === 'EXPIRE') {
        await this.expireApproved(row.orderId, now);
        continue;
      }
      // The data approve enqueued (E4): the submit job re-reads the order and returns unless it is approved.
      const data: ConsentApprovedJobData = {
        challengeId: row.challengeId,
        recordId: row.recordId,
        investorId: row.investorId,
        subjectType: row.subjectType as ConsentSubjectType,
        subjectIds: (row.subjectIds ?? []).map((s) => s.id),
      };
      await this.jobs.enqueue(db, 'orders.redemption.submit', data, {
        singletonKey: row.challengeId,
      });
    }
  }

  /**
   * F5's own CONSENT_EXPIRED path ('execute_before_missed', evidence 'consent_expired'): useConsumed would
   * refuse this consent, so no FP write can follow and the units are free again. The row is locked and
   * re-read, so a submit attempt that moved it on meanwhile is left alone.
   */
  private async expireApproved(orderId: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
    await this.dbh.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      const [locked] = await tx
        .select({ id: orders.id, status: orders.status })
        .from(orders)
        .where(eq(orders.id, orderId))
        .for('update');
      if (locked === undefined) return;
      let current: { id: string; status: OrderStatus } = locked;
      if (current.status === 'CONSENT_PENDING') {
        await moveOrder(tx, current, 'CONSENTED', 'approve');
        current = { id: orderId, status: 'CONSENTED' };
      }
      if (current.status !== 'CONSENTED') return;
      await moveOrder(tx, current, 'CONSENT_EXPIRED', 'execute_before_missed', { finalAt: now });
      await releaseReservation(tx, this.audit, { orderId, evidence: 'consent_expired', now });
    });
  }

  /**
   * E20's rule, kept (RV-04-F7-4): the adopted purchase goes back to UNDER_REVIEW and, in the same
   * transaction, to E20's orders.purchase.advance (stately, singletonKey = order id; null means one is
   * already queued), which runs the H-2 checkout from there. F4's mf_purchase handler leaves orders before
   * PROCESSING to the saga jobs, so nothing else would move it on.
   */
  private async adoptPurchase(order: OrderRow): Promise<void> {
    const { items } = await this.fpRead.purchases({ sourceRefId: order.id });
    const found = items[0];
    if (found === undefined) return this.recordMiss(order);
    const purchase = toFpPurchaseView(found);
    await this.dbh.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await moveOrder(tx, order, 'UNDER_REVIEW', 'lookup_adopt_mapped', {
        fpOrderId: purchase.id,
        fpOldId: purchase.oldId,
        fpState: purchase.state,
      });
      if (order.consentChallengeId !== null) {
        await this.jobs.enqueue(
          tx,
          'orders.purchase.advance',
          { orderId: order.id, challengeId: order.consentChallengeId },
          { singletonKey: order.id },
        );
      }
    });
  }

  /**
   * D3's FpRead.redemptions lists by investment account, so the source_ref_id match is made here. The
   * adopted order goes to its mapped state: in review it rejoins F5's orders.redemption.advance;
   * submitted or successful it waits for F5's settlement sweep (orders.units.reconcile); a terminal FP
   * state ends it and releases the reservation on that provider evidence.
   */
  private async adoptRedemption(order: OrderRow): Promise<void> {
    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const [investor] = await db
      .select({ mfia: investors.fpMfInvestmentAccountId })
      .from(investors)
      .where(eq(investors.id, order.investorId));
    const mfia = investor?.mfia ?? null;
    if (mfia === null) throw new Error('redemption investor has no FP investment account');
    const { items } = await this.fpRead.redemptions({ mfInvestmentAccount: mfia });
    const found = items.map(fpObjectRef).find((r) => r.sourceRefId === order.id);
    if (found === undefined) return this.recordMiss(order);
    const to = redemptionAdoptTarget(found.state);
    if (to === null) {
      await ReconBreaks.open(db, {
        kind: 'FP_ORDER_STATE_UNEXPECTED',
        entityType: 'orders',
        entityId: order.id,
        severity: 'WARNING',
        detail: { status: order.status, fpState: found.state },
      });
      return;
    }
    const now = this.clock.now();
    const terminal = to === 'FAILED' || to === 'EXPIRED' || to === 'CANCELLED';
    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await moveOrder(tx, order, to, 'lookup_adopt_mapped', {
        fpOrderId: found.id,
        fpOldId: found.oldId,
        fpState: found.state,
        ...(terminal ? { finalAt: now } : {}),
      });
      if (terminal) {
        await releaseReservation(tx, this.audit, {
          orderId: order.id,
          evidence: `fp_${found.state}:${found.id}`,
          now,
        });
      } else if (
        (to === 'UNDER_REVIEW' || to === 'CONFIRMING') &&
        order.consentChallengeId !== null
      ) {
        await this.jobs.enqueue(
          tx,
          'orders.redemption.advance',
          { orderId: order.id, challengeId: order.consentChallengeId },
          { singletonKey: order.id },
        );
      }
    });
  }

  private async recordMiss(order: OrderRow): Promise<void> {
    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const [lastMiss] = await db
      .select()
      .from(orderEvents)
      .where(and(eq(orderEvents.orderId, order.id), eq(orderEvents.trigger, MISS_TRIGGER)))
      .orderBy(desc(orderEvents.occurredAt))
      .limit(1);
    const now = this.clock.now();
    if (lastMiss === undefined) {
      await db.insert(orderEvents).values({
        orderId: order.id,
        fromStatus: order.status,
        toStatus: order.status,
        trigger: MISS_TRIGGER,
        occurredAt: now,
      });
      return;
    }
    if (now.getTime() - lastMiss.occurredAt.getTime() < ABSENT_AFTER_MS) return;
    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await moveOrder(tx, order, 'FAILED', 'provider_object_absent', {
        failureCode: 'PROVIDER_OBJECT_ABSENT',
        finalAt: now,
      });
      // FP proved the object absent (spec §4.4). The challenge stays CONSUMED: the submit job's attempt
      // stamped first_attempt_at, so markUnused (only when no P/M write happened) does not apply.
      if (order.type === 'REDEMPTION') {
        await releaseReservation(tx, this.audit, {
          orderId: order.id,
          evidence: 'provider_object_absent',
          now,
        });
      }
    });
  }

  private async nudgePlans(): Promise<void> {
    const db = this.dbh.db;
    const live = await db
      .select({ id: plans.id, challengeId: plans.consentChallengeId })
      .from(plans)
      .where(
        and(
          inArray(plans.status, [...ADVANCED_PLAN_STATUSES]),
          isNotNull(plans.consentChallengeId),
        ),
      );
    for (const plan of live) {
      if (plan.challengeId === null) continue;
      await this.jobs.enqueue(
        db,
        'plans.sip.advance',
        { planId: plan.id, challengeId: plan.challengeId },
        { singletonKey: plan.id },
      );
    }
  }

  private async keepMandateBreaksOpen(): Promise<void> {
    const stuck = await this.dbh.db
      .select({ id: mandates.id, bankAccountId: mandates.bankAccountId })
      .from(mandates)
      .where(eq(mandates.status, 'RECONCILING'));
    for (const mandate of stuck) {
      await ReconBreaks.open(this.dbh.db, {
        kind: 'MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS',
        entityType: 'mandates',
        entityId: mandate.id,
        severity: 'CRITICAL',
        detail: { bankAccountId: mandate.bankAccountId },
      });
    }
  }
}
```

`apps/api/src/integrations/fp/fake/fake-fp.ts` (D4's file as F2 left it; replace the `purchase.list` case). FP filters `GET /v2/mf_purchases` by `mf_investment_account`; without it every investor's FakeFp purchases would appear under each account in `recon.fp.daily`:
```ts
      case 'purchase.list': {
        const sourceRefId = query.get('source_ref_id');
        const plan = query.get('plan');
        const account = query.get('mf_investment_account');
        const bySource =
          sourceRefId === null
            ? [...this.state.purchases.values()]
            : this.state.findPurchasesBySourceRefId(sourceRefId);
        const items = bySource.filter(
          (p) =>
            (plan === null || p.plan === plan) &&
            (account === null || p.mfInvestmentAccount === account),
        );
        return { statusCode: 200, data: { object: 'list', data: items.map(purchasePayload) } };
      }
```

  ```json
  "ops:nav-release": "nest build -b swc && node dist/cli/ops.js ops:nav-release"
  ```
- root `package.json` (append under `scripts`; D7's `ops:invite` and D9's `ops:nav-release` root scripts already delegate and stay as they are):
  ```json
  "ops:sync": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:sync",
  "ops:kill-switch": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:kill-switch",
  "ops:sip-switch": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:sip-switch",
  "ops:refund-utr": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:refund-utr",
  "ops:payout-ref": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:payout-ref",
  "ops:resolve-break": "pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api ops:resolve-break"
  ```

`docs/runbooks/ops-cli.md`:
````markdown
# Runbook: ops CLIs and read-only views (R-16, spec §4.6)

Every ops command runs as `SANCHAY_APP_ROLE=ops`. The process pins its database session to `sanchay_app`
(no DDL) and refuses to start if that role could run DDL. It starts no HTTP listener and no job worker,
holds no FP client, and never writes an order, plan or mandate status. Every command writes one
`audit_events` row (R-20); `ops:invite` writes one per invited mobile. A mobile number never goes on a
command line: a deployed `ops:invite` reads its list from an SSM SecureString that you delete after the
run (see "Inviting pilot investors" below).

## Commands

| Command | Who | What it writes |
|---|---|---|
| `ops:sync --order <order-id> --by <handle>` | one operator | a re-fetch request (`inbound_webhook_events`, `event_type = 'ops.sync'`) and one `fp.event.process` job, or one `fp.reconcile.nonfinal` job for a RECONCILING order |
| `ops:kill-switch --off --by <handle> --reason <text>` | one operator | `app_config` `orders.enabled = false`: new purchases and redemptions are refused |
| `ops:kill-switch --on --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle> --reason <text>` | two founders | `app_config` `orders.enabled = true` |
| `ops:sip-switch --off --by <handle> --reason <text>` | one operator | `app_config` `plans.sip.enabled = false`: new SIPs are refused |
| `ops:sip-switch --on --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle> --reason <text>` | two founders | `app_config` `plans.sip.enabled = true` (GO-2, R-06) |
| `ops:refund-utr --order <order-id> --utr <utr> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>` | two founders | the payment attempt's `refund_status = 'REFUNDED'`, `refund_ref`, `refund_recorded_at` |
| `ops:payout-ref --order <order-id> --ref <bank-ref> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>` | two founders | the settled redemption's `payout_ref` and `payout_updated_at` (evidence only: `payout.watch` marks it CREDITED at 10:00 IST) |
| `ops:invite --mobiles-param /sanchay/{env}/invites/<name> --by <handle> [--note <text>]` (deployed) or `ops:invite --mobiles-file <path> --by <handle> [--note <text>]` (local) | one founder | one 30-day `pilot_invites` row (blind index only) per listed mobile, all or none; prints each mobile as `******` and its last 4 digits |
| `ops:nav-release --isin <isin> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>` | two founders | `scheme_navs.quarantined = false` for a quarantined NAV; the next NAV sync takes the ISIN's feed value once, without the 25% check (R-35) |
| `ops:resolve-break --id <break-id> --note <text> --approver1 <handle> --approver2 <handle>` | two founders | the recon break's `status = 'RESOLVED'`; refused for `INVARIANT_*` breaks and for `MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS` while its mandate is RECONCILING |

Handles are lower-case operator ids (for example `f.anita`), never names or emails: they land in
`audit_events.actor_id`. `--off` is never blocked on a second person; anything that turns money flow back
on, or records money evidence, needs two different founders.

What each command leaves in `app.v_ops_audit` (filter on `action`, then `entity_id`):

| Command | `action` | `entity_type` | `entity_id` | `reason` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ops:sync` | `OPS_SYNC_REQUESTED` | `orders` | the order id | |
| `ops:kill-switch` | `OPS_KILL_SWITCH` | `app_config` | `orders.enabled` | `--reason` |
| `ops:sip-switch` | `OPS_SIP_SWITCH` | `app_config` | `plans.sip.enabled` | `--reason` |
| `ops:refund-utr` | `OPS_REFUND_UTR_RECORDED` | `payment_attempts` | the payment attempt id | |
| `ops:payout-ref` | `OPS_PAYOUT_REF_RECORDED` | `orders` | the order id | |
| `ops:invite` | `PILOT_INVITE_ADDED` | `pilot_invite` | the invite id (one row per invited mobile) | |
| `ops:nav-release` | `NAV_RELEASE` | `scheme_navs` | the ISIN | |
| `ops:resolve-break` | `OPS_BREAK_RESOLVED` | `recon_breaks` | the break id | `--note` |

The `actor_id` is `--by`, or `--approver1` for a two-founder command.

## When to use which

| Signal | Action |
|---|---|
| Alarm `sanchay-prod-reconciling-sla` (an order, plan or mandate RECONCILING for more than 2 h) | `SELECT * FROM app.v_reconciling_orders ORDER BY reconciling_since;`. Look each one up in the FP dashboard. An order: `ops:sync --order <id> --by <handle>` re-drives LOOKUP-ADOPT. A plan: `fp.reconcile.nonfinal` re-drives it every 5 minutes. A mandate: its `MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS` break stays open; chase Cybrilla. |
| Alarm `sanchay-prod-money-invariant-breach` and the break kind starts with `INVARIANT_` (M1-M4, reservations) | `ops:kill-switch --off` first (and `ops:sip-switch --off` if a plan or mandate is involved), then investigate with the views. The break resolves itself on the next hourly `integrity.invariants` run once the data is right. |
| Alarm `sanchay-prod-money-invariant-breach` with any other kind (`RECON_FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN`, `RECON_ORDER_OUTCOME_DIFFERS`, `LEDGER_UNITS_SHORTFALL`, `REDEMPTION_EXIT_INVALID`, `REDEMPTION_REVERSED`, `MANDATE_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS`, `PLAN_CANCEL_UNRESOLVED`, …) | Freeze first if money may be wrong. Investigate (FP dashboard, Cybrilla). Once it is dealt with: `ops:resolve-break --id <break-id> --note <what was done> --approver1 <a> --approver2 <b>`. The alarm returns to OK at its next 5-minute evaluation once no CRITICAL break is open, so it pages again on the next one. |
| `RECON_FP_OBJECT_UNKNOWN` (an FP object we never placed) | `ops:kill-switch --off`, then investigate with Cybrilla. |
| `UNITS_PENDING_T3`/`UNITS_PENDING_T5`, a row in `v_units_pending`, PROCESSING beyond T+2 | Look the order up in the FP dashboard, then `ops:sync --order <id> --by <handle>`. Chase Cybrilla. |
| `RECON_ORDER_OUTCOME_DIFFERS` or `FP_ORDER_STATE_UNEXPECTED` from `recon.fp.daily` | `ops:sync --order <id> --by <handle>`; if the break stays, escalate. |
| Refund confirmed by the AMC with a UTR | `ops:refund-utr` with two founders. |
| Investor or AMC confirms a redemption payout reached the bank (FP has no `bank_credit_reference`) | `ops:payout-ref` with two founders; `payout.watch` credits it on its next run. |
| A quarantined NAV, after checking it on the AMC site | `ops:nav-release` with two founders; the next NAV sync accepts the feed value once (R-35). |
| GO-2 decided, or SIPs must pause | `ops:sip-switch --on` (two founders) or `ops:sip-switch --off` (one operator). |
| Pilot invitees from the PO's list (G-B11; only after the GO-1 decision, R-31), or the founders' own numbers before the canary | "Inviting pilot investors" below: put the list in an SSM SecureString, run `ops:invite --mobiles-param /sanchay/{env}/invites/<name> --by <handle> --note <list name>`, then delete the parameter. |

## Running a command locally

From the repo root, against the database in `apps/api/.env` (the script builds the api first, then runs
`node dist/cli/ops.js`, which forces `SANCHAY_APP_ROLE=ops`; no environment variable is needed). The same
line works in PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash:

```
pnpm ops:kill-switch --off --by ops.local --reason smoke
```

`ops:invite` never takes a mobile on the command line. Locally, write the list in an editor to a file
outside the repo (one 10-digit mobile per line, nothing else) and pass its absolute path (the script runs
in `apps/api`, so a relative path resolves from there). `--mobiles-file` works only when `SANCHAY_APP_ENV`
is `local` or `test`:

```
pnpm ops:invite --mobiles-file C:/Users/<you>/invites-local.txt --by ops.local --note local-test
```

Every command has a root script of the same name (`pnpm ops:sync`, `pnpm ops:kill-switch`,
`pnpm ops:sip-switch`, `pnpm ops:refund-utr`, `pnpm ops:payout-ref`, `pnpm ops:invite`,
`pnpm ops:nav-release`, `pnpm ops:resolve-break`). A command without a script runs from a build:

```
pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api build
pnpm --filter=@sanchay/api exec node dist/cli/ops.js ops:<command> <flags>
```

Exit codes: 0 done (one result line on stdout), 1 refused (one line on stderr naming the reason; nothing
was written), 2 usage (the usage text).

## Running a command in a deployed environment (the one form)

Every deployed ops run is a one-off ECS task on F1's **ops task definition**, family `sanchay-{env}-ops`
(D6). It has container `ops` on the api image, with `SANCHAY_APP_ROLE=ops` already in its environment. It
logs in as `sanchay_app_login` (secret `sanchay/{env}/db-app`) and carries the keyring, but no FP,
FP-webhook or MSG91 secret. Its task role may read only the SSM parameters under
`/sanchay/{env}/invites/`.

Never run an ops command on the migrate task definition `sanchay-{env}-migrate`, because it logs in as the
RDS master `sanchay_master`. Other runbooks copy this form and change only the `command` array. Prod is
the only deployed environment (R-31; RV-04-F7-3), so the commands below name it.

1. Read the stack outputs once (`AppSubnetIds`, `ServiceSecurityGroupId`; `OpsTaskDefinitionArn` names the
   ops task definition's current revision, which is what `--task-definition sanchay-prod-ops` runs):

   ```
   aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name SanchayMvpStack-prod --query "Stacks[0].Outputs" --output table
   ```

2. Write `ops-overrides.json` outside the repo, in an editor, saved as UTF-8 (PowerShell 5.1's `>`
   writes UTF-16, which `file://` cannot read). Override only `command`; the container already runs as
   `SANCHAY_APP_ROLE=ops`. This example freezes orders:

   ```json
   {
     "containerOverrides": [
       {
         "name": "ops",
         "command": ["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:kill-switch", "--off", "--by", "<your-handle>", "--reason", "<why>"]
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

   For another command only `command` changes: `["node", "dist/main.js", "<ops:command>", "<flag>",
   "<value>", …]`, one array element per flag and per value, using exactly the flags in the table above
   (a value with spaces stays one element). For example:

   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:sync", "--order", "<order-id>", "--by", "<handle>"]`
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:kill-switch", "--on", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>", "--reason", "<text>"]`
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:sip-switch", "--on", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>", "--reason", "<text>"]`
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:refund-utr", "--order", "<order-id>", "--utr", "<utr>", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>"]`
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:payout-ref", "--order", "<order-id>", "--ref", "<bank-ref>", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>"]`
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:invite", "--mobiles-param", "/sanchay/prod/invites/<name>", "--by", "<handle>", "--note", "<text>"]` (only after the SSM step in "Inviting pilot investors"; never a mobile in this file)
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:nav-release", "--isin", "<isin>", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>"]`
   - `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:resolve-break", "--id", "<break-id>", "--note", "<text>", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>"]`

3. Run it (same line in both shells; it prints the task ARN):

   ```
   aws ecs run-task --cluster sanchay-prod --launch-type FARGATE --task-definition sanchay-prod-ops --network-configuration "awsvpcConfiguration={subnets=[<AppSubnetIds>],securityGroups=[<ServiceSecurityGroupId>],assignPublicIp=DISABLED}" --overrides file://ops-overrides.json --query "tasks[0].taskArn" --output text
   ```

4. Wait for it and read the exit code (0 done, 1 refused, 2 usage):

   ```
   aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster sanchay-prod --tasks <task-arn>
   aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster sanchay-prod --tasks <task-arn> --query "tasks[0].containers[0].exitCode" --output text
   ```

5. Read the result line. The log stream is `prod/ops/<task-id>` (the task id is the last part of the task
   ARN) in `/sanchay/prod/app`.

   PowerShell:
   ```
   aws logs get-log-events --log-group-name /sanchay/prod/app --log-stream-name prod/ops/<task-id> --query "events[].message" --output text
   ```
   Git Bash (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` stops Git Bash rewriting the log group into a Windows path):
   ```
   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws logs get-log-events --log-group-name /sanchay/prod/app --log-stream-name prod/ops/<task-id> --query "events[].message" --output text
   ```

A refusal (wrong approvers, nothing to re-fetch, no refund in progress, an invite that already exists)
writes nothing. If the task exits 1 with `R-16: refusing to run an ops command`, the database login can
run DDL: do not work around it; fix the login (D6).

## Inviting pilot investors (`ops:invite` in a deployed environment)

A mobile number never goes in `ops-overrides.json`: CloudTrail keeps RunTask's
`containerOverrides.command`, and the ECS console shows it on stopped tasks. The list goes in an SSM
SecureString that only the ops task role may read, and you delete it as soon as the run is over.
CloudTrail records the parameter's name, never a SecureString's value. `--mobiles-file` is refused here;
it is for local and test only.

1. Write the list in an editor (Notepad's default UTF-8 is fine) to a file outside the repo, for example
   `invites.txt`. Put one 10-digit mobile per line (`+91` and spaces are accepted) and nothing else: no
   names. A list holds at most 300 numbers. A file written with PowerShell 5.1's `>` or `Out-File` is
   UTF-16: either the AWS CLI or `ops:invite` refuses it, and nothing is invited.

2. From the folder that holds the file, put the list as a SecureString. `<name>` uses lower-case letters,
   digits, `.`, `_` or `-` (for example `pilot-2026-11`). Without `--key-id`, SSM encrypts the value with
   the AWS managed key `alias/aws/ssm`, which the ops task role can use through SSM.

   PowerShell:
   ```
   aws ssm put-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/<name> --type SecureString --value file://invites.txt
   ```
   Git Bash (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` stops Git Bash rewriting `/sanchay/...` into a Windows path):
   ```
   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/<name> --type SecureString --value file://invites.txt
   ```

3. Run steps 2 to 5 of the deployed form with this `command`:
   `["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:invite", "--mobiles-param", "/sanchay/prod/invites/<name>", "--by", "<your-handle>", "--note", "<list name>"]`.
   - Exit 0 prints `ops:invite: invited ******<last4>, … (expires <ISO>)`: every listed mobile is invited.
   - Exit 1 means nothing was written. Either a listed mobile already has an invite (it is named by its
     last 4 digits), or a line is not a mobile (its line number is named, never its value), or the
     parameter does not exist.

4. Whatever the exit code, delete the parameter, then check that nothing is left under the prefix (the
   second command prints nothing). Deleting a parameter removes every version of it.

   PowerShell:
   ```
   aws ssm delete-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/<name>
   aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters "Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/sanchay/prod/invites/" --query "Parameters[].Name" --output text
   ```
   Git Bash:
   ```
   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm delete-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/<name>
   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters "Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/sanchay/prod/invites/" --query "Parameters[].Name" --output text
   ```

   To fix a refused list, correct the local file, put it under a new `<name>`, run again and delete
   again. Delete `invites.txt` once the invites are in.

5. Check the result over SSM as `sanchay_readonly_login`: `app.v_pilot_invites_count` (`LIVE` rises by the
   number invited) and `app.v_ops_audit` (one `PILOT_INVITE_ADDED` row per invited mobile).

## Read-only investigation views (`sanchay_readonly`, over SSM)

Connect as `sanchay_readonly_login` (secret `sanchay/{env}/db-readonly`, D6) through the SSM port-forward,
then:

```sql
SELECT * FROM app.v_reconciling_orders ORDER BY reconciling_since;
SELECT * FROM app.v_units_pending ORDER BY units_pending_since;
SELECT * FROM app.v_recon_breaks_open ORDER BY severity, created_at;
SELECT * FROM app.v_payouts_due ORDER BY payout_due_by;
SELECT * FROM app.v_ops_audit WHERE action = 'OPS_KILL_SWITCH' ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 20;
SELECT * FROM app.v_pilot_invites_count ORDER BY status;
```

`v_reconciling_orders.reconciling_since` follows F1's gauge: the latest real move into RECONCILING (the
5-minute `fp.reconcile.nonfinal.miss` self-events do not reset it). `v_ops_audit` holds the ADMIN rows of
`audit_events` without their `data`, IP or user agent. `v_pilot_invites_count` always has three rows:
`LIVE`, `USED` and `EXPIRED`.

`sanchay_readonly` can read these six views and nothing else in schema `app`: no `*_enc`, `*_bidx`,
contact, bank, IP or reference column is reachable (`ops-views.int.test.ts`).
````

**For F1 (BRIEF D6, ROUND2) and the assembler: the ops task definition and its one SSM grant.**

F1 defines `OpsTaskDef` (re-read in `p4tasks/F1.md` on 2026-10-01):
- family `sanchay-{env}-ops`, Fargate ARM64;
- one container `ops` on the api image, with the app log driver (stream prefix `{env}`);
- `environment`: `bootEnv`, `SANCHAY_DB_USER: 'sanchay_app_login'` and `SANCHAY_APP_ROLE: 'ops'`;
- `secrets`: `SANCHAY_DB_PASSWORD` from `sanchay/{env}/db-app` (field `password`) and `SANCHAY_KEYRING_JSON`, and no FP, FP-webhook or MSG91 secret;
- default command `["node", "dist/main.js"]`, which prints the usage and exits 2;
- stack output `OpsTaskDefinitionArn`.

The deployed form above runs it by family, with no environment override.

FR-21 adds one requirement for F1. The ops task's task role (the role CDK creates for `OpsTaskDef`, or an explicit one) gets exactly one SSM statement: `ssm:GetParameter` on `arn:aws:ssm:<region>:<account>:parameter/sanchay/{env}/invites/*`, and nothing else in SSM. For example: `opsTaskDef.addToTaskRolePolicy(new iam.PolicyStatement({ actions: ['ssm:GetParameter'], resources: [this.formatArn({ service: 'ssm', resource: 'parameter', resourceName: 'sanchay/<env>/invites/*' })] }))`.
- No KMS statement is needed: the SecureStrings use the AWS managed key `alias/aws/ssm`, which any principal in the account may use through SSM.
- ECS sets `AWS_REGION` and `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI` in a Fargate container (platform 1.4+), and `opsInputsFor` reads both.
- F1 may also put `AWS_REGION: this.region` in the ops container's `environment`, so the region never depends on the platform. Without a region the command refuses: `--mobiles-param needs AWS_REGION`.

A run uses the service security group, the only one the database accepts. If F1 names the family, the container or the output differently, only `docs/runbooks/ops-cli.md` and this task's Produces line change.

It also closes a second E2 gap: with `.env.example`'s identical app and api hostnames, E2 classified every request as APP and 404'd the webhook and payment returns locally. E2's own case "an ordinary (non-infra) route on the api host is 404" sends only a `Host` header; under H-1 that request reaches ClientGuard (403 `ORIGIN_REJECTED`), so Step 1 rewrites it to send the web client, which both rules refuse (EF8-6).
  2. **The matrix is swept, not listed.** `hostguard.int.test.ts` reads every registered route (`listRoutes`) and asserts HostGuard's own decision through a spy on `HostGuard.prototype.canActivate` (4 hosts × 3 request shapes per route), so a 404 from a handler is never mistaken for a HostGuard refusal and a route added later is covered without editing the file. The outline's 8 rows are kept as named cases.
  3. **The OTP lockout answers `429 RATE_LIMITED`, not `OTP_LOCKED`.** That is what B13's `assertNotLockedOut` throws on issue (with `retryAfterSeconds`); `OTP_LOCKED` (401) is the verify-side answer for the 5th wrong code, and the suite asserts both.
  4. **`prod-image-guard` builds its prod baseline from `testEnv`'s parsed output**, so a required key a later task adds (E20's `SANCHAY_PLATFORM_ARN`, for example) is inherited without editing this file, and it first proves that baseline boots, so each refusal is caused by its one changed key.

`apps/api/test/int/security/routes.ts` (test support, consumed by `hostguard.int.test.ts` and by F9):
```ts
import { type INestApplication, RequestMethod } from '@nestjs/common';
import { METHOD_METADATA, PATH_METADATA } from '@nestjs/common/constants.js';
import { ModulesContainer, Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import {
  INFRA_ROUTE,
  type InfraRouteHosts,
  IS_PUBLIC,
} from '../../../src/modules/platform/http-decorators.js';

export type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';

export interface AppRoute {
  /** `Controller.handler`, for failure messages. */
  name: string;
  method: HttpMethod;
  /** Nest pattern without the `/api/v1` prefix, e.g. `/orders/:id`. */
  path: string;
  /** `@Public()` on the handler or its class (SessionGuard skips it). */
  isPublic: boolean;
  /** `@InfraRoute(...)` scope, or null for an ordinary route. */
  infra: InfraRouteHosts | null;
}

const METHODS: Partial<Record<RequestMethod, HttpMethod>> = {
  [RequestMethod.GET]: 'GET',
  [RequestMethod.POST]: 'POST',
  [RequestMethod.PUT]: 'PUT',
  [RequestMethod.PATCH]: 'PATCH',
  [RequestMethod.DELETE]: 'DELETE',
};

function pathsOf(meta: unknown): string[] {
  if (Array.isArray(meta)) return meta.filter((p): p is string => typeof p === 'string');
  return typeof meta === 'string' ? [meta] : ['/'];
}

function join(...parts: string[]): string {
  const joined = parts
    .flatMap((p) => p.split('/'))
    .filter((s) => s.length > 0)
    .join('/');
  return `/${joined}`;
}

/**
 * Every HTTP handler the booted app registered, read from Nest's own metadata: the same
 * `@Public()` and `@InfraRoute()` keys SessionGuard and HostGuard read. `@Implement(contract.x.y)`
 * (oRPC) registers through Nest's `@Get/@Post`, so contract procedures and raw controllers are
 * enumerated alike. Nothing here is a hand-maintained list.
 */
export function listRoutes(app: INestApplication): AppRoute[] {
  const reflector = new Reflector();
  const routes: AppRoute[] = [];
  for (const mod of app.get(ModulesContainer).values()) {
    for (const wrapper of mod.controllers.values()) {
      const cls = wrapper.metatype;
      if (typeof cls !== 'function') continue;
      const proto = cls.prototype as Record<string, unknown>;
      for (const key of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(proto)) {
        if (key === 'constructor') continue;
        const handler = proto[key];
        if (typeof handler !== 'function') continue;
        const method = METHODS[Reflect.getMetadata(METHOD_METADATA, handler) as RequestMethod];
        const handlerPath: unknown = Reflect.getMetadata(PATH_METADATA, handler);
        if (method === undefined || handlerPath === undefined) continue;
        const targets = [handler, cls];
        const isPublic =
          reflector.getAllAndOverride<boolean | undefined>(IS_PUBLIC, targets) === true;
        const infra =
          reflector.getAllAndOverride<InfraRouteHosts | undefined>(INFRA_ROUTE, targets) ?? null;
        for (const base of pathsOf(Reflect.getMetadata(PATH_METADATA, cls))) {
          for (const sub of pathsOf(handlerPath)) {
            routes.push({
              name: `${cls.name}.${key}`,
              method,
              path: join(base, sub),
              isPublic,
              infra,
            });
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return routes;
}

/** A concrete `/api/v1/...` URL for a route pattern, every `:param`/`*param` filled with `value`. */
export function urlOf(
  route: Pick<AppRoute, 'path'>,
  value = '0199a0b2-3c4d-7e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b',
): string {
  return `/api/v1${route.path.replace(/[:*]\w+/g, value)}`;
}
```

```ts
import type { ExecutionContext } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { AppConfig } from '../../config/app-config.js';
import type { Env } from '../../config/env.js';
import { AppError } from './errors.js';
import { HostGuard, ordinaryRouteAllowed, type PresentedClient } from './host.guard.js';
import { InfraRoute } from './http-decorators.js';

const WEB: PresentedClient = { client: 'web', bearer: false };
const NATIVE: PresentedClient = { client: 'android', bearer: true };
const BARE: PresentedClient = { client: undefined, bearer: false };

describe('ordinaryRouteAllowed (H-1)', () => {
  it.each([
    ['APP', WEB, true],
    ['APP', NATIVE, false],
    ['APP', { client: 'android', bearer: false }, false],
    ['APP', { client: 'web', bearer: true }, false],
    ['APP', BARE, true],
    ['API', WEB, false],
    ['API', { client: 'web', bearer: true }, false],
    ['API', NATIVE, true],
    ['API', { client: 'android', bearer: false }, true],
    ['API', BARE, true],
    [null, WEB, false],
    [null, NATIVE, false],
    [null, BARE, false],
  ] as const)('%s host, %j -> %s', (host, presented, allowed) => {
    expect(ordinaryRouteAllowed(host, presented)).toBe(allowed);
  });
});

class Routes {
  ordinary(): void {}
  @InfraRoute('API_HOST')
  webhook(): void {}
  @InfraRoute('APP_AND_API_HOSTS')
  health(): void {}
}

const guard = new HostGuard(
  new Reflector(),
  new AppConfig({
    SANCHAY_APP_ORIGIN: 'https://app.sanchay.in',
    SANCHAY_API_ORIGIN: 'https://api.sanchay.in',
  } as Env),
);

function contextFor(handler: () => void, headers: Record<string, string>): ExecutionContext {
  return {
    getHandler: () => handler,
    getClass: () => Routes,
    switchToHttp: () => ({ getRequest: () => ({ headers }) }),
  } as unknown as ExecutionContext;
}

function decide(handler: () => void, headers: Record<string, string>): 'pass' | 'NOT_FOUND' {
  try {
    guard.canActivate(contextFor(handler, headers));
    return 'pass';
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof AppError) return e.code as 'NOT_FOUND';
    throw e;
  }
}

describe('HostGuard', () => {
  const p = Routes.prototype;
  const web = { 'x-sanchay-client': 'web', cookie: '__Host-sanchay_sid=x' };
  const native = { 'x-sanchay-client': 'android', authorization: `Bearer ${'x'.repeat(43)}` };

  it.each([
    ['app.sanchay.in', web, 'pass'],
    ['app.sanchay.in', native, 'NOT_FOUND'],
    ['api.sanchay.in', web, 'NOT_FOUND'],
    ['api.sanchay.in:443', native, 'pass'],
    ['API.SANCHAY.IN', native, 'pass'],
    ['evil.example.com', web, 'NOT_FOUND'],
  ] as const)('ordinary route on %s with %j -> %s', (host, headers, expected) => {
    expect(decide(p.ordinary, { host, ...headers })).toBe(expected);
  });

  it('an ordinary route with no Host header is NOT_FOUND', () => {
    expect(decide(p.ordinary, web)).toBe('NOT_FOUND');
  });

  it('an API_HOST infra route passes only on the api host, whatever the request presents', () => {
    expect(decide(p.webhook, { host: 'api.sanchay.in' })).toBe('pass');
    expect(decide(p.webhook, { host: 'api.sanchay.in', ...web })).toBe('pass');
    expect(decide(p.webhook, { host: 'app.sanchay.in' })).toBe('NOT_FOUND');
    expect(decide(p.webhook, {})).toBe('NOT_FOUND');
  });

  it('local development: when both origins share a hostname, it acts as either host', () => {
    const local = new HostGuard(
      new Reflector(),
      new AppConfig({
        SANCHAY_APP_ORIGIN: 'http://localhost:3001',
        SANCHAY_API_ORIGIN: 'http://localhost:3000',
      } as Env),
    );
    const run = (handler: () => void, headers: Record<string, string>) => {
      try {
        local.canActivate(contextFor(handler, { host: 'localhost:3000', ...headers }));
        return 'pass';
      } catch (e) {
        return e instanceof AppError ? e.code : 'other';
      }
    };
    expect(run(p.ordinary, web)).toBe('pass');
    expect(run(p.ordinary, native)).toBe('pass');
    expect(run(p.webhook, {})).toBe('pass');
  });

  it('an APP_AND_API_HOSTS infra route passes on any host (ALB health checks use the target IP)', () => {
    for (const host of ['app.sanchay.in', 'api.sanchay.in', '10.0.1.23:3000']) {
      expect(decide(p.health, { host, ...native })).toBe('pass');
    }
    expect(decide(p.health, {})).toBe('pass');
  });
});
```

`apps/api/test/int/security/otp-abuse.int.test.ts`:
```ts
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { eq, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { auditEvents } from '../../../src/db/schema.js';
import { istDayStart, OTP_POLICY } from '../../../src/modules/identity/otp.service.js';
import { AUDIT_ACTIONS } from '../../../src/modules/platform/audit.service.js';
import { DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND } from '../../../src/modules/platform/clock.js';
import { bootTestApp, type TestApp } from '../app.js';
import { signInWeb } from '../flows.js';
import { fromIp, nativeHeaders } from '../http.js';

/**
 * F8: the H-3 OTP quotas end to end over POST /api/v1/auth/otp (ClientGuard, the device header,
 * the socket client IP and the anonymous throttler all in the path). OtpService's own unit-level
 * tests (otp-issue, otp-cap) stay; this suite proves the HTTP surface wires ip and device through.
 * Every test uses its own IP, installations and mobiles, and the clock moves an hour first.
 */

let t: TestApp;
let mobileSeq = 0;
let ipSeq = 0;

beforeAll(async () => {
  t = await bootTestApp();
});
afterAll(async () => {
  await t.close();
});
beforeEach(() => {
  t.clock.advance(HOUR + MINUTE);
});
afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

/** Unique per call: 98 + 8 digits. */
function nextMobile(): string {
  mobileSeq += 1;
  return `98${String(70_000_000 + mobileSeq)}`;
}
/** RFC 5737 TEST-NET-2, one address per call. */
function nextIp(): string {
  ipSeq += 1;
  return `198.51.100.${ipSeq}`;
}

function sendOtp(mobile: string, opts: { ip: string; installationId?: string }) {
  return t.app.inject({
    method: 'POST',
    url: '/api/v1/auth/otp',
    headers: nativeHeaders({ installationId: opts.installationId ?? randomUUID() }),
    payload: { mobile },
    ...fromIp(opts.ip),
  });
}

function verifyOtp(challengeId: string, code: string, ip: string) {
  return t.app.inject({
    method: 'POST',
    url: '/api/v1/auth/otp/verify',
    headers: nativeHeaders({ installationId: randomUUID() }),
    payload: { challengeId, code },
    ...fromIp(ip),
  });
}

const outcome = (res: { statusCode: number; json(): { code?: string } }) =>
  res.statusCode === 200 ? 200 : [res.statusCode, res.json().code];

const wrongCode = (real: string): string => (real === '000000' ? '111111' : '000000');
const afterCooldown = () => t.clock.advance(OTP_POLICY.cooldownMs + SECOND);

describe('OTP abuse over HTTP: H-3 quotas (LOGIN)', () => {
  it('cooldown: a resend inside 30 s is 429 OTP_COOLDOWN; after 30 s it is sent', async () => {
    const mobile = nextMobile();
    const ip = nextIp();
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip }))).toBe(200);
    const early = await sendOtp(mobile, { ip });
    expect([early.statusCode, early.json().code, early.json().data.retryAfterSeconds]).toEqual([
      429,
      'OTP_COOLDOWN',
      30,
    ]);
    afterCooldown();
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip }))).toBe(200);
  });

  it('5 per destination per hour: the 6th is RATE_LIMITED even from a new device and IP', async () => {
    const mobile = nextMobile();
    for (let i = 0; i < OTP_POLICY.perDestinationPerHour; i += 1) {
      expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toBe(200);
      afterCooldown();
    }
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toEqual([429, 'RATE_LIMITED']);
  });

  it('15 per destination per day: three hourly bursts of 5, then the 16th is refused although the hour is fresh', async () => {
    const mobile = nextMobile();
    for (let burst = 0; burst < 3; burst += 1) {
      for (let i = 0; i < OTP_POLICY.perDestinationPerHour; i += 1) {
        expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toBe(200);
        afterCooldown();
      }
      t.clock.advance(HOUR + MINUTE);
    }
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toEqual([429, 'RATE_LIMITED']);
    t.clock.advance(DAY);
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toBe(200);
  });

  it('20 per IP per hour: the 21st send from one IP is refused; another IP is not', async () => {
    const ip = nextIp();
    for (let i = 0; i < OTP_POLICY.perIpPerHour; i += 1) {
      expect(outcome(await sendOtp(nextMobile(), { ip }))).toBe(200);
    }
    const blocked = nextMobile();
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(blocked, { ip }))).toEqual([429, 'RATE_LIMITED']);
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(blocked, { ip: nextIp() }))).toBe(200);
  });

  it('10 per device per hour: the 11th send from one installation is refused', async () => {
    const installationId = randomUUID();
    for (let i = 0; i < OTP_POLICY.perDevicePerHour; i += 1) {
      expect(outcome(await sendOtp(nextMobile(), { ip: nextIp(), installationId }))).toBe(200);
    }
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(nextMobile(), { ip: nextIp(), installationId }))).toEqual([
      429,
      'RATE_LIMITED',
    ]);
  });

  it('lockout: 3 codes burned by wrong guesses lock the mobile for 30 min, audited STARTED then REFUSED', async () => {
    const mobile = nextMobile();
    const ip = nextIp();
    for (let burn = 0; burn < OTP_POLICY.lockoutBurns; burn += 1) {
      const sent = await sendOtp(mobile, { ip });
      expect(sent.statusCode).toBe(200);
      const challengeId = sent.json().challengeId as string;
      const wrong = wrongCode(t.sms.latestCode(mobile));
      const results: unknown[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < OTP_POLICY.maxAttempts; i += 1) {
        results.push(outcome(await verifyOtp(challengeId, wrong, ip)));
      }
      expect(results.at(-1)).toEqual([401, 'OTP_LOCKED']);
      afterCooldown();
    }
    const locked = await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() });
    expect([locked.statusCode, locked.json().code]).toEqual([429, 'RATE_LIMITED']);
    expect(locked.json().data.retryAfterSeconds).toBeGreaterThan(29 * 60);
    expect(locked.json().data.retryAfterSeconds).toBeLessThanOrEqual(30 * 60);

    const audits = await t.db.db
      .select({ data: auditEvents.data })
      .from(auditEvents)
      .where(eq(auditEvents.action, AUDIT_ACTIONS.AUTH_OTP_LOCKOUT));
    const outcomes = audits.map((a) => a.data.outcome);
    expect(outcomes).toContain('STARTED');
    expect(outcomes).toContain('REFUSED');

    t.clock.advance(OTP_POLICY.lockoutMs);
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toBe(200);
  });
});

describe('H-5 anti-enumeration over HTTP', () => {
  it('a registered and an unknown mobile get the same status, keys and timings, and the same wrong-code error', async () => {
    const known = nextMobile();
    await signInWeb(t, known, nextIp());
    afterCooldown();
    const unknown = nextMobile();
    const a = await sendOtp(known, { ip: nextIp() });
    const b = await sendOtp(unknown, { ip: nextIp() });
    expect(a.statusCode).toBe(200);
    expect(b.statusCode).toBe(a.statusCode);
    expect(Object.keys(b.json()).sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(a.json()).sort());
    expect({ ...b.json(), challengeId: 'x' }).toEqual({ ...a.json(), challengeId: 'x' });

    const wa = await verifyOtp(a.json().challengeId, wrongCode(t.sms.latestCode(known)), nextIp());
    const wb = await verifyOtp(
      b.json().challengeId,
      wrongCode(t.sms.latestCode(unknown)),
      nextIp(),
    );
    const shape = (res: typeof wa) => {
      const { requestId: _requestId, ...data } = res.json().data as Record<string, unknown>;
      return [res.statusCode, { ...res.json(), data }];
    };
    expect(shape(wb)).toEqual(shape(wa));
    expect(shape(wa)[0]).toBe(401);
  });
});

/** Last: it fills the IST day's SMS budget for this database. */
describe('global SMS cap over HTTP', () => {
  it('the 2,001st SMS of the IST day is 503 SMS_UNAVAILABLE, logged, and nothing is sent', async () => {
    const errorLog = vi.spyOn(Logger.prototype, 'error').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    const dayStart = istDayStart(t.clock.now());
    const [{ n } = { n: 0 }] = await t.db.db
      .execute<{ n: number }>(sql`
      SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM app.otp_codes
      WHERE channel = 'SMS' AND created_at >= ${dayStart.toISOString()}::timestamptz
    `)
      .then((r) => r.rows);
    const created = new Date(dayStart.getTime() + MINUTE).toISOString();
    const expires = new Date(dayStart.getTime() + 6 * MINUTE).toISOString();
    await t.db.db.execute(sql`
      INSERT INTO app.otp_codes (id, created_at, purpose, channel, destination_bidx, destination_masked,
        destination_enc, pepper_kid, code_hmac, attempts, expires_at, consumed_at, consumed_reason)
      SELECT uuidv7(), ${created}::timestamptz, 'LOGIN', 'SMS', decode(md5('f8-cap-' || g::text), 'hex'),
        'seeded', decode('00', 'hex'), 1, decode('00', 'hex'), 0, ${expires}::timestamptz,
        ${created}::timestamptz, 'SUPERSEDED'
      FROM generate_series(1, ${OTP_POLICY.smsPerIstDay - n}::int) AS g
    `);
    const mobile = nextMobile();
    const sentBefore = t.sms.outbox.length;
    expect(outcome(await sendOtp(mobile, { ip: nextIp() }))).toEqual([503, 'SMS_UNAVAILABLE']);
    expect(t.sms.outbox).toHaveLength(sentBefore);
    expect(errorLog).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.stringContaining('otp.sms_daily_cap'));
  });
});
```

`apps/api/test/int/security/hostguard.int.test.ts`:
```ts
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { SESSION_COOKIE } from '../../../src/modules/platform/cookies.js';
import { HostGuard } from '../../../src/modules/platform/host.guard.js';
import { bootTestApp, type TestApp } from '../app.js';
import { apiHost, appHost, nativeHeaders, webHeaders } from '../http.js';
import { type AppRoute, type HttpMethod, listRoutes, urlOf } from './routes.js';

/**
 * F8: the H-1/R-11 host matrix, swept over every route the booted app registered (listRoutes reads
 * Nest's own metadata, so a raw route or procedure added later is swept without editing this file).
 * The assertion is HostGuard's own decision, read from a spy, so a 404 from a handler is never
 * mistaken for a HostGuard refusal.
 */

type HostKind = 'app' | 'api' | 'unknown' | 'none';
type Flavour = 'web-cookie' | 'native-bearer' | 'bare';
type Decision = 'pass' | 'deny';

const HOST_KINDS: readonly HostKind[] = ['app', 'api', 'unknown', 'none'];
const FLAVOURS: readonly Flavour[] = ['web-cookie', 'native-bearer', 'bare'];

let t: TestApp;
let routes: AppRoute[];
const guard = vi.spyOn(HostGuard.prototype, 'canActivate');

beforeAll(async () => {
  t = await bootTestApp();
  routes = listRoutes(t.app);
});
afterAll(async () => {
  guard.mockRestore();
  await t.close();
});

function headersFor(host: HostKind, flavour: Flavour): Record<string, string> {
  const hostHeader: Record<string, string> =
    host === 'app'
      ? { host: appHost() }
      : host === 'api'
        ? { host: apiHost() }
        : host === 'unknown'
          ? { host: 'evil.example.com' }
          : {};
  if (flavour === 'web-cookie') {
    const { host: _default, ...web } = webHeaders({
      cookies: { [SESSION_COOKIE]: 'x'.repeat(43) },
    });
    return { ...web, ...hostHeader };
  }
  if (flavour === 'native-bearer') {
    const { host: _default, ...native } = nativeHeaders({
      installationId: randomUUID(),
      token: 'x'.repeat(43),
    });
    return { ...native, ...hostHeader };
  }
  return hostHeader;
}

/** H-1 and R-11, written out independently of HostGuard's code. */
function expected(route: AppRoute, host: HostKind, flavour: Flavour): Decision {
  if (route.infra === 'APP_AND_API_HOSTS') return 'pass';
  if (route.infra === 'API_HOST') return host === 'api' ? 'pass' : 'deny';
  if (host === 'app') return flavour === 'native-bearer' ? 'deny' : 'pass';
  if (host === 'api') return flavour === 'web-cookie' ? 'deny' : 'pass';
  return 'deny';
}

async function decide(
  method: HttpMethod,
  url: string,
  headers: Record<string, string>,
): Promise<{ decision: Decision; statusCode: number; code: unknown }> {
  const before = guard.mock.calls.length;
  const res = await t.app.inject({
    method,
    url,
    headers,
    ...(method === 'GET' ? {} : { payload: {} }),
  });
  expect(guard.mock.calls.length, `HostGuard ran once for ${method} ${url}`).toBe(before + 1);
  const decision = guard.mock.results.at(-1)?.type === 'throw' ? 'deny' : 'pass';
  let code: unknown = null;
  try {
    code = res.json().code;
  } catch {
    code = null;
  }
  return { decision, statusCode: res.statusCode, code };
}

describe('HostGuard sweep over every registered route (H-1, R-11)', () => {
  it('finds the R-11 raw routes with their host scopes', () => {
    const scopes = Object.fromEntries(
      routes.filter((r) => r.infra !== null).map((r) => [`${r.method} ${r.path}`, r.infra]),
    );
    expect(scopes).toMatchObject({
      'GET /health': 'APP_AND_API_HOSTS',
      'POST /webhooks/fp': 'API_HOST',
      'GET /pg/return/:ref': 'API_HOST',
      'POST /pg/return/:ref': 'API_HOST',
    });
    expect(routes.filter((r) => r.infra !== null && !r.isPublic)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('every route x {app, api, unknown, no} host x {web cookie, native bearer, bare} matches H-1', async () => {
    const mismatches: string[] = [];
    for (const route of routes) {
      for (const host of HOST_KINDS) {
        for (const flavour of FLAVOURS) {
          const { decision, statusCode, code } = await decide(
            route.method,
            urlOf(route),
            headersFor(host, flavour),
          );
          const want = expected(route, host, flavour);
          if (decision !== want) {
            mismatches.push(
              `${route.name} ${route.method} ${route.path} on ${host} as ${flavour}: ${decision}, want ${want}`,
            );
          } else if (decision === 'deny' && (statusCode !== 404 || code !== 'NOT_FOUND')) {
            mismatches.push(
              `${route.name} on ${host} as ${flavour}: denied with ${statusCode} ${String(code)}, want 404`,
            );
          }
        }
      }
    }
    expect(mismatches).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('the outline 8-row matrix ({app, api} x {cookie, bearer, webhook, return})', () => {
  const ref = 'r7Qx2mV9pL4sN8wK1cZ5bA';
  const rows: Array<[string, HttpMethod, string, HostKind, Flavour, Decision]> = [
    ['app + cookie', 'GET', '/api/v1/auth/session', 'app', 'web-cookie', 'pass'],
    ['api + cookie', 'GET', '/api/v1/auth/session', 'api', 'web-cookie', 'deny'],
    ['app + bearer', 'GET', '/api/v1/auth/session', 'app', 'native-bearer', 'deny'],
    ['api + bearer', 'GET', '/api/v1/auth/session', 'api', 'native-bearer', 'pass'],
    ['app + webhook', 'POST', '/api/v1/webhooks/fp', 'app', 'bare', 'deny'],
    ['api + webhook', 'POST', '/api/v1/webhooks/fp', 'api', 'bare', 'pass'],
    ['app + return', 'GET', `/api/v1/pg/return/${ref}`, 'app', 'bare', 'deny'],
    ['api + return', 'GET', `/api/v1/pg/return/${ref}`, 'api', 'bare', 'pass'],
  ];

  it.each(rows)('%s -> HostGuard %s', async (_name, method, url, host, flavour, want) => {
    const res = await decide(method, url, headersFor(host, flavour));
    expect(res.decision).toBe(want);
    if (want === 'deny') expect([res.statusCode, res.code]).toEqual([404, 'NOT_FOUND']);
    if (want === 'pass' && url.endsWith('/auth/session')) {
      // The bogus session is refused by SessionGuard, never by HostGuard.
      expect([res.statusCode, res.code]).toEqual([401, 'AUTH_REQUIRED']);
    }
  });

  it('R-11: the raw routes on their own host never meet ClientGuard or SessionGuard', async () => {
    for (const route of routes.filter((r) => r.infra !== null)) {
      const res = await decide(route.method, urlOf(route), headersFor('api', 'bare'));
      expect(res.decision, route.name).toBe('pass');
      expect([403, 'ORIGIN_REJECTED'], route.name).not.toEqual([res.statusCode, res.code]);
      expect([401, 'AUTH_REQUIRED'], route.name).not.toEqual([res.statusCode, res.code]);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { type Env, EnvError, parseEnv } from '../../../src/config/env.js';
import { testEnv } from '../env.js';

/**
 * F8: the production configuration refuses every local/dev-only provider (B2 invariants 1, 2, 5–7;
 * D3 8–9; D7 10; D6 11–12; E1 13). The baseline is built from testEnv's own parsed output, so a
 * required key added by any later task is inherited here without editing this file.
 */

const LOCAL_KEYS = [
  'SANCHAY_LOCAL_PII_KEY',
  'SANCHAY_LOCAL_BIDX_KEY',
  'SANCHAY_OTP_PEPPER',
  'SANCHAY_AUTH_TOKEN_KEY',
] as const;

const key = (fill: number): string => Buffer.alloc(32, fill).toString('base64');

function rawOf(env: Env): Record<string, string> {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(env)
      .filter(
        ([name, value]) => value !== undefined && !(LOCAL_KEYS as readonly string[]).includes(name),
      )
      .map(([name, value]) => [name, String(value)]),
  );
}

/** A configuration prod accepts: secrets keyring, ALB client IP, MSG91, SES, the production FP transport. */
const PROD: Record<string, string> = {
  ...rawOf(testEnv('postgres://sanchay@db.internal:5432/sanchay')),
  SANCHAY_APP_ENV: 'prod',
  SANCHAY_APP_ORIGIN: 'https://app.sanchay.in',
  SANCHAY_API_ORIGIN: 'https://api.sanchay.in',
  SANCHAY_KEY_SERVICE: 'secrets',
  SANCHAY_KEYRING_JSON: JSON.stringify({
    currentKid: 1,
    pii: { '1': key(5) },
    bidx: key(6),
    otpPepper: { '1': key(7) },
    authToken: key(8),
  }),
  SANCHAY_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE: 'alb',
  SANCHAY_OTP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR: '20',
  SANCHAY_SMS_RETRIEVER_HASH: 'FA+9qCX9VSu',
  SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_SMS: 'msg91',
  SANCHAY_MSG91_CREDENTIALS_JSON: JSON.stringify({
    authKey: 'test-auth-key',
    senderId: 'SNCHAY',
    peId: '1001',
    templateIds: { LOGIN: 't1', CONSENT: 't2', CONSENT_UNITS: 't3', ATTEST: 't4' },
  }),
  SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_EMAIL: 'ses',
  SANCHAY_SES_FROM: 'no-reply@sanchay.in',
  SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_FP: 'production',
  SANCHAY_FP_WEBHOOK_SECRET: 'w'.repeat(32),
  SANCHAY_PILOT_INVITE_ONLY: 'true',
};

function refusal(raw: Record<string, string | undefined>): string {
  try {
    parseEnv(raw);
  } catch (error) {
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(EnvError);
    return (error as Error).message;
  }
  throw new Error('expected parseEnv to refuse this configuration');
}

describe('prod image guard (boot invariants)', () => {
  it('the prod baseline boots, so every refusal below is caused by its one changed key', () => {
    expect(parseEnv(PROD)).toMatchObject({
      SANCHAY_APP_ENV: 'prod',
      SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_SMS: 'msg91',
      SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_EMAIL: 'ses',
      SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_FP: 'production',
      SANCHAY_KEY_SERVICE: 'secrets',
    });
  });

  const FAKE_PROVIDERS =
    /fake SMS\/email providers \(capture, mailpit\) are refused in staging\/prod/;

  it.each<[string, Record<string, string | undefined>, RegExp]>([
    ['capture SMS', { SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_SMS: 'capture' }, FAKE_PROVIDERS],
    ['mailpit SMS', { SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_SMS: 'mailpit' }, FAKE_PROVIDERS],
    ['capture email', { SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_EMAIL: 'capture' }, FAKE_PROVIDERS],
    ['mailpit email', { SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_EMAIL: 'mailpit' }, FAKE_PROVIDERS],
    [
      'the local keyring',
      {
        SANCHAY_KEY_SERVICE: 'local',
        SANCHAY_LOCAL_PII_KEY: key(1),
        SANCHAY_LOCAL_BIDX_KEY: key(2),
        SANCHAY_OTP_PEPPER: key(3),
        SANCHAY_AUTH_TOKEN_KEY: key(4),
      },
      /the local keyring is refused outside local\/test/,
    ],
    [
      'the fake FP transport',
      { SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_FP: 'fake' },
      /SANCHAY_PROVIDER_MODE_FP=fake is refused outside local\/test/,
    ],
    [
      'an open pilot',
      { SANCHAY_PILOT_INVITE_ONLY: 'false' },
      /SANCHAY_PILOT_INVITE_ONLY=false is refused in prod until P2/,
    ],
    [
      'a raised OTP IP quota',
      { SANCHAY_OTP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR: '1000' },
      /SANCHAY_OTP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR must be 20 outside local\/test/,
    ],
    [
      'the socket client IP',
      { SANCHAY_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE: 'socket' },
      /SANCHAY_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE must be alb outside local\/test/,
    ],
    [
      'no retriever hash',
      { SANCHAY_SMS_RETRIEVER_HASH: undefined },
      /SANCHAY_SMS_RETRIEVER_HASH is required outside local\/test/,
    ],
    [
      'no webhook secret',
      { SANCHAY_FP_WEBHOOK_SECRET: undefined },
      /SANCHAY_FP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is required outside local\/test/,
    ],
    [
      'MSG91 without credentials',
```

`apps/api/src/modules/platform/host.guard.ts` (E2's file; key-level edit). Add below `hostnameOf`:
```ts
/** What a request presents before ClientGuard runs: its x-sanchay-client value and whether it carries Authorization. */
export interface PresentedClient {
  client: string | undefined;
  bearer: boolean;
}

/**
 * H-1 for an ordinary (non-infra) route: the app host serves the web client (cookie auth, never a
 * bearer); the api host serves the native client (bearer auth, never the web client). A request
 * with no client header passes here and is refused by ClientGuard. An unknown host is refused.
 */
export function ordinaryRouteAllowed(host: AppHost | null, presented: PresentedClient): boolean {
  if (host === 'APP') {
    return !presented.bearer && (presented.client === undefined || presented.client === 'web');
  }
  if (host === 'API') return presented.client !== 'web';
  return false;
}
```
and replace E2's class (`canActivate` and `classify`; constructor, token and guard order unchanged) with:
```ts
/**
 * R-11 and H-1: classifies the inbound request's Host header against SANCHAY_APP_ORIGIN /
 * SANCHAY_API_ORIGIN. Any mismatch is 404 (never 403 — an unrecognised host should look like
 * nothing is there). Routes carrying @InfraRoute are scoped by their own metadata; every other
 * route follows `ordinaryRouteAllowed`. When both origins share a hostname (local development,
 * `.env.example`), a request on it may act as either host. Runs first in app.module.ts's guard chain.
 */
@Injectable()
export class HostGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(
    @Inject(Reflector) private readonly reflector: Reflector,
    @Inject(AppConfig) private readonly config: AppConfig,
  ) {}

  canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    const req = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest<FastifyRequest>();
    const hosts = this.classify(headerValue(req.headers.host));
    const infra = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<InfraRouteHosts | undefined>(INFRA_ROUTE, [
      ctx.getHandler(),
      ctx.getClass(),
    ]);
    if (infra === 'APP_AND_API_HOSTS') return true;
    if (infra === 'API_HOST') {
      if (!hosts.includes('API')) throw new AppError('NOT_FOUND');
      return true;
    }
    const presented: PresentedClient = {
      client: headerValue(req.headers['x-sanchay-client']),
      bearer: headerValue(req.headers.authorization) !== undefined,
    };
    if (!hosts.some((host) => ordinaryRouteAllowed(host, presented))) {
      throw new AppError('NOT_FOUND');
    }
    return true;
  }

  /** The hosts this Host header names: none, one, or both when the two origins share a hostname. */
  private classify(hostHeader: string | undefined): AppHost[] {
    const bare = hostHeader?.split(':')[0]?.toLowerCase();
    if (bare === undefined) return [];
    const hosts: AppHost[] = [];
    if (bare === hostnameOf(this.config.env.SANCHAY_APP_ORIGIN)) hosts.push('APP');
    if (bare === hostnameOf(this.config.env.SANCHAY_API_ORIGIN)) hosts.push('API');
    return hosts;
  }
}
```

```ts
export function nativeHeaders(opts: {

  platform?: 'android' | 'ios';
  host?: string;
}): Record<string, string> {
```
