Create `docs/probes/invitee-dry-run-2026-11.md`:

````markdown
# Invitee dry run and kill-switch drill (F27)

Everything runs on prod, the only deployed stack, paused until GO-1 (R-31): invite-only, orders and SIPs off,
and no invite but the founders' test accounts. Drill (D1-D7): Wed 2026-11-25, between canary legs. Pre-GO-1
check (D1, D2, D9): Thu 2026-11-26, after the canary is reconciled and before the GO-1 meeting on Fri 11-27.
Invitee seed (D8, D9): only after the owner's GO-1 decision. Invitees start on Mon 11-30, and only after a GO-1.

Operator: Dev B. Witness: the PO. Times in IST. This log never holds a mobile number, a name or an email: refer
to invitees by their row number in the PO's private list, and to people by their operator handle (a
lower-case id such as `f.anita`; F7 refuses anything else).

Every ops command below is a one-off ECS task on the ops task definition, run with the one deployed form in
the [runbooks README](../runbooks/README.md#running-an-ops-command) (copied from F7's
[ops CLIs](../runbooks/ops-cli.md)): write `ops-overrides.json` outside the repo with the `command` shown here,
run the task, wait for it, read its exit code (0 done, 1 refused with nothing written, 2 usage) and its result
line, then delete the file. Prod is the only deployed stack (R-31), so every line below is prod's.

## Pass criteria

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Caps | `app/config` shows `limits.perOrderMax` `100000.00` and `limits.perInvestorPerDayMax` `200000.00`, equal to G-B11 |
| D2 | SIP flag | `flags.sipEnabled` is `false` in prod (R-06) |
| D3 | Invite seed (one founder-owned spare SIM, a founders' test account) | the task exits 0; its result line shows the mobile only as `******` and the last 4 digits; `v_ops_audit` has one `PILOT_INVITE_ADDED` row for it, with the operator's handle; the SSM parameter and the local list file are deleted |
| D4 | Gate | the invited spare number signs up; a founder-owned number that was never invited sees "Sanchay is invite-only right now. Please use the mobile number your invitation was sent to." after a correct OTP |
| D5 | Per-order cap (in D7's window, on a founder's canary account: the spare SIM has no KYC on prod) | a ₹1,00,000.01 purchase is refused (`AMOUNT_ABOVE_MAX`, field `PILOT_CAP`) before any FP call |
| D6 | Kill switch off | the task exits 0; `flags.ordersEnabled` is `false`; Invest on a founder's canary account shows "New investments are paused right now. Please try again later."; `v_ops_audit` has the `OPS_KILL_SWITCH` row with the operator's handle and the reason |
| D7 | Kill switch on (a window of a few minutes, like a canary leg's) | two different founders; `flags.ordersEnabled` is `true`; a ₹500 purchase on a founder's canary account reaches the consent screen and is not approved; `v_ops_audit` has the row with `--approver1` as `actor_id`; one operator turns orders off again straight after D5 (reason `F27 drill done`) |
| D8 | Invite seed (the PO's list, only after the GO-1 decision, R-31) | `v_pilot_invites_count` shows `LIVE` equal to the number of rows in the PO's list (G-B11); re-running the same parameter exits 1 with the masked refusal and adds no `PILOT_INVITE_ADDED` row; the SSM parameter and the local list file are deleted |
| D9 | Prod stays off | `flags.ordersEnabled` is `false` in prod after the drill, before and after D8, until two founders turn it on for the pilot after the GO-1 decision |

## Commands

Read the public config (D1, D2, D6, D7, D9) on the app host: F8's HostGuard refuses the web client on the api
host. Same line in both shells:

```
curl.exe -s -H "x-sanchay-client: web" https://app.sanchay.in/api/v1/app/config
```

Invites (D3, D8) never put a mobile on a command line: F7's `ops:invite` reads the list from an SSM
SecureString that only the ops task role may read (FR-20/FR-21). Write the list in an editor, outside the
repository, as `invite-list.txt`: one 10-digit mobile per line (a `+91` prefix and spaces are dropped), no
names, saved as UTF-8. For D3 it holds the one spare SIM; for D8, after the GO-1 decision, the PO's list. Put it
as a SecureString (the name is `/sanchay/<env>/invites/<name>`; F7 refuses any other prefix and a parameter
that is not a SecureString). PowerShell:

```
aws ssm put-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/pilot-2026-11 --type SecureString --value file://invite-list.txt
```

Git Bash (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` stops Git Bash rewriting the parameter name into a Windows path):

```
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/pilot-2026-11 --type SecureString --value file://invite-list.txt
```

For D3 use `/sanchay/prod/invites/f27-drill` in place of `pilot-2026-11`. The `command` arrays for
`ops-overrides.json`:

- Invite every mobile in the parameter (D3, D8). All or nothing: if any listed mobile already has an invite,
  the run exits 1, names it masked and writes nothing:

```
["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:invite", "--mobiles-param", "/sanchay/prod/invites/pilot-2026-11", "--by", "<handle>", "--note", "pilot-2026-11"]
```

  As soon as the checks below are done, delete the parameter, check that nothing is left under the prefix (the
  `describe-parameters` line prints nothing), and delete the local file. PowerShell:

```
aws ssm delete-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/pilot-2026-11
aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters "Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/sanchay/prod/invites/" --query "Parameters[].Name" --output text
rm invite-list.txt
```

  Git Bash:

```
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm delete-parameter --name /sanchay/prod/invites/pilot-2026-11
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters "Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/sanchay/prod/invites/" --query "Parameters[].Name" --output text
rm invite-list.txt
```

  A list refused for a reason other than the D8 repeat (a line that is not a mobile, a number that already has
  an invite) wrote nothing: correct the file, put it under a new name such as `pilot-2026-11-2`, run again and
  delete again (F7's "Inviting pilot investors").

- Turn orders off (D6, the end of the D7 window, and before D8 if anything left them on). One operator:

```
["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:kill-switch", "--off", "--by", "<handle>", "--reason", "F27 drill"]
```

- Turn orders on (D7 only: prod is paused until GO-1, R-31, so this window lasts only as long as D7 and D5,
  like a canary leg's, F20). Two different founders:

```
["node", "dist/main.js", "ops:kill-switch", "--on", "--approver1", "<handle>", "--approver2", "<handle>", "--reason", "F27 drill"]
```

Run each one, wait for it and read its exit code (same lines in both shells):

```
aws ecs run-task --cluster sanchay-prod --launch-type FARGATE --task-definition sanchay-prod-ops --network-configuration "awsvpcConfiguration={subnets=[<AppSubnetIds>],securityGroups=[<ServiceSecurityGroupId>],assignPublicIp=DISABLED}" --overrides file://ops-overrides.json --query "tasks[0].taskArn" --output text
aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster sanchay-prod --tasks <task-arn>
aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster sanchay-prod --tasks <task-arn> --query "tasks[0].containers[0].exitCode" --output text
```

Read the result line. PowerShell:

```
aws logs get-log-events --log-group-name /sanchay/prod/app --log-stream-name prod/ops/<task-id> --query "events[].message" --output text
```

Git Bash:

```
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws logs get-log-events --log-group-name /sanchay/prod/app --log-stream-name prod/ops/<task-id> --query "events[].message" --output text
```

Read-only checks (D3, D6, D7, D8), as `sanchay_readonly_login` over SSM
([database access](../runbooks/db-access.md), "Read-only SQL over SSM (spec §2.4)"):

```
SELECT status, invites FROM app.v_pilot_invites_count ORDER BY status;
SELECT action, actor_id, entity_id, occurred_at FROM app.v_ops_audit WHERE action = 'PILOT_INVITE_ADDED' ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 50;
SELECT action, actor_id, entity_id, reason, occurred_at FROM app.v_ops_audit WHERE action = 'OPS_KILL_SWITCH' ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 5;
```

The RunTask overrides carry only the parameter name, so CloudTrail and the ECS console never see a mobile; the
result line in CloudWatch and the audit rows show only the last four digits. The list exists only in the
SecureString and the local file until both are deleted.

The founders' own prod accounts for the canary (F20, from Tue 11-17) need invites too: F20 Step 6 seeds them
before the first canary leg, with the same form and the parameter `/sanchay/prod/invites/canary-founders`, and
they show as `USED` in `v_pilot_invites_count` once the founders have signed up. They and the D3 spare SIM are
already invited, so keep them out of the PO's list, or the D8 run refuses the whole list.
````

- **The saga** (spec §4.3 CANCEL_PENDING, R-08, research fp-api §4: "Cancel: `POST /v2/mf_purchase_plans/cancel {id, cancellation_code, cancellation_reason?}`", states `created|active → cancelled`, "cancellation takes effect immediately; instalments already generated are unaffected"; sandbox run 1, P-09 row 9: `invest_later` accepted, plan `cancelled`, FP stored `cancellation_code: custom_reason`):
  1. **Request (api):** lock the plan; reclaim a dead CANCEL_PENDING; refuse anything but ACTIVE; `ConsentEngine.create` (subjects: the plan only) → move to CANCEL_PENDING → `SIP_CANCEL_REQUESTED`. No FP call.
  2. **Approve (E4):** enqueues `plans.cancel.submit` with `singletonKey = challengeId`. Every other enqueue of the job (the sweep, and F2's `plans.sip.advance` branch, which also carries the job's own re-read) uses the same key. The queue is `exclusive` (R-32, RV-04-F28-1), so a send while a job for this cancel is queued, retrying or running is refused (null): one live cancel job at a time.
  3. **Submit (worker), inside `useConsumed`:** `GET /v2/mf_purchase_plans/{id}` first (class R).
     - FP `active`/`created`: `SIP_CANCEL_SUBMITTED` is recorded in its own autocommit write, then `POST /v2/mf_purchase_plans/cancel {id, cancellation_code: 'invest_later'}`. FP `cancelled` in the reply → CANCELLED (`fp_cancelled`, `cancelled_by = 'INVESTOR'`, `final_at`), `SIP_CANCELLED` audit and email, in one transaction. Only the reply's `state` is read: the sandbox does not keep the code we send (BRIEF D7).
     - FP already `cancelled` and no `SIP_CANCEL_SUBMITTED` for this challenge (an FP auto-cancel, for example three failed instalments) → CANCELLED with `cancelled_by = 'EXTERNAL'`, `markUnused`, email. When `SIP_CANCEL_SUBMITTED` exists, a previous run's write landed and its reply was lost → CANCELLED by INVESTOR, no `markUnused`.
     - FP `completed`/`failed`/other → ACTIVE (`cancel_not_applicable`), `markUnused`, WARNING `PLAN_CANCEL_NOT_APPLICABLE`.
  4. **Failures:** `CONSENT_EXPIRED` before anything was sent → ACTIVE (`cancel_consent_lapsed`, failure code `CONSENT_EXPIRED`) and `markUnused`. A failed pre-check read is re-thrown, and pg-boss retries inside the saga window. A 4xx on the cancel → **FP is read again first**: FP also refuses a plan that is already cancelled (a second delivery of the job, or FP itself, got there after our live read), so `cancelled` → CANCELLED by INVESTOR; anything else → ACTIVE (`fp_cancel_rejected`, failure code = FP's code), WARNING `PLAN_CANCEL_REJECTED` (ops follow up on SEBI's two-working-day cancel), consent stays CONSUMED. A failed re-read is re-thrown (pg-boss retries). Ambiguous (timeout, 5xx, 409, a reply without `cancelled`) → RECONCILING (`ambiguous`) with `cancel_reconciling_since = clock.now()`, and a re-read in 60 s. The job cannot enqueue its own key while it runs (exclusive), so it enqueues `plans.sip.advance` (stately, key = the plan id, `startAfter` 60), whose F28 branch enqueues this job again after this run has ended.
  5. **Re-read (LOOKUP-ADOPT, no consent needed):** FP `cancelled` → CANCELLED by INVESTOR (`lookup_adopt_mapped`). Still `active` 10 minutes after `cancel_reconciling_since` → ACTIVE (`lookup_adopt_mapped`, failure code `FP_PLAN_STILL_ACTIVE`), WARNING `PLAN_CANCEL_NOT_APPLIED`. Any other state → CRITICAL `PLAN_CANCEL_UNRESOLVED`, left RECONCILING for ops. F7's 5-minute backstop reaches this through `plans.sip.advance`. The grace is measured on the app clock on both sides; `order_events.occurred_at` is the database's `now()` and is not used.
  6. **Sweep (`*/5`):** for each CANCEL_PENDING plan it locks the plan, then reads the challenge `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (approve locks the challenge first and the plan second, so waiting here could deadlock; a challenge approve holds is live and is seen again next run). A dead challenge (EXPIRED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, CONSUMED_UNUSED, or PENDING past `expires_at`) → ACTIVE (`cancel_consent_lapsed`, failure code `CONSENT_NOT_GIVEN`). A CONSUMED challenge approved at least 5 minutes ago (`consumed_at`) → `plans.cancel.submit` re-enqueued with `singletonKey = challengeId`, so a lost job cannot strand the plan; earlier, approve's own job may still be running and is left alone. The sweep's cadence puts the re-enqueue 5 to 10 minutes after approve, inside `execute_before` (approve + 10 minutes) for a saga that never started.
  - The mandate is never touched (R-08). Instalments FP raised before the cancel keep syncing (F2's sync now also reads CANCEL_PENDING, cancel-RECONCILING and plans CANCELLED in the last 7 days) and settle through F4's `PurchaseSettlement`.
- **Deviations from the outline:**
  1. **Subject type and document.** The outline asks to append `SIP_CANCELLATION`/`TPL_SIP_CANCELLATION` "if absent". Plan 01 already has `PLAN_CANCEL` and `TPL_PLAN_CANCEL`, and E3 already created `docs/legal/documents/tpl-plan-cancel.md`, so nothing is appended and no second placeholder is created.
  2. **Factors.** The outline says "SMS code". E3's `requiredFactorsFor` puts PLAN_CANCEL in H-21's `EMAIL_ALWAYS`, so the challenge needs SMS and EMAIL. The SMS text is as the outline says.
  3. **Placement.** The outline's `modules/orders/{sip-cancel.service.ts, sip-cancel-submit.job.ts}` move to `modules/plans/` (Assembly notes: all SIP code lives there).
  4. **Refusal code.** The outline names no code. `PLAN_NOT_MODIFIABLE` (Plan 01, 409) is the investor-facing refusal; F2's `PLAN_STATE_INVALID` stays the internal illegal-transition error.
  5. **Reconcile.** The outline's "LOOKUP-ADOPT by re-fetching the plan" is done by `plans.cancel.submit` itself. F2's `plans.sip.advance` adopts only a RECONCILING plan with no FP id, so F28 adds a branch there that routes F7's backstop to this job.
  6. **Extra state handling** the outline does not list, because without it a plan can stay CANCEL_PENDING forever: three D5 edges back to ACTIVE, the lazy reclaim in `requestCancel`, and `plans.cancel.sweep`.
  7. **Sandbox smoke.** `--chain=sip` gets no cancel step. F2 did not wire a SIP chain into D4's `tools/fp-probes` smoke, so there is nothing to extend. Sandbox run 1 (P-09 row 9) already cancelled a plan with `invest_later`; running this task's code against the FP sandbox stays an open item before GO-2 (R-06).
  8. **Idempotency key in the sheet.** One key per intent, as F12 and F16 do: `CancelSipSheet` reuses its key after a network error, a 5xx or `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` (the first request may still land), and mints a new one after any other 4xx (a definitive refusal ends the intent; D1's `requireIdempotency` releases the key of any refusal, Plan 02 RV-02-37).

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS,
  CANCEL_SUBMIT_LOST_AFTER_MS,
  cancelReconcileStep,
  cancelSweepStep,
  isDeadCancelChallenge,
  PLAN_CANCEL_ACTION,
  preCancelCheck,
} from './plan-cancel.js';

const NOW = new Date('2026-11-18T05:00:00.000Z');
const at = (offsetMs: number) => new Date(NOW.getTime() + offsetMs);

describe('isDeadCancelChallenge', () => {
  it('EXPIRED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED and CONSUMED_UNUSED are dead whatever the expiry', () => {
    for (const status of ['EXPIRED', 'CANCELLED', 'SUPERSEDED', 'CONSUMED_UNUSED'] as const) {
      expect(isDeadCancelChallenge({ status, expiresAt: at(60_000) }, NOW), status).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('PENDING is dead only from expires_at on', () => {
    expect(isDeadCancelChallenge({ status: 'PENDING', expiresAt: at(1) }, NOW)).toBe(false);
    expect(isDeadCancelChallenge({ status: 'PENDING', expiresAt: at(0) }, NOW)).toBe(true);
    expect(isDeadCancelChallenge({ status: 'PENDING', expiresAt: at(-1) }, NOW)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('CONSUMED is never dead here: plans.cancel.submit decides (useConsumed owns the deadline)', () => {
    expect(isDeadCancelChallenge({ status: 'CONSUMED', expiresAt: at(-60 * 60_000) }, NOW)).toBe(
      false,
    );
    expect(isDeadCancelChallenge({ status: 'APPROVED', expiresAt: at(-1) }, NOW)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('cancelSweepStep', () => {
  it('a dead challenge returns the plan to ACTIVE; a live PENDING one is left alone', () => {
    expect(
      cancelSweepStep({ status: 'CANCELLED', expiresAt: at(60_000), consumedAt: null }, NOW),
    ).toBe('REVERT');
    expect(cancelSweepStep({ status: 'PENDING', expiresAt: at(0), consumedAt: null }, NOW)).toBe(
      'REVERT',
    );
    expect(cancelSweepStep({ status: 'PENDING', expiresAt: at(1), consumedAt: null }, NOW)).toBe(
      'LEAVE',
    );
  });

  it("a CONSUMED cancel is re-enqueued only once approve's own job has had its time", () => {
    const consumed = (consumedAt: Date | null) =>
      cancelSweepStep({ status: 'CONSUMED', expiresAt: at(-60_000), consumedAt }, NOW);
    expect(consumed(at(-CANCEL_SUBMIT_LOST_AFTER_MS + 1))).toBe('LEAVE');
    expect(consumed(at(-CANCEL_SUBMIT_LOST_AFTER_MS))).toBe('REQUEUE');
    expect(consumed(null)).toBe('REQUEUE');
  });
});

describe('preCancelCheck', () => {
  it('sends for a created or active FP plan', () => {
    expect(preCancelCheck('active')).toBe('SEND');
    expect(preCancelCheck('created')).toBe('SEND');
  });
  it('does not write to an already cancelled plan', () =>
    expect(preCancelCheck('cancelled')).toBe('ALREADY_CANCELLED'));
  it('refuses completed, failed and unknown states', () => {
    for (const state of ['completed', 'failed', 'review_completed', ''])
      expect(preCancelCheck(state), state).toBe('NOT_CANCELLABLE');
  });
});

describe('cancelReconcileStep', () => {
  it('FP cancelled -> CANCELLED at once', () => {
    expect(cancelReconcileStep({ fpState: 'cancelled', reconcilingSince: NOW, now: NOW })).toBe(
      'CANCELLED',
    );
  });
  it('FP still active -> WAIT inside the grace, ACTIVE from the grace on', () => {
    const since = at(-CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS);
    expect(
      cancelReconcileStep({
        fpState: 'active',
        reconcilingSince: at(-CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS + 1),
        now: NOW,
      }),
    ).toBe('WAIT');
    expect(cancelReconcileStep({ fpState: 'active', reconcilingSince: since, now: NOW })).toBe(
      'ACTIVE',
    );
    expect(cancelReconcileStep({ fpState: 'created', reconcilingSince: since, now: NOW })).toBe(
      'ACTIVE',
    );
  });
  it('no RECONCILING stamp yet counts from now (WAIT)', () => {
    expect(cancelReconcileStep({ fpState: 'active', reconcilingSince: null, now: NOW })).toBe(
      'WAIT',
    );
  });
  it('completed or failed at FP -> UNRESOLVED', () => {
    expect(
      cancelReconcileStep({
        fpState: 'completed',
        reconcilingSince: at(-CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS),
        now: NOW,
      }),
    ).toBe('UNRESOLVED');
    expect(cancelReconcileStep({ fpState: 'failed', reconcilingSince: NOW, now: NOW })).toBe(
      'UNRESOLVED',
    );
  });
});

describe('constants', () => {
  it('the SMS action fits one DLT variable', () => {
    expect(PLAN_CANCEL_ACTION.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(30);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { ConsentEngine } from '../../src/modules/legal-consent/consent-engine.js';
import { consentChallenges } from '../../src/modules/legal-consent/legal-consent.schema.js';
import { notifications } from '../../src/modules/notifications/notifications.schema.js';
import { orders } from '../../src/modules/orders/orders.schema.js';
import { InstalmentsSyncJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/instalments-sync.job.js';
import { MandatesPollJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/mandates-poll.job.js';
import { MandatesSubmitJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/mandates-submit.job.js';
import { mandates, plans } from '../../src/modules/plans/plans.schema.js';
import { SipService } from '../../src/modules/plans/sip.service.js';
import { SipAdvanceJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/sip-advance.job.js';
import { SipCancelService } from '../../src/modules/plans/sip-cancel.service.js';
import { SipCancelSubmitJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/sip-cancel-submit.job.js';
import { SipCancelSweepJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/sip-cancel-sweep.job.js';
import { SipSubmitJob } from '../../src/modules/plans/sip-submit.job.js';
import { MINUTE } from '../../src/modules/platform/clock.js';
import type { JobName } from '../../src/modules/platform/jobs/job-registry.js';
import { Jobs } from '../../src/modules/platform/jobs/jobs.service.js';
import { reconBreaks } from '../../src/modules/platform/kernel.schema.js';
import { pgConstraintOf } from '../../src/modules/platform/pg-errors.js';
import { auditEvents } from '../../src/modules/platform/platform.schema.js';
import { expectBola } from './bola.js';
import { expectNoPmWritesBeforeConsumed } from './consent-first.js';
import { bootFpTestApp, type FpTestApp } from './fake-fp.js';
import { webHeaders } from './http.js';
import { jobOf } from './jobs.js';
import { seedSipInvestor, seedSipScheme, setSipEnabled } from './sip-seed.js';

let t: FpTestApp;
const enqueued: Array<{ name: string; data: unknown; opts: unknown }> = [];

beforeAll(async () => {
  t = await bootFpTestApp();
  vi.spyOn(t.app.get(Jobs), 'enqueue').mockImplementation(async (_exec, name, data, opts) => {
    enqueued.push({ name, data, opts });
    return 'job-id';
  });
  await setSipEnabled(t, true);
});
afterAll(async () => {
  await t.close();
});
beforeEach(() => {
  enqueued.length = 0;
});

type SipInvestor = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof seedSipInvestor>>;

const lastJob = (name: JobName) => [...enqueued].reverse().find((j) => j.name === name);
/** Every plans.cancel.submit enqueue for one cancel (approve's, the sweep's, and plans.sip.advance's for the backstop and the re-read). */
const cancelJobsFor = (challengeId: string) =>
  enqueued.filter(
    (j) =>
      j.name === 'plans.cancel.submit' &&
      (j.data as { challengeId?: string }).challengeId === challengeId,
  );
const planOf = async (id: string) =>
  (await t.db.db.select().from(plans).where(eq(plans.id, id)))[0];
const mandateOf = async (id: string) =>
  (await t.db.db.select().from(mandates).where(eq(mandates.id, id)))[0];
const challengeOf = async (id: string) =>
  (await t.db.db.select().from(consentChallenges).where(eq(consentChallenges.id, id)))[0];
const auditFor = async (entityType: string, entityId: string) =>
  (
    await t.db.db
      .select()
      .from(auditEvents)
      .where(and(eq(auditEvents.entityType, entityType), eq(auditEvents.entityId, entityId)))
  ).map((r) => r.action);
const notificationsFor = async (investorId: string, templateKey: string) =>
  t.db.db
    .select()
    .from(notifications)
    .where(
      and(
        eq(notifications.investorId, investorId),
        eq(notifications.templateKey, templateKey as never),
      ),
    );
const breaksFor = async (planId: string) =>
  (await t.db.db.select().from(reconBreaks).where(eq(reconBreaks.entityId, planId))).map(
    (b) => `${b.kind}:${b.severity}`,
  );
const cancelCalls = () => t.fakeFp.calls({ op: 'purchasePlan.cancel' }).length;

/** Sends every factor the challenge needs and approves it (E4 + RV-03-1). */
async function approveChallenge(challengeId: string, investor: SipInvestor): Promise<void> {
  const engine = t.app.get(ConsentEngine);
  const needsEmail = (await challengeOf(challengeId))?.requiredFactors.includes('EMAIL') === true;
  await engine.sendOtp(challengeId, 'SMS');
  if (needsEmail) await engine.sendOtp(challengeId, 'EMAIL');
  await engine.approve(challengeId, {
    smsCode: t.sms.latestCode(investor.mobile),
    ...(needsEmail ? { emailCode: t.email.latestCode(investor.email) } : {}),
  });
}

const sipAdvance = (planId: string, challengeId: string) =>
  t.app.get(SipAdvanceJob).handle(jobOf('plans.sip.advance', { planId, challengeId }));
const cancelSubmit = (data: unknown) =>
  t.app.get(SipCancelSubmitJob).handle(jobOf('plans.cancel.submit', data));
const sweep = () => t.app.get(SipCancelSweepJob).handle(jobOf('plans.cancel.sweep', {}));
const requestCancel = (investor: SipInvestor, planId: string) =>
  t.app.get(SipCancelService).requestCancel(investor.investorId, planId);
const httpCancel = (investor: SipInvestor, planId: string, key?: string) =>
  t.app.inject({
    method: 'POST',
    url: `/api/v1/plans/${planId}/cancel`,
    headers: {
      ...webHeaders({ cookies: investor.cookies }),
      ...(key === undefined ? {} : { 'idempotency-key': key }),
    },
    payload: {},
  });

/** F2's chain to an ACTIVE new-mandate SIP; the clock then moves on so the cancel's consent window is its own. */
async function activeSip() {
  const investor = await seedSipInvestor(t);
  const scheme = await seedSipScheme(t);
  const draft = await t.app.get(SipService).createSip({
    investorId: investor.investorId,
    schemeId: scheme.id,
    amount: '5000.00',
    installmentDay: 10,
    numberOfInstalments: null,
    rail: 'UPI_AUTOPAY', // F3; drop this line if T6 removed F3
    userIp: '203.0.113.10',
    initiatedVia: 'web',
  });
  await approveChallenge(draft.challengeId, investor);
  await t.app
    .get(MandatesSubmitJob)
    .handle(jobOf('mandates.submit', lastJob('mandates.submit')?.data));
  t.fakeFp.advanceMandate(Number((await mandateOf(draft.mandateId))?.fpMandateId), 'APPROVED');
  await t.app.get(MandatesPollJob).handle(jobOf('mandates.poll', { scope: 'PENDING' }));
  await t.app
    .get(SipSubmitJob)
    .handle(jobOf('plans.sip.submit', lastJob('plans.sip.submit')?.data));
  const fpPlanId = (await planOf(draft.planId))?.fpPlanId ?? '';
  t.fakeFp.advancePlan(fpPlanId, 'review_completed');
  await sipAdvance(draft.planId, draft.challengeId);
  t.fakeFp.advancePlan(fpPlanId, 'active', {
    startDate: draft.firstInstalmentDate,
    nextInstallmentDate: draft.firstInstalmentDate,
  });
  await sipAdvance(draft.planId, draft.challengeId);
  expect((await planOf(draft.planId))?.status).toBe('ACTIVE');
  t.clock.advance(MINUTE);
  return {
    investor,
    planId: draft.planId,
    mandateId: draft.mandateId,
    registrationChallengeId: draft.challengeId,
    fpPlanId,
  };
}

/** An ACTIVE SIP whose cancel is approved; `jobData` is what approve enqueued for plans.cancel.submit. */
async function approvedCancel() {
  const sip = await activeSip();
  const { challengeId } = await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
  t.clock.advance(MINUTE);
  await approveChallenge(challengeId, sip.investor);
  const job = lastJob('plans.cancel.submit');
  // E4's key; every other enqueue of this job uses the same one.
  expect(job).toMatchObject({
    data: { challengeId, subjectIds: [sip.planId] },
    opts: { singletonKey: challengeId },
  });
  return { ...sip, challengeId, jobData: job?.data };
}

describe('plans.cancel', () => {
  it('FakeFp has zero P/M writes before CONSUMED (SIP cancel); CONSUMED -> CANCELLED by INVESTOR, mandate kept', async () => {
    const sip = await activeSip();
    const mWrites = t.fakeFp.calls({ class: 'M' }).length;
    const cancels = cancelCalls();
    const { challengeId } = await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    expect(await planOf(sip.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'CANCEL_PENDING',
      cancelChallengeId: challengeId,
    });
    expect(await challengeOf(challengeId)).toMatchObject({
      subjectType: 'PLAN_CANCEL',
      templateKey: 'TPL_PLAN_CANCEL',
      requiredFactors: ['SMS', 'EMAIL'],
    });
    expect(t.fakeFp.calls({ class: 'M' })).toHaveLength(mWrites);

    t.clock.advance(MINUTE);
    await approveChallenge(challengeId, sip.investor);
    await cancelSubmit(lastJob('plans.cancel.submit')?.data);
    await expectNoPmWritesBeforeConsumed(t, challengeId);

    expect(await planOf(sip.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'CANCELLED',
      cancelledBy: 'INVESTOR',
      fpState: 'cancelled',
      finalAt: expect.any(Date),
      cancelReconcilingSince: null,
    });
    expect(cancelCalls()).toBe(cancels + 1);
    expect(
      t.fakeFp
        .calls()
        .slice(-2)
        .map((c) => c.op),
    ).toEqual(['purchasePlan.get', 'purchasePlan.cancel']);
    // What our request sent; FP's reply carries 'custom_reason' (BRIEF D7) and is not read.
    expect(t.fakeFp.state.purchasePlans.get(sip.fpPlanId)).toMatchObject({
      state: 'cancelled',
      cancellationCode: 'invest_later',
    });
    expect((await mandateOf(sip.mandateId))?.status).toBe('APPROVED');
  });

  it('CANCELLED writes audit_events rows (R-20) and one SIP_CANCELLED email; a re-delivered job changes nothing', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await auditFor('plans', c.planId)).toEqual(
      expect.arrayContaining(['SIP_CANCEL_REQUESTED', 'SIP_CANCEL_SUBMITTED', 'SIP_CANCELLED']),
    );
    expect(await auditFor('consent_challenges', c.challengeId)).toContain('CONSENT_APPROVED');
    expect(await notificationsFor(c.investor.investorId, 'SIP_CANCELLED')).toHaveLength(1);

    const cancels = cancelCalls();
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(cancelCalls()).toBe(cancels);
    expect(await notificationsFor(c.investor.investorId, 'SIP_CANCELLED')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect((await challengeOf(c.challengeId))?.status).toBe('CONSUMED');
  });

  it('SMS body uses SANCHAY_CONSENT_OTP_V1 with action "cancel SIP of"', async () => {
    const sip = await activeSip();
    const { challengeId } = await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    await t.app.get(ConsentEngine).sendOtp(challengeId, 'SMS');
    const sms = [...t.sms.outbox].reverse().find((m) => m.to === sip.investor.mobile);
    expect(sms?.templateId).toBe('SANCHAY_CONSENT_OTP_V1');
    expect(sms?.text).toContain('is your OTP to cancel SIP of Rs 5000.00 in ');
  });

  it('cancel needs Idempotency-Key; replay returns the same challenge', async () => {
    const sip = await activeSip();
    const missing = await httpCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    expect(missing.statusCode).toBe(428);
    expect(missing.json()).toMatchObject({ code: 'IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED' });
    expect((await planOf(sip.planId))?.status).toBe('ACTIVE');

    const key = randomUUID();
    const first = await httpCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId, key);
    const second = await httpCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId, key);
    expect(first.statusCode).toBe(200);
    expect(second.statusCode).toBe(200);
    expect(second.json()).toEqual(first.json());
    const issued = await t.db.db
      .select({ id: consentChallenges.id })
      .from(consentChallenges)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(consentChallenges.investorId, sip.investor.investorId),
          eq(consentChallenges.subjectType, 'PLAN_CANCEL'),
        ),
      );
    expect(issued).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('only ACTIVE plans can be cancelled; CANCEL_PENDING blocks a second request', async () => {
    const investor = await seedSipInvestor(t);
    const scheme = await seedSipScheme(t);
    const draft = await t.app.get(SipService).createSip({
      investorId: investor.investorId,
      schemeId: scheme.id,
      amount: '5000.00',
      installmentDay: 10,
      numberOfInstalments: null,
      rail: 'UPI_AUTOPAY', // F3; drop this line if T6 removed F3
      userIp: '203.0.113.10',
      initiatedVia: 'web',
    });
    await expect(requestCancel(investor, draft.planId)).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'PLAN_NOT_MODIFIABLE',
    });

    const sip = await activeSip();
    await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    const again = await httpCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId, randomUUID());
    expect(again.statusCode).toBe(409);
    expect(again.json()).toMatchObject({ code: 'PLAN_NOT_MODIFIABLE' });
  });

  it('BOLA on plans.cancel', async () => {
    const sip = await activeSip();
    await expectBola(t, 'plans.cancel', { id: sip.planId });
    expect((await planOf(sip.planId))?.status).toBe('ACTIVE');
  });
});

describe('plans.cancel.submit', () => {
  it('timeout -> RECONCILING (stamped with the app clock) -> re-fetch shows cancelled -> CANCELLED', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    t.fakeFp.script('purchasePlan.cancel', 'timeout');
    enqueued.length = 0;
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'RECONCILING',
      cancelReconcilingSince: t.clock.now(),
    });
    // R-32: plans.cancel.submit is exclusive, so the re-read comes back through plans.sip.advance (stately).
    expect(enqueued.map((j) => j.name)).toEqual(['plans.sip.advance']);
    expect(lastJob('plans.sip.advance')).toMatchObject({
      data: { planId: c.planId, challengeId: c.registrationChallengeId },
      opts: { startAfter: 60, singletonKey: c.planId },
    });
    enqueued.length = 0;
    await sipAdvance(c.planId, c.registrationChallengeId); // that job, 60 s later: it routes the cancel here
    const requeued = lastJob('plans.cancel.submit');
    expect(requeued).toMatchObject({
      data: { challengeId: c.challengeId, subjectIds: [c.planId] },
      opts: { singletonKey: c.challengeId },
    });

    const cancels = cancelCalls();
    await cancelSubmit(requeued?.data);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'CANCELLED',
      cancelledBy: 'INVESTOR',
      cancelReconcilingSince: null,
    });
    expect(cancelCalls()).toBe(cancels);
    expect(await auditFor('plans', c.planId)).toContain('SIP_CANCELLED');
  });

  it('ambiguous and FP still active 10 minutes after RECONCILING -> ACTIVE, not applied; plans.sip.advance routes the RECONCILING cancel here', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    t.fakeFp.script('purchasePlan.cancel', '5xx');
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'RECONCILING',
      cancelReconcilingSince: t.clock.now(),
    });
    // A scripted reply replaces the response of a call FakeFp already applied; undo it so FP "never cancelled".
    t.fakeFp.advancePlan(c.fpPlanId, 'active');

    enqueued.length = 0;
    await sipAdvance(c.planId, c.registrationChallengeId); // F7's backstop path
    const routed = lastJob('plans.cancel.submit');
    expect(routed).toMatchObject({
      data: { challengeId: c.challengeId, subjectIds: [c.planId] },
      opts: { singletonKey: c.challengeId },
    });

    await cancelSubmit(routed?.data); // inside the grace: wait
    expect((await planOf(c.planId))?.status).toBe('RECONCILING');
    t.clock.advance(10 * MINUTE);
    await cancelSubmit(routed?.data);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'ACTIVE',
      cancelledBy: null,
      cancelFailureCode: 'FP_PLAN_STILL_ACTIVE',
      cancelReconcilingSince: null,
    });
    expect(await breaksFor(c.planId)).toContain('PLAN_CANCEL_NOT_APPLIED:WARNING');
    expect(await auditFor('plans', c.planId)).toContain('SIP_CANCEL_NOT_APPLIED');

    await requestCancel(c.investor, c.planId); // the investor can try again
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'CANCEL_PENDING',
      cancelFailureCode: null,
    });
  });

  it('FP rejects the cancel and the re-read shows a plan FP no longer runs -> ACTIVE with the provider code and a WARNING break; the consent stays CONSUMED', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    // FP completes the plan between the live read and the write: the read still says active, the cancel is a 400.
    t.fakeFp.advancePlan(c.fpPlanId, 'completed');
    t.fakeFp.script('purchasePlan.get', {
      status: 200,
      body: { object: 'mf_purchase_plan', id: c.fpPlanId, state: 'active' },
    });
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'ACTIVE',
      cancelFailureCode: 'INVALID_STATE',
    });
    expect(
      t.fakeFp
        .calls()
        .slice(-3)
        .map((call) => call.op),
    ).toEqual(['purchasePlan.get', 'purchasePlan.cancel', 'purchasePlan.get']);
    expect(await breaksFor(c.planId)).toContain('PLAN_CANCEL_REJECTED:WARNING');
    expect((await challengeOf(c.challengeId))?.status).toBe('CONSUMED');
  });

  it('FP refuses because the plan is already cancelled (a second delivery got there first) -> re-read -> CANCELLED by INVESTOR, never reverted', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    // The other delivery's cancel landed after this delivery's live read, which still saw the plan active.
    t.fakeFp.advancePlan(c.fpPlanId, 'cancelled');
    t.fakeFp.script('purchasePlan.get', {
      status: 200,
      body: { object: 'mf_purchase_plan', id: c.fpPlanId, state: 'active' },
    });
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'CANCELLED',
      cancelledBy: 'INVESTOR',
      cancelFailureCode: null,
    });
    expect(await breaksFor(c.planId)).not.toContain('PLAN_CANCEL_REJECTED:WARNING');
    expect((await challengeOf(c.challengeId))?.status).toBe('CONSUMED');
    expect(await notificationsFor(c.investor.investorId, 'SIP_CANCELLED')).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('consent lapsed before the job ran -> ACTIVE, CONSUMED_UNUSED, no FP write', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    const cancels = cancelCalls();
    t.clock.advance(11 * MINUTE);
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'ACTIVE',
      cancelFailureCode: 'CONSENT_EXPIRED',
    });
    expect((await challengeOf(c.challengeId))?.status).toBe('CONSUMED_UNUSED');
    expect(await auditFor('consent_challenges', c.challengeId)).toContain('CONSENT_MARKED_UNUSED');
    expect(cancelCalls()).toBe(cancels);
  });

  it('FP already cancelled the plan -> CANCELLED by EXTERNAL, CONSUMED_UNUSED, no FP write', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    t.fakeFp.advancePlan(c.fpPlanId, 'cancelled');
    const cancels = cancelCalls();
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({ status: 'CANCELLED', cancelledBy: 'EXTERNAL' });
    expect((await challengeOf(c.challengeId))?.status).toBe('CONSUMED_UNUSED');
    expect(cancelCalls()).toBe(cancels);
    expect(await notificationsFor(c.investor.investorId, 'SIP_CANCELLED')).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});

describe('plans.cancel.sweep and instalments', () => {
  it('an abandoned challenge: the sweep returns the plan to ACTIVE; a cancelled one is reclaimed by the next request', async () => {
    const sip = await activeSip();
    const first = await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    t.clock.advance(11 * MINUTE); // PENDING past expires_at: it can never be approved
    await sweep();
    expect(await planOf(sip.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'ACTIVE',
      cancelFailureCode: 'CONSENT_NOT_GIVEN',
    });
    expect(await auditFor('plans', sip.planId)).toContain('SIP_CANCEL_NOT_APPLIED');

    const second = await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    expect(second.challengeId).not.toBe(first.challengeId);
    await t.app.get(ConsentEngine).cancel(t.db.db, second.challengeId);
    const third = await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId);
    expect(await planOf(sip.planId)).toMatchObject({
      status: 'CANCEL_PENDING',
      cancelChallengeId: third.challengeId,
      cancelFailureCode: null,
    });
  });

  it("a CONSUMED cancel whose job was lost is re-enqueued under approve's key once approve's job has had 5 minutes", async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel(); // the spy swallowed approve's job
    enqueued.length = 0;
    await sweep();
    expect(cancelJobsFor(c.challengeId)).toEqual([]); // approve's own job may still be running
    t.clock.advance(5 * MINUTE);
    await sweep();
    expect(cancelJobsFor(c.challengeId)).toEqual([
      {
        name: 'plans.cancel.submit',
        data: { challengeId: c.challengeId, subjectIds: [c.planId] },
        opts: { singletonKey: c.challengeId },
      },
    ]);
    expect((await planOf(c.planId))?.status).toBe('CANCEL_PENDING');
    await cancelSubmit(cancelJobsFor(c.challengeId)[0]?.data); // still inside execute_before
    expect(await planOf(c.planId)).toMatchObject({ status: 'CANCELLED', cancelledBy: 'INVESTOR' });
  });

  it('an instalment FP raised before the cancel is still mirrored after CANCELLED', async () => {
    const c = await approvedCancel();
    const fpPurchaseId = t.fakeFp.addInstalment(c.fpPlanId, 'submitted');
    await cancelSubmit(c.jobData);
    expect((await planOf(c.planId))?.status).toBe('CANCELLED');
    await t.app.get(InstalmentsSyncJob).handle(jobOf('plans.instalments.sync', {}));
    const rows = await t.db.db.select().from(orders).where(eq(orders.planId, c.planId));
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rows[0]).toMatchObject({
      origin: 'SIP_INSTALMENT',
      status: 'PROCESSING',
      fpOrderId: fpPurchaseId,
    });
  });
});

describe('guards', () => {
  it('trg_plan_cancel_guard refuses an INVESTOR cancel without a CONSUMED PLAN_CANCEL consent; cancelled_by needs CANCELLED', async () => {
    const sip = await activeSip();
    const investorCancel = `UPDATE app.plans SET status = 'CANCELLED', cancelled_by = 'INVESTOR' WHERE id = $1`;
    // The plan's own CONSUMED SIP registration consent does not count.
    await expect(t.db.pool.query(investorCancel, [sip.planId])).rejects.toThrow(
      /trg_plan_cancel_guard/,
    );
    await requestCancel(sip.investor, sip.planId); // a PENDING cancel consent does not count either
    await expect(t.db.pool.query(investorCancel, [sip.planId])).rejects.toThrow(
      /trg_plan_cancel_guard/,
    );

    const err = await t.db.db
      .update(plans)
      .set({ cancelledBy: 'INVESTOR' })
      .where(eq(plans.id, sip.planId))
      .catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect(pgConstraintOf(err)).toBe('plans_cancelled_by_status_ck');
  });
});
```

`packages/features/src/sip/CancelSipSheet.test.tsx` (the consents routes answer with E4's wire shapes, as F16's fixtures do; RV-03-9's facade adapts them for `ConsentOtpSheet`):
```tsx
import { screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { HttpResponse, http } from 'msw';
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { renderWithProviders, TEST_API } from '../test-utils';
import { CancelSipSheet } from './CancelSipSheet';

const PLAN_ID = '0190c0de-0000-7000-8000-000000000010';
const CHALLENGE_ID = '0190c0de-0000-7000-8000-0000000000f1';
/** newIdempotencyKey() is a UUIDv7. */
const KEY = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-7[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** E4's wire shapes, as F16's fixtures use them (RV-03-9's facade adapts them for ConsentOtpSheet). */
const PLAN_CANCEL_CHALLENGE = {
  challengeId: CHALLENGE_ID,
  status: 'PENDING',
  requiredFactors: ['SMS', 'EMAIL'],
  expiresAt: '2026-11-18T05:10:00.000Z',
};
const CANCEL_REQUESTED = { challengeId: CHALLENGE_ID, expiresAt: '2026-11-18T05:10:00.000Z' };

const refusal = (code: string, status: number) =>
  HttpResponse.json(
    {
      defined: true,
      code,
      status,
      message: code,
      data: { retryable: false, requestId: '0190c0de-0000-7000-8000-0000000000f2' },
    },
    { status },
  );

const server = setupServer();
beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }));
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());

/** Answers plans.cancel with `replies` in order (the last one repeats) and records each Idempotency-Key. */
function cancelRoute(replies: ReadonlyArray<() => Response>): Array<string | null> {
  const keys: Array<string | null> = [];
  server.use(
    http.post(`${TEST_API}/plans/${PLAN_ID}/cancel`, ({ request }) => {
      keys.push(request.headers.get('idempotency-key'));
      const reply = replies[Math.min(keys.length, replies.length) - 1];
      if (reply === undefined) throw new Error('cancelRoute needs at least one reply');
      return reply();
    }),
    http.get(`${TEST_API}/consents/challenges/${CHALLENGE_ID}`, () =>
      HttpResponse.json(PLAN_CANCEL_CHALLENGE),
    ),
    http.post(`${TEST_API}/consents/challenges/${CHALLENGE_ID}/otp`, () =>
      HttpResponse.json({ ok: true }),
    ),
  );
  return keys;
}

function renderSheet() {
  const onDone = vi.fn();
  const onClose = vi.fn();
  renderWithProviders(
    <CancelSipSheet
      planId={PLAN_ID}
      schemeName="Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund"
      amount="5000.00"
      onDone={onDone}
      onClose={onClose}
    />,
  );
  return { onDone, onClose };
}

describe('CancelSipSheet (SIPM-02, R-08)', () => {
  it('confirms first, then asks for both codes; the cancel carries an Idempotency-Key', async () => {
    const keys = cancelRoute([() => HttpResponse.json(CANCEL_REQUESTED)]);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderSheet();
    expect(
      screen.getByText(/^Your monthly SIP of ₹5,000\.00 in Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund stops\./),
    ).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByText(/stays active for future SIPs/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(keys).toEqual([]);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel SIP' }));
    expect(await screen.findByLabelText('SMS code')).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Email code')).toBeTruthy();
    expect(keys).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(keys[0]).toMatch(KEY);
  });

  it('retries a network failure with the same key', async () => {
    const keys = cancelRoute([
      () => HttpResponse.error(),
      () => HttpResponse.json(CANCEL_REQUESTED),
    ]);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderSheet();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel SIP' }));
    expect(
      await screen.findByText('You seem to be offline. Check your connection and try again.'),
    ).toBeTruthy();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel SIP' }));
    expect(await screen.findByLabelText('SMS code')).toBeTruthy();
    expect(keys).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(keys[0]).toMatch(KEY);
    expect(keys[1]).toBe(keys[0]);
  });

  it('shows the safe copy when the SIP can no longer be cancelled; the next tap is a new intent', async () => {
    const keys = cancelRoute([() => refusal('PLAN_NOT_MODIFIABLE', 409)]);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { onClose } = renderSheet();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel SIP' }));
    expect(await screen.findByText('This SIP cannot be changed right now.')).toBeTruthy();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel SIP' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(keys).toHaveLength(2));
    expect(keys[1]).toMatch(KEY);
    expect(keys[1]).not.toBe(keys[0]);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Keep SIP' }));
    expect(onClose).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });
});
```

`apps/api/src/modules/plans/plan-cancel.ts`:
```ts
import type { ChallengeStatus } from '@sanchay/domain';
import { MINUTE } from '../platform/clock.js';

/** The consent SMS action (SANCHAY_CONSENT_OTP_V1: "{code} is your OTP to cancel SIP of Rs {amount} in …"). */
export const PLAN_CANCEL_ACTION = 'cancel SIP of';

/**
 * The FP cancellation code sent with every investor cancel (research fp-api §4). Sandbox run 1 (P-09,
 * BRIEF D7) stored `custom_reason` whatever was sent, so nothing reads the code back from FP.
 */
export const PLAN_CANCELLATION_CODE = 'invest_later';

/** How long after a cancel entered RECONCILING FP may still report the plan active before it is adopted as not applied. */
export const CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS = 10 * MINUTE;

/** Seconds between re-reads of an ambiguous cancel. */
export const CANCEL_RECONCILE_POLL_SECONDS = 60;

/**
 * How long after approve the sweep leaves a CONSUMED cancel to approve's own plans.cancel.submit (approve
 * enqueues it in its own transaction; a sweep enqueue before then could only run beside it). The sweep
 * runs every 5 minutes, so a lost job is re-enqueued 5 to 10 minutes after approve: still inside
 * execute_before (approve + 10 minutes) for a saga that never started.
 */
export const CANCEL_SUBMIT_LOST_AFTER_MS = 5 * MINUTE;

const DEAD_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<ChallengeStatus> = new Set<ChallengeStatus>([
  'EXPIRED',
  'CANCELLED',
  'SUPERSEDED',
  'CONSUMED_UNUSED',
]);

/**
 * A cancel challenge that can never lead to an FP write: expired, cancelled, superseded, swept unused,
 * or still PENDING past `expires_at` (E4's approve refuses it from then on). Its CANCEL_PENDING plan goes
 * back to ACTIVE.
 */
export function isDeadCancelChallenge(
  challenge: { status: ChallengeStatus; expiresAt: Date },
  now: Date,
): boolean {
  if (DEAD_STATUSES.has(challenge.status)) return true;
  return challenge.status === 'PENDING' && challenge.expiresAt.getTime() <= now.getTime();
}

export type CancelSweepStep = 'REVERT' | 'REQUEUE' | 'LEAVE';

/**
 * plans.cancel.sweep's decision for a CANCEL_PENDING plan's challenge: a dead one returns the plan to
 * ACTIVE; a CONSUMED one gets plans.cancel.submit re-enqueued once approve's own job has had
 * CANCEL_SUBMIT_LOST_AFTER_MS to run (a lost job must not strand the plan); anything else is left alone.
 */
export function cancelSweepStep(
  challenge: { status: ChallengeStatus; expiresAt: Date; consumedAt: Date | null },
  now: Date,
): CancelSweepStep {
  if (isDeadCancelChallenge(challenge, now)) return 'REVERT';
  if (challenge.status !== 'CONSUMED') return 'LEAVE';
  if (challenge.consumedAt === null) return 'REQUEUE';
  const sinceApproval = now.getTime() - challenge.consumedAt.getTime();
  return sinceApproval >= CANCEL_SUBMIT_LOST_AFTER_MS ? 'REQUEUE' : 'LEAVE';
}

export type PreCancelCheck = 'SEND' | 'ALREADY_CANCELLED' | 'NOT_CANCELLABLE';

/** The live read inside useConsumed, before the one M write: FP cancels only `created` or `active` plans. */
export function preCancelCheck(fpState: string): PreCancelCheck {
  if (fpState === 'active' || fpState === 'created') return 'SEND';
  if (fpState === 'cancelled') return 'ALREADY_CANCELLED';
  return 'NOT_CANCELLABLE';
}

export type CancelReconcileStep = 'CANCELLED' | 'ACTIVE' | 'WAIT' | 'UNRESOLVED';

/**
 * LOOKUP-ADOPT for an ambiguous cancel (the FP plan id is known, so a re-read is enough):
 * `cancelled` -> CANCELLED; still `active`/`created` -> WAIT, then ACTIVE (not applied) once the grace has
 * passed since `reconcilingSince` (plans.cancel_reconciling_since, app clock); anything else
 * (`completed`, `failed`, …) -> UNRESOLVED, a CRITICAL break for ops.
 */
export function cancelReconcileStep(input: {
  fpState: string;
  reconcilingSince: Date | null;
  now: Date;
}): CancelReconcileStep {
  if (input.fpState === 'cancelled') return 'CANCELLED';
  if (input.fpState === 'active' || input.fpState === 'created') {
    const since = input.reconcilingSince ?? input.now;
    return input.now.getTime() - since.getTime() >= CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS ? 'ACTIVE' : 'WAIT';
  }
  return 'UNRESOLVED';
}
```

`apps/api/drizzle/0035_plans_cancel_guard.sql` (custom, after the generated `0034_plans_cancel`). F2's `trg_consent_guard` cannot be reused: the plan's own CONSUMED registration consent would satisfy it.
```sql
CREATE FUNCTION "app"."trg_plan_cancel_guard"() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.cancelled_by = 'INVESTOR' AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM app.consent_challenges cc
    JOIN app.consent_subjects cs ON cs.challenge_id = cc.id
    WHERE cc.id = NEW.cancel_challenge_id
      AND cc.subject_type = 'PLAN_CANCEL'
      AND cc.status = 'CONSUMED'
      AND cs.subject_table = 'plans'
      AND cs.subject_id = NEW.id
      AND cs.status = 'CONSENTED'
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'trg_plan_cancel_guard: plan % needs a CONSUMED PLAN_CANCEL consent to be cancelled by the investor', NEW.id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

CREATE TRIGGER "trg_plans_cancel_guard"
  BEFORE UPDATE OF status, cancelled_by ON "app"."plans"
  FOR EACH ROW
  WHEN (NEW.status = 'CANCELLED' AND (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status OR OLD.cancelled_by IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.cancelled_by))
  EXECUTE FUNCTION "app"."trg_plan_cancel_guard"();
```
